chapters.title: Chapter 215: Riding An Ant
paragraphs: "Even better than what I thought." Lian muttered to himself.
Maybe they really could reach the tribe within a few hours!
Sometimes One would jump over a rotten trunk, and upon landing, its entire body would drop for a moment, but its six legs would distribute the impact among themselves.
Ravian constantly pointed out the direction.
"Right side. After that root, take the path upward."
Lian transmitted the command.
One obeyed without pausing.
After a while, they reached a massive root whose surface was spread out like a complete floor.
A long crack ran through the middle of the root, and clear water was flowing in it.
For them, the crack looked more like a narrow river than a split in the wood.
The water flowed down the slope at high speed and had formed deep pools in some places.
Fish-like creatures were moving in the water.
Their bodies looked small, but each was almost the size of a dog. They had transparent fins and their round mouths were full of tiny teeth.
Lian glanced at them briefly. These were the largest fish he had ever seen with his own eyes.
The problem was that these were literally not monsters, just normal fish, and yet they had such massive size.
This made him curious whether the gigantism of everything in this forest was natural, or the result of some kind of mutation or external intervention.
At first glance it seemed foolish, but the natural and logical explanation was that there must be a reason behind everything, just like this forest.
There had to be some reason why everything was gigantic.
"Go from that edge. The middle is deep." Ravian pointed to a narrow section beside the river.
One changed its path.
Its left legs landed on the dry part of the root, and its right legs dipped into the water several times.
The fish-like creatures immediately moved toward the movement. One of them jumped out of the water and snapped its jaw at One’s leg.
The Heavy Carapace shell prevented the teeth from penetrating.
One shook its leg.
The creature fell back into the water, and the current carried it away.
Nemi looked down at the river from above.
"Even the fish here want to eat you, is there anything in this forest that doesn’t?" Lian said.
In this forest, practically all living things were omnivorous. The food chain and the structure of the forest creatures made him wonder how the creatures of this forest had not gone extinct yet?
In any ecosystem, there had to be some kind of balance, but here all he saw were predators, predators that hunted weaker predators.
No one answered, because they had no answer to give.
For them, this situation was completely normal, after all, they had grown up here.
A few kilometers ahead, One suddenly stopped, its six legs locked on the ground at the same time.
Hive Link sent a faint warning to Lian’s mind.
A heavy and approaching vibration.
"Don’t move." Lian immediately raised his hand.
Ravian looked at the ground. A few seconds later, he himself felt the vibration too.
From a distance, the sound of breaking branches and heavy footsteps was heard.
One changed its path toward a large piece of bark that had separated from the tree trunk.
The bark was curved like a roof over the ground, and the space beneath it seemed enough for the ant to hide.
Everyone stayed low.
One pulled itself under the bark and pressed its body to the ground.
A few moments later, the massive creature appeared. Only its legs were visible from under the bark’s gap.
It had green and gray skin, and curved claws protruded from the tips of each toe.
The identification panel appeared for a moment.
[Stonehide Root Strider]
[Level: 31]
Every step shook the ground. One of its feet landed only a few meters away, and the impact made the bark above them tremble and soil fall from the ceiling onto them.
Nemi held her breath. Sera placed her hand on her shoulder.
Even One, with its elephant-sized body, was nothing more than an insect next to that creature.
The Stonehide Root Strider passed by without noticing them.
Its heavy tail dragged over the moss and uprooted a massive bush, and the sound of its footsteps slowly faded away.
Lian waited a few moments, then through Hive Link made sure the vibrations had weakened.
He gave the command to move.
One came out from under the bark and the journey continued.
About an hour later, a shadow suddenly passed over their heads.
One reacted before anyone else.
Vibration Detection this time was not from the ground, but the change in air pressure and the faint trembling of the leaves had given the warning.
A massive dragonfly was descending through the mist.
Its body was over ten meters long, and its four transparent wings moved at such speed that they created a roaring sound.
Its multi-segmented eyes fixed on One. Compared to the aerial predator, the ant seemed like suitable prey.
Lian immediately spotted the path of a large leaf that was bent on the ground and sent a quick command.
Take cover.
One Dashed toward the leaf without delay. Its legs pounded on the soil, and its massive body slid under the leaf’s shadow.
At that same moment, the dragonfly passed over their heads. The wind from its wings violently shook the leaf.
Nemi almost separated from One’s back, but Sera grabbed the rope around her waist.
The dragonfly circled in the sky once and hovered above the leaf for a few moments.
But One remained still. Lian kept its presence calm through Hive Link. Finally, the aerial predator lost interest and disappeared into the columns of mist.
"On foot, we couldn’t have escaped from that." Ravian let out his breath.
He looked at One with gratitude, the monster that he had been afraid of, he now understood what a great blessing it was.
He was even slowly coming to the conclusion that he wished their tribe could also tame such monsters.
At that time, their tribe could become the strongest among all the forest tribes! But unfortunately, such a thing was only a dream, and they did not have such an ability...

Its multi-segmented eyes fixed on One.
Compared to the aerial predator, the ant seemed like suitable prey.
Lian immediately spotted the path of a large leaf that was bent on the ground and sent a quick command.
Take cover.
One Dashed toward the leaf without delay.
Its legs pounded on the soil, and its massive body slid under the leaf’s shadow.
At that same moment, the dragonfly passed over their heads.
The wind from its wings violently shook the leaf.
Nemi almost separated from One’s back, but Sera grabbed the rope around her waist.
The dragonfly circled in the sky once and hovered above the leaf for a few moments.
But One remained still.
Lian kept its presence calm through Hive Link.
Finally, the aerial predator lost interest and disappeared into the columns of mist.
"On foot, we couldn’t have escaped from that." Ravian let out his breath.
He looked at One with gratitude, the monster that he had been afraid of, he now understood what a great blessing it was.
He was even slowly coming to the conclusion that he wished their tribe could also tame such monsters.
At that time, their tribe could become the strongest among all the forest tribes!
But unfortunately, such a thing was only a dream, and they did not have such an ability...

chapters.title: Chapter 216: The Tribe Of Lacerians I
paragraphs: Lian agreed
Fighting against monsters that could fly was a hellish torment. Victory against them was extremely difficult.
Unless the awakened one also had the ability to fly or the ability to perform long-range attacks. Otherwise, against such monsters, the best decision was to hide.
"Not a bad choice." Then he gave a short tap on One’s shell.
The ant’s antennae moved with satisfaction for a moment.
A little later, the path split between two large roots. The left path was wider and straighter, and the right path was narrower and full of slopes.
"Both eventually reach the Blue Stone area. The left path is faster, but I don’t know if it’s safe now." Ravian said.
Lian stopped One, closed his eyes, and decided to share one of his senses with the monster.
This time, he only chose the sense of vibration.
The visual world faded for him. Instead, the ground turned into a network of waves.
The vibration of One’s legs was close and clear. The movement of small insects felt like very weak impacts.
On the left path, something large and heavy was moving at a distance.
Not one, but several creatures. The rhythm of the steps was irregular and sometimes stopped. Perhaps a herd of monsters or predators fighting.
The right path only had small and scattered vibrations.
"Right." Lian cut the connection.
"Did you sense something?"
"The left side is busy."
Ravian, without further questions, pointed to the right path, and One entered the narrow route.
The ability to climb roots showed its true value in this section. The ant climbed a surface that for four people was almost a vertical wall.
The claws on its legs sank into the cracks in the bark and pulled its body up.
If those four wanted to take this path themselves, it could take them hours, and Lian doubted that except for him, it would even be possible for the other three.
He himself could climb by sinking his claws into the wall, but the three of them didn’t have that ability, and he would have to carry them up.
When they reached the top of the root, the view of the Forest of Giants opened up widely before them for the first time.
From that height, the forest floor looked like another world.
Giant trees rose in all directions, their trunks lost in layers of mist.
Massive leaves at different heights were like green islands.
Water fell from the edge of some leaves, creating narrow but hundreds-of-meters-high waterfalls.
Luminous plants in the dark parts of the lower forest glowed in blue, purple, and green.
Massive creatures moved on distant branches. One looked like a snake, but its body was so long that it had wrapped several times around a branch as thick as a tower.
Birds larger than buildings flew through the mist, and every time they opened their wings, the surrounding clouds parted.
Nemi forgot her fear for a while and looked at the view with a half-open mouth.
"I’ve never seen the forest from this high up."
Sera also fixed her gaze on the distance, and the tiredness and pain left her face for a moment.
Such a beautiful view made them completely forget all the hardships they had endured and made them realize even more how small and insignificant they were in front of this forest.
Ravian, instead of admiring the beauty, was more focused on the path’s signs.
His eyes fixed on a mass of blue mushrooms in the distance.
Then he saw a trunk with three vertical cracks on it. His expression changed, and joy and excitement could be seen.
"We’re close."
"Are you sure?" Nemi immediately leaned forward, feeling like she had just heard the best news of her life.
Ravian pointed to the southeast.
"Those mushrooms grow near the tribe’s hunting ground. If we follow the right path, not much is left."
Excitement was clear in his voice. They were finally getting close!
After all this hardship, after all those near-death experiences, they were finally approaching their home!
Nothing could describe their happiness at this moment.
One climbed down from the root, and the journey continued.
The further they went, the more natural signs gave way to traces of intelligent creatures.
Regular cuts could be seen on some roots.
Not claw marks from monsters, but directional signs probably made to guide the tribe’s hunters.
Ropes were stretched between the lower roots, and some mushrooms had carved marks on their caps.
Small traps for catching insects were placed along the path.
One of them was made of thick webs and thin bones, and inside it, an insect the size of a rabbit was trapped.
In the distance, a thin column of smoke rose among the roots.
Then a faint sound was heard.
A drumbeat, and a few seconds later, another beat.
Ravian suddenly sat up straight, his eyes shining.
"We’re here."
Lian also looked into the distance. He too could see from the signs that they were finally approaching a civilization.
Sera looked through the trees. The remaining tension on her face slowly faded.
One passed between two giant roots.
And the tribe appeared before them. Houses carved into the massive root walls.
Round and rectangular openings could be seen at different heights, and narrow wooden bridges were stretched between them.
Watchtowers were built on dried mushroom stems, and guards from above watched the entire surroundings.
Green and blue lights shone inside transparent bubbles, lighting up the dark part of the forest.
A wall of giant thorns, carved wood, and monster shells was built around the entrance.
Behind the wall, hundreds of Lacerians were moving on different paths.
Some carried baskets of fruit and roots, some wore armor, children ran on the lower bridges.
But as soon as One emerged from among the roots, everything changed.
One of the guards on the tower saw the ant, his eyes widened, and he struck a large bell.
The alarm sound echoed throughout the tribe. Other guards immediately appeared. Bows were drawn, and spears were lowered from above the wall.
A few mana lights lit up at the tips of the weapons. People inside the tribe started retreating, and mothers pulled children inside the houses.
One stopped in front of the gate, and its massive jaws moved for a moment.
All the weapons were fixed on its head.
Just from that first look, it was clear that the entire tribe considered that ant as a monster attack and were ready for battle.
How quickly they reacted and prepared for battle was also amazing.
Ravian stood on the ant’s back, balancing himself by holding the rope, and shouted with all his might.
"Don’t shoot! It’s us!"
His voice echoed among the roots. For a moment, no one moved. One of the guards came forward from above the tower.
His eyes fixed on Ravian, then on Sera, and then on Nemi. Suddenly, the color drained from his face.
"Ravian...?"
His voice was full of disbelief. A murmur spread among the guards and people behind the wall.
The names of the three siblings passed from mouth to mouth. Apparently, they had been presumed dead for a long time.
Now they had not only returned alive, but were riding on the back of one of the most dangerous insects of the Forest of Giants.
The gate began to open with the heavy sound of chains.
Lian looked down from One’s back at the hundreds of shocked faces.
The gazes were not only on Ravian and his sisters. Most of them were fixed on him.
An unknown creature.
A stranger who had returned with the tribe’s lost members and had a massive Crimson Needle Ant under his control like an obedient animal.
After three days of running, blood, and battle, they had finally reached the tribe; but the gazes fixed on Lian told him that his arrival here was not the end of his problems.

chapters.title: Chapter 217: The Tribe Of Lacerians II
paragraphs: The tribe’s gate opened with the heavy sound of chains being pulled.
Its two massive leaves, made of compressed wood, monster bones, and layers of insect shells, slowly moved apart.
The guards on the wall still kept their bows ready, and green mana light shone on the tips of several spears.
One took its first step inside the tribe’s territory.
Its six massive legs landed on the wooden path one after another, and with each step, a dry and heavy sound echoed among the roots.
Lian looked around from the ant’s back.
Up close, the tribe was much larger and more complex than it appeared from outside.
The houses were carved into the giant roots.
Some entrances were at ground level, but many of the houses were built several meters higher, and thin rope bridges connected them to each other.
Wooden platforms stuck out from the root walls at different heights.
Thick ropes moved baskets and loads between the upper and lower levels.
Lamps made from the sap of luminous plants hung inside transparent containers.
Their green and blue light fell on the Lacerians’ scales and created trembling shadows on the root walls.
On one side, a few hunters were separating the skin and shell of a beetle-like monster.
Two craftsmen were striking a sheet of black shell with stone hammers, shaping it into a curved shield.
Men and women carried baskets full of edible roots, mushrooms, and small fruits.
A few children were peeking from behind a platform.
In another section, six-legged, lizard-like animals were tied next to stables made of roots and wood.
Leather armor was placed on their sides, and their short horns were marked with the tribe’s colors.
Everything was alive.
Busy and orderly, but as soon as One entered, all this life froze for a moment.
The sound of hammers stopped, baskets were lowered, and children hid.
The guards jumped down from the platforms.
At first, the gazes were on the massive ant.
Then on Ravian, Sera, and Nemi, and finally, they fixed on Lian.
His appearance was far too different among the hundreds of Lacerians.
He had no tail, no antennae, no scales, smooth skin, tall stature, and eyes that looked nothing like theirs.
Even his clothes were made of a material that most of the tribe’s people had never seen.
A murmur spread through the crowd.
"What is that?"
"What kind of creature is it? It looks like us but very different?"
"Where did it come from?"
"Why is it with that ant?"
A group of warriors blocked the way.
The guards’ commander was a broad-shouldered man with gray scales and a deep scar next to his jaw.
He aimed his long spear directly at One.
"Ravian, step away from that creature."
His gaze then fixed on Lian.
"And that stranger get down from behind the ant too."
Ravian jumped down from One without delay, but instead of stepping away, he stood directly in front of Lian.
He did not have his spear in his hand, but his body posture was completely defensive.
"Lower your weapons."
"You don’t know what you’ve brought into the tribe." The guards’ commander frowned.
Ravian stepped forward, the exhaustion of the journey was still visible on his face, but his tone had no doubt.
"I know exactly what I’ve brought into the tribe." His voice grew louder.
"If it wasn’t for him, neither I, nor Sera, nor Nemi would be here."
Sera also climbed down from behind One and stood next to her brother, her wounded shoulder was still bandaged, but her gaze was firm.
"This person saved our lives more than once."
Nemi hesitated for a few moments, her gaze moving from the ready spears to the angry faces, and then she came out from behind the two of them.
"He is not an enemy." Her voice was not loud, but in the silence that had formed, everyone heard it.
A few guards looked at each other, this support was unexpected for them.
Ravian did not trust anyone easily.
Sera was usually too cautious to defend a stranger.
And Nemi, the youngest and most fearful of the three, was now standing in front of the tribe with dozens of weapons aimed at her, defending Lian.
This was enough to show that this person might really be trustworthy.
But they still could not trust an outsider.
Lian said nothing, through Hive Link he commanded One.
Sit down.
The ant immediately bent its six legs and brought its massive body close to the ground.
Its antennae folded, its jaws remained closed.
One’s sudden movement made a few spears come forward, but when no attack occurred, the tension decreased slightly.
However, the weapons were still not lowered.
Before the guards’ commander could say anything else, a firm but quiet voice was heard from the crowd.
"Lower your weapons." The voice was not loud, but that one sentence was enough.
The crowd parted, and a man came forward through the opened path.
He was taller than most Lacerians, and his sturdy body was hidden under a robe made of dark monster skin.
The scales on his face and neck were a mix of dark green and gray.
Two longer and thicker antennae than the others came out from the sides of his head.
Several old scars could be seen on his face and arms.
A necklace made of teeth and pieces of monster horns rested on his chest, but he wore no crown or other sign of luxury.
His authority came from something deeper than clothes, from the silence, from his gaze, and from the way all the warriors lowered their weapons without protest.
Averian, the leader of the Lacerians, stepped forward.
At first, his face was formal, but when his gaze fixed on Ravian, Sera, and Nemi, that calmness crumbled for a moment.
He moved faster, going straight to Nemi.
The younger girl had not said anything yet when Averian pulled her into his arms.
So tightly that Nemi’s breath caught for a moment.
Then he pulled Sera close with his other arm.
Ravian stood a step back, but Averian reached out his hand and pulled him into the family embrace too.
For a few moments, no one spoke.
Averian only took a deep breath, as if he still was not sure this image was real.
Nemi pressed her face to her father’s chest.
Sera closed her eyes.
Ravian looked down and clenched his jaw.
The tribe leader finally pulled back a little and examined all three from head to toe.
"What happened?" His voice was quiet, but heavy worry was in it.
"Where were you? Do you know how worried I was?" Then his gaze fixed on One and then on Lian.
"And who are this creature... and this stranger?"
"He is the legendary Otherworldly." Ravian stood up straight.
The murmurs suddenly turned into a wave of sound.
A few people stepped back, mothers who had their children close pulled them behind themselves.
"Impossible." One of the tribe’s elders whispered under his breath.
"Otherworldlies are only in old stories." An older man with shorter antennae added.
"He pulled us out of the Sky Giant Bird’s nest." Ravian raised his voice and pointed at Lian.
"He led us through the Forest of Giants. He defeated and killed thousands of Crimson Needle Ants."
For a few seconds, even the murmurs fell silent.
The claim was too big, so big that believing it seemed harder than rejecting it.
Averian said nothing, he only looked at Lian.
His gaze was calm, but precise.
Then at his children’s closed wounds.
At One, which remained motionless on the ground.
At Nemi, who unconsciously stood close to Lian.
Finally, he said.
"Come inside." He turned his gaze to the crowd.
"This is not the place to talk about such things."
Before moving, Lian commanded One.
Stay here, do not attack anyone.
He thought for a moment and then made the command more precise, even if they come close to you, just step back. Do not fight without my order.
One moved its antennae briefly, a few guards still remained around it.
From their looks, it was clear that the presence of a massive Crimson Needle Ant in the center of the tribe was like bringing a predator among families.
Lian followed Averian and his three children into the central part of the tribe.
The leader’s house was built inside the hollow part of one of the giant roots.
Its entrance was larger than the surrounding houses, but no sign of luxury could be seen in it.
The interior space was warm and bright, a few crystals were placed in the grooves of the walls, creating a soft green light.
The table and chairs were made of dark wood, maps on dried skins were hung on the walls.
An old spear and a short sword were placed next to each other.
Clay pots, pieces of bone, and a few carved stones could be seen on the shelves.
Averian asked everyone to sit and placed himself on the other side of the table.
For a few moments, he only looked at his children, and then he turned to Ravian.
"Tell it from the beginning."
Ravian took a deep breath and began the story from a few days ago.
About the decrease in hunting around the tribe, about the lack of water, about their decision to go to an area farther than the usual borders.
He explained that they, along with a small group of young hunters, had left the known paths.
First, they followed the trail of a large prey, then they got caught in mist in an area, and unfortunately, before they even realized what had happened, the bird had caught them.
Unfortunately, they had no news of the others who were with them.
"We thought we were still in the tribe’s area, but it turned out we had entered that monster’s territory." Ravian lowered his gaze.
"I told you so many times not to leave the tribe without an elder! What if you had been killed?" Averian added with the anger of a father.
And his three children just lowered their heads... they had no excuse.

"He pulled us out of the Sky Giant Bird’s nest." Ravian raised his voice and pointed at Lian.
"He led us through the Forest of Giants.
He defeated and killed thousands of Crimson Needle Ants."
For a few seconds, even the murmurs fell silent.
The claim was too big, so big that believing it seemed harder than rejecting it.
Averian said nothing, he only looked at Lian.
His gaze was calm, but precise.
Then at his children’s closed wounds.
At One, which remained motionless on the ground.
At Nemi, who unconsciously stood close to Lian.
Finally, he said.
"Come inside." He turned his gaze to the crowd.
"This is not the place to talk about such things."
Before moving, Lian commanded One.
Stay here, do not attack anyone.
He thought for a moment and then made the command more precise, even if they come close to you, just step back.
Do not fight without my order.
One moved its antennae briefly, a few guards still remained around it.
From their looks, it was clear that the presence of a massive Crimson Needle Ant in the center of the tribe was like bringing a predator among families.
Lian followed Averian and his three children into the central part of the tribe.
The leader’s house was built inside the hollow part of one of the giant roots.
Its entrance was larger than the surrounding houses, but no sign of luxury could be seen in it.
The interior space was warm and bright, a few crystals were placed in the grooves of the walls, creating a soft green light.
The table and chairs were made of dark wood, maps on dried skins were hung on the walls.
An old spear and a short sword were placed next to each other.
Clay pots, pieces of bone, and a few carved stones could be seen on the shelves.
Averian asked everyone to sit and placed himself on the other side of the table.
For a few moments, he only looked at his children, and then he turned to Ravian.
"Tell it from the beginning."
Ravian took a deep breath and began the story from a few days ago.
About the decrease in hunting around the tribe, about the lack of water, about their decision to go to an area farther than the usual borders.
He explained that they, along with a small group of young hunters, had left the known paths.
First, they followed the trail of a large prey, then they got caught in mist in an area, and unfortunately, before they even realized what had happened, the bird had caught them.
Unfortunately, they had no news of the others who were with them.
"We thought we were still in the tribe’s area, but it turned out we had entered that monster’s territory." Ravian lowered his gaze.
"I told you so many times not to leave the tribe without an elder!
What if you had been killed?" Averian added with the anger of a father.
And his three children just lowered their heads... they had no excuse.

chapters.title: Chapter 218: The Tribe Of Lacerians III
paragraphs: "We are sorry." In the end, all three of them could only apologize.
They knew that their father was only worried about them.
They knew that whatever their father said was for their own good and safety.
Maybe they had not realized this before, but after experiencing all those hardships and near-death experiences, their minds had become more mature than before.
"Continue." The tribe leader sighed.
Then Ravian continued telling the events that had happened, from when they found Lian, or more precisely, when he came to them.
Then he talked about their escape from the nest, the experience of free falling and passing through the massive branches.
Hiding from the larger creatures, and when they reached the Crimson Needle Ants, Averian’s expression changed.
"A whole colony?"
"At first we thought they were after us." Ravian nodded.
"But they were moving their nest. We didn’t exactly understand what was going on, but it seemed like it was related to their Queen."
Averian sharpened his gaze.
Ravian told the story of the carnivorous mushrooms, crossing the gap, Lian’s battle with the wave of ants, and finally, the parasite emerging from the immature Queen.
"It controlled the entire colony." Sera said quietly.
"Even Lian himself wanted us to retreat at first. The situation was very bad. But they didn’t let us escape."
"He almost died because of us." Nemi added with a low voice.
Averian kept his gaze on her, and Nemi did not continue.
Ravian explained about the Brood Carapace.
The armor made from thousands of ants, about the threads that could control the body.
About the moment Lian went inside the armor, about the time when the Parasite Thread almost reached his heart.
Averian looked at Lian several times during the story, each time slightly differently.
At first with doubt, then with caution, and finally, with disbelief.
"He crushed its core with his bare hands." Ravian said.
A heavy silence formed in the house for a few moments.
The tribe leader had locked his fingers together on the table.
His gaze fixed on Lian.
As if he was trying to understand whether the creature sitting in front of him was really the one who had defeated thousands of ants and a Calamity Seed.
The story was too big, but the testimony of all three of his children was consistent.
None of them had contradictions in the details.
And more importantly, Nemi was sitting next to Lian without the slightest fear.
Averian knew his younger child better than anyone.
She would not get close to strangers, especially after such a terrifying experience, but he could see the hidden warmth and attachment of his youngest daughter toward this strange creature.
And this itself was a great proof that everything he had heard was true.
Averian slowly stood up, stopped in front of Lian, and placed his hand on his chest.
A brief movement, but clearly important.
"You returned something to me that I thought I had lost forever." His voice was calm.
"Whatever is within my power and the Lacerians’ power, we will do to repay you."
"I only want information." Lian answered without exaggeration or false humility.
He did not try to act modest.
After all that effort, he really did not have the patience to act modest.
"About what?"
"The other two forests, Emberroot Forest and Glassthorn Forest." He paused briefly.
"And also anything you have about the Forgotten Tree." He kept his gaze fixed on the tribe leader.
"And if anyone has reported about other creatures like me, I want to know."
"The tribe’s archive is not complete." Averian thought for a few moments and then nodded.
"But I will gather every book, scroll, and old report we have for you." A tired smile formed on his face.
"But not tonight." He looked at his children.
"Now that you have returned, the tribe will celebrate tonight."
"Besides, your mother was waiting for you every day." His gaze stayed on Ravian for a moment.
"She cried almost every night. Before anything else, go see her."
Nemi immediately stood up, Sera also could not hide her emotions, and Ravian lowered his head for a moment.
The weight of the decision he had made had just taken on another form.
He had not only risked himself.
He had kept his entire family between hope and grief for long days.
The three siblings left the house.
Averian stood in his place for a moment and then looked at Lian again.
"Be our guest tonight."
The celebration began after the forest’s green light set.
The tribe’s central square was located among several massive roots.
The fires were lit inside stone bowls so the flames could not reach the moss or roots.
The orange light of the fire combined with the green and blue mana lamps, making the square’s space colorful.
The food was arranged on high platforms.
Pieces of large insect meat were being roasted on bone skewers.
Sweet forest fruits were placed in woven baskets, and cooked roots were served with spicy seasonings.
The mushrooms were grilled with monster fat and fragrant herbs, and a fermented drink made from plant sap was being passed around among the crowd in clay containers.
The sound of drums made from monster skin echoed in the square.
The warriors struck their spears on the ground with a regular rhythm.
A group of Lacerians were dancing with coordinated movements of their legs and tails.
An old man was standing on a short platform and telling a story about one of the tribe’s ancestors.
Ravian, Sera, and Nemi were standing in the center of the square.
An elderly woman tied blue bands around the base of their antennae.
The "returned from death" bands.
Every time a band was tied, the warriors struck their spears firmly on the ground once.
The tribe’s people hugged those three.
Their mother did not let go of Nemi for a long time.
The Lacerian woman touched her three children’s faces several times, as if she still feared their image would disappear.
Lian saw this scene from a short distance.
Seeing the traditions and cultures of different civilizations had its own appeal, especially for him who had a great interest in such topics.
It was interesting to see that besides humans, there were other creatures who could show and understand love, worry, and affection as well as them.
Then he turned his gaze back to the crowd.
The people were still keeping their distance from him.
The looks were not hidden.
Some with fear, some with curiosity, and some with distrust.
Children were peeking from behind the adults.
Every time Lian turned his head toward them, they would quickly hide.
After a while, a few young warriors dared to come closer, and one of them asked.
"Did you really fight those giant ants alone?"
"Yes." Lian chewed a piece of grilled meat.
"Without a spear?" another warrior asked hesitantly.
"Without weapons."
They looked at his healthy fists, as if they expected a sign of that battle to still remain on his hands.
How could a person have such powerful fists?
An old woman with bent antennae came closer.
She looked at the skin on Lian’s forearm for a few moments and then asked.
"Why don’t you have scales?"
"Our species doesn’t have scales." Lian answered.
The old woman, without permission, ran her finger over his forearm.
"Much softer."
Lian said nothing.
"Why don’t you have a tail?" another person asked from behind.
"Are all Otherworldlies this strange?" a child standing near their mother asked loudly.
A few people fell silent, and Lian gave his gaze to the child.
"For us, you are strange. But yes, we don’t have tails, wings, or scales."
There was silence for a moment, then a few people laughed.
Even the child’s mother could not hide her smile.
The tension in the surrounding space eased slightly.
The children came a little closer, the warriors asked more questions, and the looks slowly changed from pure fear to curiosity.
Sera came over with two drink containers and sat next to Lian.
She gave one to him.
"I hope it’s not annoying." She gestured with her gaze around.
"Most of them have never seen anyone from outside the three tribes."
Lian took a sip, and its taste was sweet and slightly spicy.
"It’s fine."
He looked at one of the children who was still examining him without a tail.
Even though it might have seemed annoying, Lian did not care.
In fact, he found talking to the people of this tribe entertaining and interesting.
To some extent, he felt famous and popular, and this feeling, unlike in his own world, gave him a sense of being more special.
"When I was a child, if I saw someone with a tail and antennae who could talk, I would probably stare too."
For the first time, Sera laughed without pressure or worry.
Her laugh was short.
However, while speaking, Lian noticed that the celebration was not completely normal.
A few warriors were leaving the square earlier than the others.
The guards on the wall were more than what seemed necessary for a celebration night.
On some platforms, there were large barrels that were empty.
The families were sharing the drink carefully.
A few people in the corners were talking with low voices and serious faces.
Even the sound of the drums could not completely cover the tribe’s hidden anxiety.
During the days when Ravian and his sisters were absent, something else had happened.
He noticed this, but he did not pay much attention to it.
After all, it was none of his concern.
Averian came over after a while and said to Sera.
"If you don’t mind, I want to talk to your friend alone for a bit."

chapters.title: Chapter 219: The Tribe Of Lacerians IV
paragraphs: Sera looked at her father, she did not know why he wanted to talk to Lian alone, but with the knowledge she had of her father, she was not worried that he would do something wrong or say something bad.
She nodded and stood up, and returned to her family.

Averian sat next to Lian, unlike many leaders, he did not create a formal distance and picked up a cup of drink and said calmly: "The celebration has become lively, what do you think? Are you having fun?"
"I haven’t attended a real celebration in a long time, but everyone is really not calm." Lian answered, he was not lying either.
This was the first real celebration that truly felt like a celebration that he had attended after a long time.
His sister’s birthday celebration was more like a political conflict and only for showing off, strengthening positions, and unveiling his sister.
All the people who were there were nothing but a bunch of wolf-like people, each with their own malicious and evil thoughts and intentions.
But here? This celebration was pure, a happy celebration where you could see everyone’s true intentions from their faces, everyone was happy about the return of the tribe leader’s children.
Although the worry that they were trying to hide in the depths of their being for tonight did not diminish anything.
The tribe leader looked at him for a moment and then gave a faint smile.
"You see correctly." He fixed his gaze on the square.
"The Lacerians are one of the three Lizardman tribes in the Forest of Giants."
He pointed toward the distance.
"The Varkesh live near the rivers and rocky lands. They are more warlike, stricter, and usually solve problems with power."
"The Mireclaws live in the swamps and deep roots. They know poison, plants, and healing better than any other tribe."
"Sometimes we are allies and sometimes enemies, borders, hunting, water... there is always something to disagree about, the reason for the people’s worry is also partly related to this matter."
"So a conflict, huh? I understand, but I became curious, do residential areas like this exist in the other forests?" Lian raised his gaze to the giant roots.
"Yes, but we have no connection with them." Averian said.
"The Forest of Giants is only one of the three forests."

"Very few creatures can travel between the forests. The paths are either destroyed, or so dangerous that no one returns alive, it has been a long time since we had direct contact with the other two forests, and that is why we are not sure what is happening there."

In the other two forests, there was also civilization like their forest, in fact, from his own view, because they live in a calmer and less dangerous structure, they might even have more advanced civilizations.
But it could not be said with certainty.

"The Forgotten Tree, in the legends, is the center of all three forests, it used to help a lot for inter-forest travel, but problems have arisen and no one from our generation has seen it." He then added with a quieter voice: "Our tribe has not seen easy days for a long time."
His gaze remained on his children. "But tonight I don’t want our problems to ruin the joy of my children’s return."

Lian remembered the sentence, although his curiosity about the state of this world increased even more, and more importantly, about the Forgotten Tree, which was probably the only way for him and the others to leave this world.

It was not that he currently had a plan to leave this Special Area, his intuition told him that there were many opportunities in this world and that he would not leave until he had passed his first evolution.
But for this purpose, he might need to search all three forests and find the opportunities, and for this, he needed a way to travel between the three forests.
One could be a great help, but he was not sure if he could cross between the forests with its help or not.
’Maybe the best decision is to find a flying monster’ he thought to himself, a flying monster should not have a problem with traveling between the forests.
And a flying mount would be a great help to him.
But for this, he needed to find one and defeat it first, which currently did not seem like an easy task.

It was in times like these that he understood what a great blessing it was to have a companion and teammate as powerful as himself who could help... but unfortunately, he did not have such a companion.
And he only knew one person who could be such a good companion, and that girl was not here right now.
After the celebration ended, a small house was given to Lian, the house was built inside a low part of the root.
There was a bed of dry moss and monster skin inside it, a small mana lamp was lighting the wall.
There was a bowl of water and a narrow window facing the forest, One remained outside the house and near the tribe’s wall.
Before sleeping, Lian activated Hive Link and checked One’s condition.
Calm, alert.
But in the distance, the sound of guard drums could be heard, a few groups of warriors were moving in the darkness.
The tribe was sleeping, but it was not completely calm.
The next morning, the sound of intense movement woke Lian up, when he came out of the house, there was no trace of the light atmosphere of the previous night left.
The warriors were putting on armor, spears, bows, and shields were being distributed among the groups, a few Lacerians were riding armored six-legged beasts.
They were not riding monsters, but a type of ordinary beast of this world, like horses, that could be tamed.
Water skins, ropes, and large water containers were prepared on the platforms.
Armed groups were leaving the gate, the tribe elders were talking with serious faces.
Lian stood for a few moments and examined the scene, the tribe was preparing for a conflict and he thought about the tribe leader’s words from last night.
Could it be a conflict with one of the other two tribes?
"My father wants to see you." Ravian came toward him with light armor and a new spear, paused briefly and then added: "It seems the information you asked for is ready."
The two moved along the main path. Lian looked at a group of armed warriors. "What happened?"
"I don’t know completely, but we had a few conflicts with the Varkesh." Ravian shrugged.
"You look very relaxed." Lian kept his gaze on his face.
"This is not our first conflict, the three tribes always argue over hunting, borders, or water." Ravian said.
But his tone showed that he himself did not know the real severity of the situation.
They reached the tribe’s council building, inside, Averian and a few tribe elders were standing around a large table.
A map of the water routes was opened on the table, a few colored stones were placed on various points.
The atmosphere was so serious that Ravian frowned at that moment, maybe he was young but he knew this atmosphere was not normal, the seriousness was so heavy that he also felt it.
And he realized that maybe everything was not a simple conflict.
Averian raised his head. "Wait a few minutes, when I’m done with my work, I’ll call you."
"What happened?" Ravian stepped forward.
His father did not answer and he continued: "I also need to know."

Averian wanted to say something, but one of the elders intervened. "He is the future heir of the tribe." The old man kept his gaze fixed on Ravian. "If he is going to take your place one day, he needs to know."
"Were you aware of the drought and water shortage?" The tribe leader sighed and then asked his son.
"Yes, and that’s why we had to go farther for hunting and finding resources and got caught by that bird."
"Which was a very foolish decision." Averian said with a serious look.
His son said nothing, and the tribe leader moved his finger over a few blue lines on the map.
"The situation has gotten worse since you left, the waterways that originated from the upper roots have dried up one after another." He stopped on a thicker branch.
"One of the tribe’s two main water branches also completely dried up three days ago."
The silence became heavier, Averian placed his hand on a point in the west of the map. "Only the Silvervein Basin remains, a source that is shared between us and the Varkesh."
"Those Varkesh claim they need all the water for their tribe’s survival." one of the elders said.
"In the past few days, we have had three conflicts." another elder added, his face hardening. "In the last one, four of our people were killed."
"How did all the waterways dry up so quickly?" Ravian asked in shock, he did not have a complete source of this information but he knew such a thing was not normal.
Such an event was unprecedented and had never been reported before and does not exist in the historical archives.
What was happening to the Forgotten Tree that such a drought was occurring?
"We don’t know, whatever it is, it is related to the Forgotten Tree, maybe something has happened to it." The tribe leader’s gaze remained fixed on the map.
"It seems something is swallowing the water flow before it reaches this area."
Lian looked at the map, the drying up of several routes in a short time did not seem natural.
"Today we will send another group to protect the water route and see if we can negotiate with the Varkesh or not." Averian continued.
"Do I need to come too?" Ravian asked.
"For now, the conflicts have been small." Averian then turned to the elders. "But I am also going today." A few people immediately objected.
"If it’s an ambush, the risk is high."
"The tribe cannot lose its leader."
"Exactly for that reason I have to go, if the Varkesh leader is there, maybe we can stop this conflict before it turns into war." The tribe leader added calmly.
It was clear that his mind could not be changed!

"The Mireclaws live in the swamps and deep roots.
They know poison, plants, and healing better than any other tribe."
"Sometimes we are allies and sometimes enemies, borders, hunting, water... there is always something to disagree about, the reason for the people’s worry is also partly related to this matter."
"So a conflict, huh?
I understand, but I became curious, do residential areas like this exist in the other forests?" Lian raised his gaze to the giant roots.
"Yes, but we have no connection with them." Averian said.
"The Forest of Giants is only one of the three forests."
"Very few creatures can travel between the forests.

The paths are either destroyed, or so dangerous that no one returns alive, it has been a long time since we had direct contact with the other two forests, and that is why we are not sure what is happening there."

In the other two forests, there was also civilization like their forest, in fact, from his own view, because they live in a calmer and less dangerous structure, they might even have more advanced civilizations.
But it could not be said with certainty.

"The Forgotten Tree, in the legends, is the center of all three forests, it used to help a lot for inter-forest travel, but problems have arisen and no one from our generation has seen it." He then added with a quieter voice: "Our tribe has not seen easy days for a long time."
His gaze remained on his children.
"But tonight I don’t want our problems to ruin the joy of my children’s return."

Lian remembered the sentence, although his curiosity about the state of this world increased even more, and more importantly, about the Forgotten Tree, which was probably the only way for him and the others to leave this world.

It was not that he currently had a plan to leave this Special Area, his intuition told him that there were many opportunities in this world and that he would not leave until he had passed his first evolution.
But for this purpose, he might need to search all three forests and find the opportunities, and for this, he needed a way to travel between the three forests.
One could be a great help, but he was not sure if he could cross between the forests with its help or not.
’Maybe the best decision is to find a flying monster’ he thought to himself, a flying monster should not have a problem with traveling between the forests.
And a flying mount would be a great help to him.
But for this, he needed to find one and defeat it first, which currently did not seem like an easy task.

It was in times like these that he understood what a great blessing it was to have a companion and teammate as powerful as himself who could help... but unfortunately, he did not have such a companion.
And he only knew one person who could be such a good companion, and that girl was not here right now.
After the celebration ended, a small house was given to Lian, the house was built inside a low part of the root.
There was a bed of dry moss and monster skin inside it, a small mana lamp was lighting the wall.
There was a bowl of water and a narrow window facing the forest, One remained outside the house and near the tribe’s wall.
Before sleeping, Lian activated Hive Link and checked One’s condition.
Calm, alert.
But in the distance, the sound of guard drums could be heard, a few groups of warriors were moving in the darkness.
The tribe was sleeping, but it was not completely calm.
The next morning, the sound of intense movement woke Lian up, when he came out of the house, there was no trace of the light atmosphere of the previous night left.
The warriors were putting on armor, spears, bows, and shields were being distributed among the groups, a few Lacerians were riding armored six-legged beasts.
They were not riding monsters, but a type of ordinary beast of this world, like horses, that could be tamed.
Water skins, ropes, and large water containers were prepared on the platforms.
Armed groups were leaving the gate, the tribe elders were talking with serious faces.
Lian stood for a few moments and examined the scene, the tribe was preparing for a conflict and he thought about the tribe leader’s words from last night.
Could it be a conflict with one of the other two tribes?
"My father wants to see you." Ravian came toward him with light armor and a new spear, paused briefly and then added: "It seems the information you asked for is ready."
The two moved along the main path.
Lian looked at a group of armed warriors.
"What happened?"
"I don’t know completely, but we had a few conflicts with the Varkesh." Ravian shrugged.
"You look very relaxed." Lian kept his gaze on his face.
"This is not our first conflict, the three tribes always argue over hunting, borders, or water." Ravian said.
But his tone showed that he himself did not know the real severity of the situation.
They reached the tribe’s council building, inside, Averian and a few tribe elders were standing around a large table.
A map of the water routes was opened on the table, a few colored stones were placed on various points.
The atmosphere was so serious that Ravian frowned at that moment, maybe he was young but he knew this atmosphere was not normal, the seriousness was so heavy that he also felt it.
And he realized that maybe everything was not a simple conflict.
Averian raised his head.
"Wait a few minutes, when I’m done with my work, I’ll call you."
"What happened?" Ravian stepped forward.
His father did not answer and he continued: "I also need to know."
Averian wanted to say something, but one of the elders intervened.
"He is the future heir of the tribe." The old man kept his gaze fixed on Ravian.
"If he is going to take your place one day, he needs to know."
"Were you aware of the drought and water shortage?" The tribe leader sighed and then asked his son.
"Yes, and that’s why we had to go farther for hunting and finding resources and got caught by that bird."
"Which was a very foolish decision." Averian said with a serious look.
His son said nothing, and the tribe leader moved his finger over a few blue lines on the map.
"The situation has gotten worse since you left, the waterways that originated from the upper roots have dried up one after another." He stopped on a thicker branch.
"One of the tribe’s two main water branches also completely dried up three days ago."
The silence became heavier, Averian placed his hand on a point in the west of the map.
"Only the Silvervein Basin remains, a source that is shared between us and the Varkesh."
"Those Varkesh claim they need all the water for their tribe’s survival." one of the elders said.
"In the past few days, we have had three conflicts." another elder added, his face hardening.
"In the last one, four of our people were killed."
"How did all the waterways dry up so quickly?" Ravian asked in shock, he did not have a complete source of this information but he knew such a thing was not normal.
Such an event was unprecedented and had never been reported before and does not exist in the historical archives.
What was happening to the Forgotten Tree that such a drought was occurring?
"We don’t know, whatever it is, it is related to the Forgotten Tree, maybe something has happened to it." The tribe leader’s gaze remained fixed on the map.
"It seems something is swallowing the water flow before it reaches this area."
Lian looked at the map, the drying up of several routes in a short time did not seem natural.
"Today we will send another group to protect the water route and see if we can negotiate with the Varkesh or not." Averian continued.
"Do I need to come too?" Ravian asked.
"For now, the conflicts have been small." Averian then turned to the elders.
"But I am also going today." A few people immediately objected.
"If it’s an ambush, the risk is high."
"The tribe cannot lose its leader."
"Exactly for that reason I have to go, if the Varkesh leader is there, maybe we can stop this conflict before it turns into war." The tribe leader added calmly.
It was clear that his mind could not be changed!

chapters.title: Chapter 220: The Tribe Of Lacerians ( Final )
paragraphs: The tribe leader’s gaze fell on Lian. "Your request has been fulfilled."
"Every book, scroll, and old report we had about the other two forests and the Forgotten Tree, I have gathered in my personal hut." He pointed at Ravian.
"He will take you there."
The archive of the tribe’s books and scrolls was very old, dating back decades and even hundreds of years.
Under normal circumstances, gathering information about the topics Lian had requested could have taken days.
The topics he had requested were very broad, and there was a great deal of information about them.
But the tribe leader had ordered that everything possible be gathered as quickly as possible for the one who had saved his children.
"Thank you." Lian expressed his gratitude.
Averian just nodded.
The leader’s private hut was located on a higher platform, in a quieter part of the tribe.

"You’re lucky. Almost no one is allowed to enter there." On the way, Ravian said, though there was no jealousy in his tone because that hut was for studying, and he didn’t really enjoy studying that much.
"How is it different from his house?" Lian asked.
"It’s used for studying, maps, and when he wants to be alone. Even we don’t enter without permission."
The hut was built inside a narrower root. When they entered, the smell of dry skin, wood, and plant ink reached their noses.
Shelves of wood and bone were on the walls.
Scrolls were tied with colored threads, old maps were spread on the tables.
Carved stone pieces with faded writings could be seen in the corners, books with monster skin covers were on the shelves.
A large mana lamp on the center table created a white light, and several books and scrolls were already arranged on the main table.
Ravian pointed at them. "This is it."
Then he gripped his spear tighter. "I’m going to the training ground." A serious eagerness could be seen in his eyes.
"I need to become strong like you. If I’m going to protect the tribe one day, I can’t be that weak again."
"Good, good luck, but don’t push yourself too hard. Recovery is also part of training." Lian said calmly.
"Of course!" A brief smile settled on Ravian’s face.
He left the hut.
Lian sat behind the table and opened the first scroll. The title was written in red ink.
[Emberroot Forest]
The text described a forest where a large part of the ground and roots were always warm.
Its soil was dark and red, heat veins like arteries moving beneath the ground.
The trees had roots like glowing coal.
Rivers of very hot water passed through the forest, and in some areas, semi-molten flows could be seen.
At night, red steam rose from the ground, natural fire in Emberroot never died out, it would transfer from one root to another.
In a section of the scroll, known monsters were introduced.
Ashhide Behemoth.
A massive creature with stone and heat armor that radiated heat through the cracks in its body.
Emberwing Mantis.
A flying insect with burning blades.
Cinder Wolves.
Wolves that hunted in packs and left footprints that kept the ground burning for a few minutes.
There were reports of Salamander tribes, also fire-born creatures and groups of armored humanoids mentioned only in stories.
But the main danger of Emberroot was not the heat. According to several reports, the forest had periods where all the roots started moving in harmony.
The text referred to these periods as the "Forest’s Awakening."
One writer had claimed that Emberroot grew on the body of a very large creature.
Lian lingered on that sentence for a few moments.
If other Awakened ones had appeared there, those with heat resistance or Fire talents would have a better chance of survival.
But even they would not be safe against a forest that could awaken on its own.
He opened the second scroll.
[Glassthorn Forest]
Its description was completely different.
A cold, transparent, and deceptive forest, the trees had glass-like or crystal shells.
Transparent thorns refracted light and were almost invisible from a distance, a constant mist covered a large part of the forest.
The sound of breaking glass would sometimes echo without any clear reason, the ground was covered with very sharp crystal pieces.
But the main danger was light, the reflections made paths appear multiple.
Some travelers had moved in circles for days without realizing they had returned to their starting point.
Mirror Stalkers hid among the reflections.
Glasshorn Stags could deflect mana and light attacks with their crystal horns.
Shard Spiders made almost invisible webs of glass.
One report mentioned white-skinned, eyeless humanoid creatures that sensed the environment through vibration and light.
Another scroll spoke of a crystalline and abandoned city deep in the forest.
Lian thought to himself that Awakened ones who appeared in Glassthorn either died in the first few days or were forced to form groups very quickly.
Being alone in a forest where even the path in front of you could not be trusted was almost certain death.
The scrolls about the Forgotten Tree were much older. The ink on some of them had faded, and some sections were missing.
The tree’s name changed in different documents.
The Forgotten Tree.
Root of Three Worlds.
The Tree Without a Forest.
The First Root.

Legend said that all three forests were connected to this tree, but the tree itself did not belong to any of them. Its roots burned in Emberroot, turned into crystal in Glassthorn, and rose from the ground like mountains in the Forest of Giants.
But the main trunk was located in a place that was not accessible from the usual paths.
One text said the tree was at the center of the world.
Another claimed the tree was outside the world and that the three forests were only shadows of its roots.
In a broken scroll, a sentence remained.
"Whoever reaches the heart of the Forgotten Tree can open the path between all three forests."
Lian opened another scroll, a line in the middle caught his attention.
"The tree knows those who do not belong to this world better than the children of this world."
Lian was silent for a few moments. Otherworldlies, in the present, this concept referred to him and those like him.
But in the past, it clearly referred to the natives of the tenth Ruined Realm, meaning they too could come to this world, but why and how?
What was the purpose of the rifts opening between worlds? What was behind it?
These were questions he had no answers to, and it was unlikely he would find answers anytime soon.
Then he pushed the thoughts aside and continued reading the reports.
In the reports about finding the path, certain signs were repeated.
A root without a shadow, a waterway that moves against the slope, three moons or three lights seen from one point.
A gateway inside a dead trunk, but there was no precise map, no confirmed path was recorded.
Lian placed the documents next to each other.
The Awakened ones were probably scattered across all three forests. It would be logical for survivors to move toward civilization, water, and safe areas.
In the Forest of Giants, the Lizardman tribes and rivers were the best destination.
In Emberroot, probably the hot rivers, stone caves, and Salamander territory.
In Glassthorn, perhaps the crystalline city or any place that offered protection against the mist and reflections.
But if the final goal was the Forgotten Tree, sooner or later the survivors from all three forests would be forced to move toward the center.
"If the others are alive, they are either looking for civilization... or looking for that same tree." Lian whispered under his breath.

chapters.title: Chapter 221: Another Otherworldly? I
paragraphs: With his knowledge of his group members, there was no need to worry about them, they could all handle themselves and adapt to conditions.
It was even possible that they had already reached civilizations or found each other.
If they were in the other two forests, their situation would be much better, because at least those forests are of normal size and they are not like ants there.
In this Forest of Giants, it is the most dangerous area for awakened ones, even moving and traveling through this forest can take days and weeks.
He was lucky to have obtained One, otherwise even for him it could have taken days and weeks.
A few hours later, he closed the last scroll, arranged the documents neatly on the table, there was not much else to read.
He had obtained all the information he wanted, the only problem was that there was no precise way to travel between the three forests.

Not that there were no paths, on the contrary, several paths were mentioned, but each of them was deadly, and at least based on the descriptions in these reports, each had creatures at least as powerful as the Sky Giant Bird.
He now understood why contact between the three forests had been cut off for so long, with such monsters blocking the paths between them, who could travel to another forest?
However, there was one option that led to the Glassthorn Forest, a valley path known as the Giants’ Graveyard.
Its name was terrifying, and so was its path, but no creature at the level of the Sky Giant Bird lived there, and that at least opened a window of hope for Lian.
If he wanted to travel between the forests on the ground, the Giants’ Graveyard was the only option.
And then he left the hut.
He decided to see the training ground and find Ravian. The training ground was located in the space between several roots.
Dummies made of skin, bone, and moss were installed in the corners, stone pillars for testing strength existed.
Obstacle courses were built on the roots, several small fields for fighting existed.
Targets hung from ropes for archery and spear throwing moved. In a separate section, riding beasts were being trained.
Ravian was training in one of the fields, thrusting his spear forward.
Pulling it back, changing his step, striking again. His movements were powerful, but still raw.
He was putting too much pressure on his shoulder, and his back foot’s position during the attack was too open.
He repeated the same movement many times, even when his hands were trembling from exhaustion.
Lian watched his training from a distance. There were many mistakes in using the spear. His attacks were instinctive, meaning they had no skill or strategy.
His foot placement was terrible. He attacked recklessly and only went for the head. Maybe it was not bad, but it made his pattern predictable, exactly like monsters.
But even though his form was very raw and his attacks were instinctive, with just one look it was clear that he had high physical strength.
In every attack, his muscles would contract and a lot of power would be used, and he could maintain this level of power for a long time, which showed his high stamina.
For a fighter, these were very important innate traits, and Lian could see great talent in him.
He wanted to approach, but before he could say anything, the sound of a shout came from the direction of the gate.
Then the alarm sound, then chaos.
People started running, the sound of crying and orders echoed through the tribe.
"What happened?" Lian looked around with a frown, suddenly the entire atmosphere of the tribe changed.
Ravian stopped training and lowered his spear. "What happened?" He also realized something had happened, and his gaze fell on Lian.
The two moved toward the gate without saying anything. The crowd grew larger every moment, the sound of wounded beasts was heard.
The dispatched group had returned, but not in order. The riding beasts were wounded, blood was dry on their armor.
A few soldiers were being carried on stretchers, some had broken armor.
"Bring the healers!" one of the warriors shouted.
The crowd parted. In the center of the group, Averian was lying on the back of one of the riding beasts.
His face had no color, a large part of his body was covered in blood, and both his arms had been severed from above the elbows.
The ends of the wounds had been burned with fire or mana to stop the bleeding.
But blood was still passing through the wrapped cloth.
Ravian stood motionless, the spear fell from his hand, and the sound of it hitting the ground was lost among the screams.
Sera and Nemi arrived from the other side of the crowd.
Nemi completely froze upon seeing her father, as if she had even lost the ability to breathe.
Sera took a step forward.
Then stopped, her eyes fixed on the empty space where her father’s hands used to be.
Averian was still alive, but his breaths were very weak.
One of the wounded warriors was standing next to the beast, his face covered in blood and dirt.
"It was an ambush..." he said with a broken voice, his breath trembling, his eyes full of fear.
"The Varkesh weren’t alone."
The crowd fell silent. The man raised his gaze, his eyes moving among the people, then fixed on Lian.
Fear formed on his face. His trembling finger pointed at him.
"There was something else there." His voice almost turned into a whisper.
"It looked like him."
All eyes turned toward Lian.
He looked at Averian, at the cut wounds.
At the thin black marks that remained around the burns on the arms.
They had gone to fight over water, but what had returned Averian to the tribe with both hands severed did not belong to any of the three tribes.
And according to that soldier’s words, that thing was an Otherworldly, or more precisely, an awakened one...

Then stopped, her eyes fixed on the empty space where her father’s hands used to be.
Averian was still alive, but his breaths were very weak.
One of the wounded warriors was standing next to the beast, his face covered in blood and dirt.
"It was an ambush..." he said with a broken voice, his breath trembling, his eyes full of fear.
"The Varkesh weren’t alone."
The crowd fell silent.
The man raised his gaze, his eyes moving among the people, then fixed on Lian.
Fear formed on his face.
His trembling finger pointed at him.
"There was something else there." His voice almost turned into a whisper.
"It looked like him."
All eyes turned toward Lian.
He looked at Averian, at the cut wounds.
At the thin black marks that remained around the burns on the arms.
They had gone to fight over water, but what had returned Averian to the tribe with both hands severed did not belong to any of the three tribes.
And according to that soldier’s words, that thing was an Otherworldly, or more precisely, an awakened one...

chapters.title: Chapter 222: The Wrath Of A Son
paragraphs: "It looked like him." The wounded soldier’s trembling finger was pointed at Lian.
His voice was weak, but those few words were enough to make the entire tribe fall into silence.
The screams stopped for a moment.
The sound of the alarm, which was still coming from above the towers, seemed farther away.
The gazes separated from Averian’s bloody body and fixed on Lian one after another.
Some of the Lacerians unconsciously stepped back.
A few guards tightened their hands around their spears.
The looks that until last night were mixed with fear and curiosity had now taken on a different color.
Doubt, terror, and suspicion that had not yet dared to turn into accusation.
For them, Lian was an Otherworldly, the same legendary creature who had saved the leader’s children.
But now, a soldier who had returned from the Silvervein Basin was claiming that a creature resembling him had reduced Averian to this state.
The line between savior and disaster had suddenly become thinner in the minds of the tribe’s people.
However, at that moment, there was no time left for the people to be afraid of Lian.
Nemi was the first to move.
She passed through the crowd and reached the wounded riding beast.
A few steps away from her father, she suddenly stopped, her eyes fixed on Averian’s two arms... or more precisely, on the empty space where they used to be.
Two thick and bloody pieces of cloth were tied around the upper arms.
The ends of the wounds had been burned with fire or mana, but blood was still seeping from under the cloth and dripping onto the riding beast’s side.
For a few seconds, Nemi could not even cry.
Her lips parted, but no sound came out.
Her eyes trembled, her breathing became short, as if her mind refused to accept the image she was seeing, and then her voice broke.
"Father..."
Averian showed no reaction.
His head had fallen to one side, and his face was a color between gray and dead green.
Nemi moved forward and placed her hand on his face.
"Father?" This time her voice was louder.
But again, no answer came.
The tears suddenly poured from her eyes.
"Father, wake up..." She called him again.
And again.
But Averian only took weak and broken breaths.
Sera was standing a few steps back, at first she tried to control herself.
She kept her shoulders straight, clenched her jaw, and looked at the healers, but when the cloth on the right side became completely soaked with blood, the wall of her calm broke.
A tear ran down from the corner of her eye, she turned back to the healers and almost shouted.
"Why are you still standing there? Treat him!"
One of the healers came forward. "We are trying, but—"
"Then faster!" Sera cut him off.
Her voice was not from anger, but from a terror that had found no other way to come out.
At that same time, a woman rushed forward from the crowd.
The mother of Ravian, Sera, and Nemi, the wife of Averian.
At first, she looked at the man on the beast for a few moments.
Not from distance, not from not recognizing him, but as if her mind refused to accept that this armless and bloody body was the same husband who had left the tribe healthy that morning.
Then her face crumbled, a muffled scream came from her throat, and she fell next to the beast and took her husband’s face between her two hands.
"Averian..."
She said his name once, then again with a more trembling voice.
"Averian, open your eyes."
She pressed her forehead to his, tears flowing on her facial scales.
The night before, she had held the children she thought were dead in her arms again.
Now, only a few hours later, she might lose her husband.
Around them, the tribe’s panic spread.
A few children started crying upon seeing the blood, mothers took them away from the field.
The guards who considered Averian invincible were looking at their leader in disbelief.
A few warriors struck the ends of their spears on the ground in anger.
In a corner, two tribe elders spoke quietly and quickly.
Their words were not clear, but words like "succession," "Varkesh," and "gate defense" could be heard.
"If the leader survives, what happens?" one of the people asked with a trembling voice.
Another man did not answer, because he had no answer.
Averian was not just the chief of the Lacerians, he was the balance between the elders, commanders, and families of the tribe.
He was the one who stopped small conflicts before they turned into war, the one who managed hunting routes, defense, and water distribution.
Seeing him in that state was like the tribe’s main wall breaking.
Lian was standing calmly in the middle of that chaos, not because he was insensitive, but because instead of sinking into panic, his mind immediately started analyzing.
His gaze fixed on Averian’s wounds, two cuts, almost level and completely smooth.
The limbs had been severed with something very sharp, a high-quality weapon, or a skill that ignored physical resistance.
Based on what the soldiers had said, the person who did this looked like him, so it was clear that an awakened one was involved.
The question was obvious, which Awakened could do such a thing?
The answer was more unpleasant than what the tribe’s people imagined.
Many people.
A large number of Awakened ones had entered this world, among them probably dozens or maybe more had such power.
Although the tribe leader is powerful, his raw power is equal to a level 27-28 awakened one, but that is only raw power.
He has no skills like awakened ones, he has no class or talents, and he also does not have powerful high-rank armor and weapons.
Against awakened ones, raw power alone cannot win.
However, something about the cuts was familiar, too clean, too precise.
The attacker had not tried to kill Averian.
If his goal was death, he could have targeted his neck or heart, but instead, he had severed both hands with two movements.
And besides, even among all the awakened ones who entered the Special Area, there are very, very few who could easily and decisively defeat this old man.
Even the other awakened ones, with all their advantages, would still have a hard fight, after all, this old man’s raw power can still match a level 27-28.
A name formed in Lian’s mind, but he was not sure yet, but his guess was serious from that moment, and there was only one way to find out.
At the same time, the healers lowered Averian from the beast and placed him on a wooden stretcher.
Ravian was still standing motionless, neither crying nor shouting, only looking at the blood on the ground.
His fists were clenched so tightly that his nails had cut into his palms.
Drops of blood were falling from between his fingers, his breathing became faster every moment, his silence was more terrifying than Nemi’s crying and Sera’s screaming.
Suddenly, he bent down, picked up the spear that had fallen on the ground, and without saying a word, turned and ran toward the gate.
Sera immediately understood. "Ravian!"
He did not stop, he pushed through the crowd and crossed the tribe’s main path at full speed.
Nemi looked at Lian with wet eyes. "He wants to go there..."
Sera grabbed Lian’s arm, her fingers trembling from the intensity of her anxiety.
"Please, stop him." Her gaze was on the gate. "With this state, he’ll get himself killed."
Lian looked at Ravian’s path for a moment, then nodded. "Stay here."
He moved, and a few seconds later, he passed through the gate.
Ravian was running among the massive roots, every step hitting the ground with anger, pushing aside the moss branches and moving forward without regard for the uneven paths.
He knew the direction to the Silvervein Basin, he intended to go there alone.
Alone.
Without a map.
Without enough force.
And without knowing exactly who or what had defeated his father.
Lian easily caught up to him, passed him, and stopped a few dozen meters ahead.
When Ravian rounded the root bend, he almost collided with him, he stopped with difficulty, his breathing heavy.
"Move aside."
Lian did not move.
Ravian raised his spear, his hands were trembling, not from fear, but from anger and the pressure of emotions he could no longer control.
"I said move aside!"
"Where are you going?" Lian did not even take a defensive stance.
"You know where!"
"And when you get there, what will you do?"
"I’ll kill whoever did this!" Ravian said with a loud voice.
"Alone?" Lian asked.
That one word was enough to explode Ravian’s anger, he threw the spear toward Lian’s chest.
The strike was fast, for Ravian’s level, even precise, but Lian only turned his wrist.
Two of his fingers landed on the blade and deflected its path by a few centimeters, the spear passed by his shoulder.
Ravian struck a second time without stopping, Lian stepped aside.
A third strike.
Deflected.
A fourth.
Evaded.
The more Ravian attacked, the more disorderly his movements became, it was no longer practice or technique, only a desperate attempt to get through.
Lian finally grabbed the spear’s shaft, with a simple pull, he took the weapon from Ravian’s hand and threw it a few meters away.
And that crazy boy punched his chest, the strike had no effect.
A second punch.
Then a third.
Then a fourth.
Lian allowed Ravian to hit with all his might.
On his chest, shoulder, arm, but the power gap was so great that Lian did not even step back, it was as if a breeze was caressing his skin.
That is how ineffective those strikes were.
Upon seeing the painful expression on that boy’s face, he sighed, if these childish blows could calm him down a little, then why not?
