chapters.title: Chapter 223: Another Otherworldly? II
paragraphs: Finally, Ravian’s breath broke. He threw the last punch, his hand remained on Lian’s chest, and his head dropped.
The anger inside him began to crack, and his voice broke.
"What if he dies?"
Lian said nothing and just decided to listen. Now was not the time to speak, it was time to listen.
"What if he can’t lead the tribe anymore?" His shoulders trembled.
"I am the heir." He gave a bitter and short laugh.
"But I can’t even protect myself." Everything he had held back in front of his family was now pouring out.
"I am weak." He clenched his fist on Lian’s chest.
"I have always been weak. If I was as strong as him, he wouldn’t have had to go himself." His breath trembled.
"If I was as strong as you, no one could have done this to him."
Lian looked at him for a few moments, then, unlike the heavy atmosphere, laughed briefly.
"What’s so funny?" Ravian raised his head with anger.
"That you think becoming strong happens just by wishing and regretting." Lian said calmly, and then added.
"But if you really want to become strong, I can help you."
For a moment, Ravian even forgot his grief.
"Really?"
"Yeah."
"Like you?" His eyes brightened slightly.
A faint smile settled on Lian’s face.
"No." Then more seriously.
"Like yourself. But much stronger than what you are now." Reaching his level was almost impossible, especially for the natives of this world who had a completely different power system.
A spark of hope appeared in Ravian’s eyes, very weak but real and present.
"Besides, who said your father’s future or your tribe’s future is over?" Lian then said.
"Both his arms are cut off." Ravian lowered his gaze, his voice bitter.
"Even the tribe’s best healers can’t bring back lost arms."
Lian just smiled.
"Don’t worry."
Ravian raised his head and saw Lian’s strange confidence.
"Can you do something?"
Lian did not answer directly, he picked up the spear from the ground and handed it to him.
"Let’s go back."
Ravian looked at him for a few moments, then took the spear. This time he did not resist.
When the two returned to the tribe, Averian had been taken to the medical center. The medical center was built inside a wide and moist root.
The smell of medicinal plants, blood, smoke, and bitter pastes was in the air.
A few stone beds were placed on both sides of the space, healing plants were shining with white and green light above the patients’ heads.
Averian was lying on the main bed. The two ends of his arms were wrapped with layers of plant paste and cloth.
Three healers were standing around him. One was controlling the flow of vital mana, another was trying to keep the bleeding stopped.
The third was grinding plants in a stone bowl.
The level of healing in this world was thousands of steps behind the Ruined Realm and even Lian’s world. The difference was so great that it could not even be described.
Of course, it was also logical. This world did not have access to all the advantages that awakened ones had, and they were forced to treat patients with these same plants.
Sera, Nemi, their mother, a few tribe elders, and the guards’ commander were present.
When Sera saw Ravian, she immediately went to him and struck his chest with her healthy hand.
"Never do something so stupid again!"
Ravian said nothing, and Sera struck his chest again but this time weaker.
Tears were still on her face.
"Did you think if you also went and didn’t come back, what would our mother do?"
"I’m sorry." Ravian lowered his head.
Sera looked at him for a few moments, then turned to Lian.
"Thank you for bringing him back."
Lian nodded, his gaze fixed on Averian’s wounds. From close range, what he had seen was clearer.
Two almost identical cuts, smooth, the bones were not broken or shattered but only severed. On the edge of the wound, a very thin trace of cold and dark energy remained.
Something like a shadow that had frozen on the burnt tissue.
Lian frowned, his guess became stronger, and then he stepped forward.
"May I?"
"What are you going to do?" the main healer, an elderly woman with pale blue scales, asked hesitantly.
Lian reached his hand into his storage space.
He took out a small glass bottle, a green and golden liquid was swirling inside it. Even from behind the glass, its dense vital energy could be felt.
It was one of the healing potions he had bought, of course a B-rank healing potion that had high value, but he had no problem using this potion for this old man.
But Averian was not just the tribe leader. The information, security, and trust of the Lacerians largely depended on his survival and health.
Besides, he wanted to ask this old man some questions, so he could not let him die.
Lian opened the bottle’s cap. The healer stepped forward.
"Wait, what is that?"
Without answering, he poured the liquid on Averian’s chest and arms, and everyone was shocked for a moment.
"What are you doing?!" the healer shouted.
Before the liquid could spill on the bed, it turned into green and golden light. The bright energy spread over the tribe leader’s body. First, it gathered on the severed wounds.
The bleeding stopped at that same moment. The cloths started shining from underneath.
The healers stepped back. A quiet sound was heard from under the layers of cloth.
The sound of growth. White bone came out from the severed point. At first only a few centimeters, then faster, and the two arm bones took shape.
Red muscle strands wrapped around them. Veins grew like thin branches, and nerves formed among the tissue.
Skin stretched over the muscles, and finally, green and gray scales appeared on the surface.
Two complete forearms, two wrists, and fingers.
Averian’s hands regrew right before the eyes of everyone in the medical center.
The space became completely silent.
Nemi even forgot her crying. Sera looked at the new hands with a half-open mouth.
Averian’s wife had placed both hands on her mouth, her eyes full of disbelief and hope.
The healers had stepped back a few steps, their gaze at Lian was like looking at something sacred or incomprehensible.
Averian suddenly took a deep breath. His chest rose, and color returned to his face.
His eyes opened, he looked at the ceiling for a few moments, then turned his head and his gaze fell on his family, and then on his hands.
He raised them in front of his face, bent his fingers, and opened them again.
"This..." His voice was weak and confused.
"What happened?"
His wife could no longer hold back. She hugged him, and Nemi clung to her father from the other side. Sera also came closer.
Ravian stood a few steps back, but his eyes were wet.
"Your hands... came back." the main healer said with a trembling voice.
Averian gave his gaze to Lian. It took a while for him to put everything together, and then he moved away from his family and tried to sit up.
"You?"
"Yeah." Lian said calmly.
The tribe leader looked at him for a few moments. This time, the gratitude was not from the position of a leader, nor as someone who has a political debt.
His voice came from the deepest part of his being.
"Not just my children, but now you have also saved me. This is a favor that I will never forget as long as I live."
"Thank me later. First, tell me what happened." Lian said with a little seriousness.
Averian was silent for a few moments, then allowed the healers to open the remaining cloths.
His new hands were completely healthy. He took a deep breath and started explaining.
"When we reached the Silvervein, the Varkesh were already there." His tone was calm, but anger could be felt beneath it.
"I intended to talk, but those bastards wouldn’t even listen." His gaze hardened.
"Their commander directly ordered an attack." He explained about the conflict. The Varkesh had fortified themselves around the basin beforehand.
Their archers shot arrows from above the roots. The Lacerian forces were initially pushed back.
But Averian personally entered the battle, defeated two Varkesh commanders, broke their defensive line, and the tide slowly turned.
"We were winning." He said and added.
"A few of them had even dropped their weapons. That’s when that creature appeared."
"Looked like me?" Lian asked.
"Yeah." Averian nodded.
"Was it a man or a woman?"
"A woman."
Lian’s guess moved one step closer to certainty.
"Appearance?"
Averian thought for a few moments.
"She was tall, had fair skin, silver hair, and completely black eyes."
"She wore light dark armor, built for speed, the best armor I had ever seen, a masterpiece in every way." Then he said more slowly.
"There was no emotion on her face. No anger, no excitement, and not even hatred." He looked at his new hands.
"As if cutting off my hands was no different for her than cutting a dry branch."
"Her weapon was a sword?" Lian also wanted to use the last piece of the puzzle.
"Maybe it was a sword, but I didn’t even see it clearly." He placed his hand on the previous spot of the wound.
"The first strike cut off my right hand, the second cut off my left hand." His voice became heavy for a moment.
"She could have killed me, but she didn’t. She just said we no longer have the right to approach the water."
Averian said the strange woman then stepped aside. And the Varkesh allowed the remaining soldiers to pick him up and return to the tribe.
It was complete humiliation. Not just defeat, but a major warning.
Lian let out a quiet sigh. Silver hair, black eyes, an emotionless face, and speed that Averian could not even follow.
He was almost sure. Maybe there were other details, but the chance that another person with all these characteristics existed among the Awakened ones was very low.
"I want to see the Varkesh." He then added.
"But it’s dangerous." Nemi immediately raised her head.
Her worry was real. Whatever that creature was, it was someone who had defeated her father in a few moves.
What Lian also face deadly danger?

"Both his arms are cut off." Ravian lowered his gaze, his voice bitter.
"Even the tribe’s best healers can’t bring back lost arms."
Lian just smiled.
"Don’t worry."
Ravian raised his head and saw Lian’s strange confidence.
"Can you do something?"
Lian did not answer directly, he picked up the spear from the ground and handed it to him.
"Let’s go back."
Ravian looked at him for a few moments, then took the spear.
This time he did not resist.
When the two returned to the tribe, Averian had been taken to the medical center.
The medical center was built inside a wide and moist root.
The smell of medicinal plants, blood, smoke, and bitter pastes was in the air.
A few stone beds were placed on both sides of the space, healing plants were shining with white and green light above the patients’ heads.
Averian was lying on the main bed.
The two ends of his arms were wrapped with layers of plant paste and cloth.
Three healers were standing around him.
One was controlling the flow of vital mana, another was trying to keep the bleeding stopped.
The third was grinding plants in a stone bowl.
The level of healing in this world was thousands of steps behind the Ruined Realm and even Lian’s world.
The difference was so great that it could not even be described.
Of course, it was also logical.
This world did not have access to all the advantages that awakened ones had, and they were forced to treat patients with these same plants.
Sera, Nemi, their mother, a few tribe elders, and the guards’ commander were present.
When Sera saw Ravian, she immediately went to him and struck his chest with her healthy hand.
"Never do something so stupid again!"
Ravian said nothing, and Sera struck his chest again but this time weaker.
Tears were still on her face.
"Did you think if you also went and didn’t come back, what would our mother do?"
"I’m sorry." Ravian lowered his head.
Sera looked at him for a few moments, then turned to Lian.
"Thank you for bringing him back."
Lian nodded, his gaze fixed on Averian’s wounds.
From close range, what he had seen was clearer.
Two almost identical cuts, smooth, the bones were not broken or shattered but only severed.
On the edge of the wound, a very thin trace of cold and dark energy remained.
Something like a shadow that had frozen on the burnt tissue.
Lian frowned, his guess became stronger, and then he stepped forward.
"May I?"
"What are you going to do?" the main healer, an elderly woman with pale blue scales, asked hesitantly.
Lian reached his hand into his storage space.
He took out a small glass bottle, a green and golden liquid was swirling inside it.
Even from behind the glass, its dense vital energy could be felt.
It was one of the healing potions he had bought, of course a B-rank healing potion that had high value, but he had no problem using this potion for this old man.
But Averian was not just the tribe leader.
The information, security, and trust of the Lacerians largely depended on his survival and health.
Besides, he wanted to ask this old man some questions, so he could not let him die.
Lian opened the bottle’s cap.
The healer stepped forward.
"Wait, what is that?"
Without answering, he poured the liquid on Averian’s chest and arms, and everyone was shocked for a moment.
"What are you doing?!" the healer shouted.
Before the liquid could spill on the bed, it turned into green and golden light.
The bright energy spread over the tribe leader’s body.
First, it gathered on the severed wounds.
The bleeding stopped at that same moment.
The cloths started shining from underneath.
The healers stepped back.
A quiet sound was heard from under the layers of cloth.
The sound of growth.
White bone came out from the severed point.
At first only a few centimeters, then faster, and the two arm bones took shape.
Red muscle strands wrapped around them.
Veins grew like thin branches, and nerves formed among the tissue.
Skin stretched over the muscles, and finally, green and gray scales appeared on the surface.
Two complete forearms, two wrists, and fingers.
Averian’s hands regrew right before the eyes of everyone in the medical center.
The space became completely silent.
Nemi even forgot her crying.
Sera looked at the new hands with a half-open mouth.
Averian’s wife had placed both hands on her mouth, her eyes full of disbelief and hope.
The healers had stepped back a few steps, their gaze at Lian was like looking at something sacred or incomprehensible.
Averian suddenly took a deep breath.
His chest rose, and color returned to his face.
His eyes opened, he looked at the ceiling for a few moments, then turned his head and his gaze fell on his family, and then on his hands.
He raised them in front of his face, bent his fingers, and opened them again.
"This..." His voice was weak and confused.
"What happened?"
His wife could no longer hold back.
She hugged him, and Nemi clung to her father from the other side.
Sera also came closer.
Ravian stood a few steps back, but his eyes were wet.
"Your hands... came back." the main healer said with a trembling voice.
Averian gave his gaze to Lian.
It took a while for him to put everything together, and then he moved away from his family and tried to sit up.
"You?"
"Yeah." Lian said calmly.
The tribe leader looked at him for a few moments.
This time, the gratitude was not from the position of a leader, nor as someone who has a political debt.
His voice came from the deepest part of his being.
"Not just my children, but now you have also saved me.
This is a favor that I will never forget as long as I live."
"Thank me later.
First, tell me what happened." Lian said with a little seriousness.
Averian was silent for a few moments, then allowed the healers to open the remaining cloths.
His new hands were completely healthy.
He took a deep breath and started explaining.
"When we reached the Silvervein, the Varkesh were already there." His tone was calm, but anger could be felt beneath it.
"I intended to talk, but those bastards wouldn’t even listen." His gaze hardened.
"Their commander directly ordered an attack." He explained about the conflict.
The Varkesh had fortified themselves around the basin beforehand.
Their archers shot arrows from above the roots.
The Lacerian forces were initially pushed back.
But Averian personally entered the battle, defeated two Varkesh commanders, broke their defensive line, and the tide slowly turned.
"We were winning." He said and added.
"A few of them had even dropped their weapons.
That’s when that creature appeared."
"Looked like me?" Lian asked.
"Yeah." Averian nodded.
"Was it a man or a woman?"
"A woman."
Lian’s guess moved one step closer to certainty.
"Appearance?"
Averian thought for a few moments.
"She was tall, had fair skin, silver hair, and completely black eyes."
"She wore light dark armor, built for speed, the best armor I had ever seen, a masterpiece in every way." Then he said more slowly.
"There was no emotion on her face.
No anger, no excitement, and not even hatred." He looked at his new hands.
"As if cutting off my hands was no different for her than cutting a dry branch."
"Her weapon was a sword?" Lian also wanted to use the last piece of the puzzle.
"Maybe it was a sword, but I didn’t even see it clearly." He placed his hand on the previous spot of the wound.
"The first strike cut off my right hand, the second cut off my left hand." His voice became heavy for a moment.
"She could have killed me, but she didn’t.
She just said we no longer have the right to approach the water."
Averian said the strange woman then stepped aside.
And the Varkesh allowed the remaining soldiers to pick him up and return to the tribe.
It was complete humiliation.
Not just defeat, but a major warning.
Lian let out a quiet sigh.
Silver hair, black eyes, an emotionless face, and speed that Averian could not even follow.
He was almost sure.
Maybe there were other details, but the chance that another person with all these characteristics existed among the Awakened ones was very low.
"I want to see the Varkesh." He then added.
"But it’s dangerous." Nemi immediately raised her head.
Her worry was real.
Whatever that creature was, it was someone who had defeated her father in a few moves.
What Lian also face deadly danger?

chapters.title: Chapter 224: Another Otherworldly ? III
paragraphs: Lian looked at her. This little girl had reached a point where she was worried about him. It seemed he had become more popular among the ladies than he had thought.
But anyway, he hoped this attachment wouldn’t cause problems later, because he wasn’t going to stay here for a long time.
"You saw my power, didn’t you?" He then said with a smile on his face.
Nemi pressed her lips together and said nothing.
She had seen Lian’s power. She could say without a doubt that he was one of the most powerful creatures she had ever seen, stronger than anyone else in their tribe.
But that didn’t make her fear completely disappear. The fear and worry she felt wasn’t her fault, it was an unconscious and emotional reaction.
"Do you know that woman?" Averian thought for a few moments.
"Maybe."
"And you want to fight her?"
"First I want to see her." Lian said. He had a guess about who that female awakened one could be.
But it was only a guess, and he first needed to confirm it. If it was exactly the person he was thinking of, there would be no need for any conflict or battle.
But if it was someone else... everything could go differently.
Averian looked at his face. The man who had saved his family twice.
But at the same time, someone who showed no fear of facing a creature like that woman. In the end, he nodded.
"Agreed." This was also not a bad thing for them. They really needed that river. If they lost it, all the tribe’s people would die of thirst.
He knew that this Otherworldly had already helped them more than enough and had no claim on them... but he hoped that he would help them one more time and save their tribe from extinction.
"If possible, we’ll leave tomorrow." Lian said, and then turned his gaze among the family members.
"I’ll leave you alone for now." He left the medical center. He could see that this family wanted some time alone.
Behind him, Nemi hugged her father again. This time, Averian was able to wrap his arms around his child.
The next morning, a military caravan was prepared in front of the Lacerians’ gate.
The tribe leader, completely healthy and with new armor, was sitting on his riding beast. One of the experienced elders was with him.
About thirty soldiers, a few archers, two healers, and a number of armored beasts made up the group.
One was also waiting near the gate. Lian sat on its broad back.
"I’m coming too." Ravian approached the group with light armor and a spear.
"No." Averian didn’t even think for a moment.
"But—" his son frowned and wanted to object.
"Yesterday you said you wanted to become stronger." His father said, his gaze calm but firm.
"The first step is to learn that not every battle belongs to you." He was completely determined not to take his stubborn son with them.
"They will—" Ravian clenched his teeth.
"And I am healthy now." Averian continued.
"You stay here."
Ravian wanted to object again, but this time he stopped. Maybe the conversation yesterday with Lian had changed something inside him.
Finally, he nodded.
"Okay."
Lian looked down at him from above One for a brief moment. Ravian returned his gaze.
The caravan moved.
The path to the Silvervein Basin took a few hours.
Averian kept his riding beast close to One. For a while, both were silent.
The tribe leader was looking at this giant ant with admiration before saying anything. The ability to tame such a thing... truly, this man was on a different level compared to them.

He thought to himself what if their tribe had such ants in their service... they could probably easily become the strongest tribe, right? They could go anywhere they wanted and never have a shortage of food...
"Do you really know that woman?" he finally asked.
"I said maybe before, it could be someone else too." Lian answered.
"If it is the person you think, is she a friend?" Averian said.
"The definition of friend depends." Lian thought for a moment.
Averian gave him a brief look. He didn’t seem satisfied with the answer and asked a more direct question.
"Which of you is stronger?"
"Me." Lian laughed. The answer was without pause and with complete confidence.
Even if fighting that girl was not easy, Lian had no reason to show hesitation in front of Averian.
The tribe leader said nothing for a few moments. This confidence was hopeful on one hand, and on the other hand, a little worrying.
He had seen the power of that one with his own eyes, but he had only heard about the power of this one from his children... but if what he had heard was true... then this man was definitely stronger.
The Silvervein Basin was located among several giant roots. In the past, the basin must have been very large and shining.
The silver deposits on the walls showed that the water level had once been several meters higher, but now only a shallow layer remained in the central part.
A narrow river entered the basin from a height. Several artificial channels directed the water toward the territory of the two tribes.
The Varkesh had blocked most of the path with stones, wood, and temporary dams to divert the water flow toward themselves.
A few Varkesh soldiers were guarding around the basin. Upon seeing the Lacerian caravan, they raised their weapons.
But when they saw Averian, their expressions changed, and one of them stepped back a few steps.
"Impossible..."
They had imagined that Averian was either dead or permanently crippled.
But now, the Lacerian leader was standing in front of them, healthy, armored, and with both hands.
Averian moved his riding beast forward and said with a calm but contemptuous tone.
"Go bring your cowardly, greedy leader."
A few Varkesh showed their teeth in anger, but fear and shock prevented an attack. The person who was supposed to be dead was alive in front of them.
Besides, they knew they had no chance against their enemies’ army, so the best decision was to retreat.
Three of them ran toward the tribe’s path.
"How long will it take?" Lian asked from atop One.
"Not long." Averian said and pointed toward the eastern path.
"Their tribe is built near the basin."
About half an hour later, the sound of war drums was heard, then the sound of many feet striking. The Varkesh force appeared from among the roots.
They were from the same race as the Lacerians, but their differences were clear.
Their scales were dark red, brown, or copper. They had shorter and thicker antennae, and their tails were more muscular.
Heavy armor made of monster shells and stone pieces was tied on their bodies.
Some had white or black markings on their face and chest. Their weapons were also larger.
Heavy axes, bone maces, thick spears, and their riding beasts were shorter than the Lacerians’ beasts, but had wide and very muscular bodies.
In the center of the force, their leader was moving.
Kharvek.
A very burly man with dark red scales. One of his antennae was broken from the middle. A robe made of blue monster skin was draped over his shoulder.
When he saw Averian, he pulled his beast’s reins, his eyes widened.
His gaze fixed on Averian’s hands.
Healthy, without wounds. And then he noticed One and Lian sitting on its back.
His shock multiplied several times.
"Another Otherworldly?" His face twisted in disbelief and anger.

chapters.title: Chapter 225: Another Otherworldly? ( Final )
paragraphs: "How do you also have one?" His words removed all doubts, although there was no doubt anyway.
There really was an Otherworldly among them and in their tribe. They probably considered him their hero, protector, or their weapon.
Lian got down from One and calmly walked forward between the two groups. The Varkesh soldiers readied their weapons.
He looked directly at Kharvek.
"Before I kill all of you, go tell the one who helped you yesterday to come here."
For a moment, there was silence. Then Kharvek laughed, a loud and contemptuous laugh.
"Who do you think you are?" He pointed at the soldiers behind him.
"Do you think you’re as strong as our hero?" Arrogance was completely visible in his eyes.
He did not seem worried at all. It was true that their enemy tribe had also found an Otherworldly like them, but so what?
He had no doubt that their hero was completely unique! And no one was even close to her, even if this one was from the same species as their hero, that did not mean he had power equal to their hero.
Their hero had been able to single-handedly subdue and defeat their entire tribe.
For this reason, he was not worried at all...
Their hero is a woman.
Lian only gave him an indifferent look, and Kharvek raised his hand.
"Kill him."
The soldiers moved. Spears came forward, axes were raised, bows were drawn, but before the first strike could be completed, Lian disappeared.
The first soldier only felt something hit his chest.
Lian’s fist shattered the stone armor. The force passed through the shell and crushed the ribcage bones.
The soldier’s body was lifted off the ground and crashed into the row behind him.
Lian passed by the second soldier. The edge of his palm hit his neck, the sound of breaking bones was heard.
The body did not even have time to react before falling.
The third soldier only saw a shadow, then Lian’s knee hit his stomach, and the armor bent from the middle.
The creature was thrown several meters into the air. From the Varkesh’s view, what happened was not a battle.
It was people disappearing. Every time the sound of an impact was heard, one person would fall to the ground.
A spear was still in the air when its owner was no longer standing. An axe was raised, but the arm broke from the joint before it could come down.
Blood splashed on the ground, armors cracked, and bodies fell one after another.
One of the archers wanted to release an arrow, Lian appeared in front of him, and his fingers landed on the string.
He pulled the bow from his hand and with the same wood, shattered his jaw. Two soldiers attacked from both sides, and Lian ducked.
The spears passed over his head. He struck their sides with two simultaneous punches, and both bodies were thrown in opposite directions.
Averian and the Lacerian soldiers watched motionlessly.

They had heard Ravian’s story, but hearing was different from seeing. Lian, without a massive skill, without a weapon, and without any apparent effort, had shattered the Varkesh force in a few seconds.
Was this really a power that a two-legged creature could achieve?
Their eyes sparkled with excitement because they realized that they also now had a hero and savior!
In less than ten seconds, most of the soldiers were on the ground.
Some dead, some with broken bones, some unconscious.
Lian deliberately kept four people unharmed. Not out of mercy, but to deliver a message. Kharvek had just come out of his shock when a shadow appeared in front of him.
He wanted to raise his axe, but Lian grabbed his wrist. He squeezed, and the bone broke.
Kharvek screamed.
But Lian struck his foot behind his knee. The Varkesh leader fell to the ground, and before he understood what had happened, his face was in the dirt.
Lian’s foot was placed next to his skull. A little pressure was applied, and the shell beside Kharvek’s head cracked.
"You thought I was joking with you?" He then said calmly and coldly.
Kharvek’s pride crumbled at that moment. His breath was broken, and his eyes were darting around with pure terror.
His soldiers were on the ground. The force he had brought to threaten the Lacerians was destroyed in a few seconds.
He couldn’t even understand what had happened at all... just a few seconds ago he was sitting on his riding beast, but now?
He, the leader of the great Varkesh tribe, was on the ground and being dragged in the dirt under the foot of an outsider! How could such a thing be possible?
How had all his soldiers been killed in a few seconds?
Are all the damn Otherworldlies this powerful? Why are all of them this powerful? This is the second time he is experiencing exactly this kind of humiliation!
Lian increased the pressure of his foot a little more, and Kharvek screamed.
"Go!"
The four remaining soldiers were still in shock and didn’t move until Kharvek shouted with a louder voice.
"Go bring the hero!"
His breath trembled.
"Right now!"
Three soldiers quickly ran toward the tribe. The fourth was wounded and couldn’t go with them.
Lian didn’t remove his foot from Kharvek’s head. A heavy silence formed around the basin.
A bone-chilling cold and fear had taken over Averian and his tribe’s soldiers. Until now, they had thought their tribe’s guest was a calm and ordinary person.
But what they had just seen was terrifying, so much so that they might even have nightmares about it...
A bone-chilling cold ran down their spines... just hearing Lian’s cold and soulless voice made their hair stand on end!
The shallow water of the Silvervein was flowing calmly.
The wounded Varkesh didn’t dare to move. The Lacerian soldiers were still trying to process what they had seen.
After a while, the sound of footsteps was heard from the eastern path.
Not the sound of a large army, not drums, but only a few soldiers moving with distance from a person in the center.
The woman came out from among the roots. She was tall, and her beauty was cold and almost unnatural.
Her long silver hair was flowing over her shoulders and back, moving in the wind with her calm movement.
Her eyes were completely black, deep, and without any human warmth.
She wore light, tight, dark armor, built for speed and freedom of movement, not heavy defense.
A thin sword was at her waist. Her face was completely devoid of emotion.
No concern for the Varkesh corpses, no anger at seeing Kharvek under Lian’s foot, and no surprise at the massacre that had occurred before her.
She calmly came forward.
But when her black gaze fixed on Lian, for the first time, a small change occurred on her face. Her eyes sparkled slightly with joy.
Her eyebrow rose very subtly. It wasn’t fear, it wasn’t anger, but actually something like interest or excitement that had briefly emerged from behind that emotionless face.
Lian still kept his foot on Kharvek’s head, and then with a calm smile, he looked at the silver-haired woman.
"I’m glad to see you again so soon, Seris."

The creature was thrown several meters into the air.
From the Varkesh’s view, what happened was not a battle.
It was people disappearing.
Every time the sound of an impact was heard, one person would fall to the ground.
A spear was still in the air when its owner was no longer standing.
An axe was raised, but the arm broke from the joint before it could come down.
Blood splashed on the ground, armors cracked, and bodies fell one after another.
One of the archers wanted to release an arrow, Lian appeared in front of him, and his fingers landed on the string.
He pulled the bow from his hand and with the same wood, shattered his jaw.
Two soldiers attacked from both sides, and Lian ducked.
The spears passed over his head.
He struck their sides with two simultaneous punches, and both bodies were thrown in opposite directions.
Averian and the Lacerian soldiers watched motionlessly.
They had heard Ravian’s story, but hearing was different from seeing.
Lian, without a massive skill, without a weapon, and without any apparent effort, had shattered the Varkesh force in a few seconds.
Was this really a power that a two-legged creature could achieve?
Their eyes sparkled with excitement because they realized that they also now had a hero and savior!
In less than ten seconds, most of the soldiers were on the ground.
Some dead, some with broken bones, some unconscious.
Lian deliberately kept four people unharmed.
Not out of mercy, but to deliver a message.
Kharvek had just come out of his shock when a shadow appeared in front of him.
He wanted to raise his axe, but Lian grabbed his wrist.
He squeezed, and the bone broke.
Kharvek screamed.
But Lian struck his foot behind his knee.
The Varkesh leader fell to the ground, and before he understood what had happened, his face was in the dirt.
Lian’s foot was placed next to his skull.
A little pressure was applied, and the shell beside Kharvek’s head cracked.
"You thought I was joking with you?" He then said calmly and coldly.
Kharvek’s pride crumbled at that moment.
His breath was broken, and his eyes were darting around with pure terror.
His soldiers were on the ground.
The force he had brought to threaten the Lacerians was destroyed in a few seconds.
He couldn’t even understand what had happened at all... just a few seconds ago he was sitting on his riding beast, but now?
He, the leader of the great Varkesh tribe, was on the ground and being dragged in the dirt under the foot of an outsider!
How could such a thing be possible?
How had all his soldiers been killed in a few seconds?
Are all the damn Otherworldlies this powerful?
Why are all of them this powerful?
This is the second time he is experiencing exactly this kind of humiliation!
Lian increased the pressure of his foot a little more, and Kharvek screamed.
"Go!"
The four remaining soldiers were still in shock and didn’t move until Kharvek shouted with a louder voice.
"Go bring the hero!"
His breath trembled.
"Right now!"
Three soldiers quickly ran toward the tribe.
The fourth was wounded and couldn’t go with them.
Lian didn’t remove his foot from Kharvek’s head.
A heavy silence formed around the basin.
A bone-chilling cold and fear had taken over Averian and his tribe’s soldiers.
Until now, they had thought their tribe’s guest was a calm and ordinary person.
But what they had just seen was terrifying, so much so that they might even have nightmares about it...
A bone-chilling cold ran down their spines... just hearing Lian’s cold and soulless voice made their hair stand on end!
The shallow water of the Silvervein was flowing calmly.
The wounded Varkesh didn’t dare to move.
The Lacerian soldiers were still trying to process what they had seen.
After a while, the sound of footsteps was heard from the eastern path.
Not the sound of a large army, not drums, but only a few soldiers moving with distance from a person in the center.
The woman came out from among the roots.
She was tall, and her beauty was cold and almost unnatural.
Her long silver hair was flowing over her shoulders and back, moving in the wind with her calm movement.
Her eyes were completely black, deep, and without any human warmth.
She wore light, tight, dark armor, built for speed and freedom of movement, not heavy defense.
A thin sword was at her waist.
Her face was completely devoid of emotion.
No concern for the Varkesh corpses, no anger at seeing Kharvek under Lian’s foot, and no surprise at the massacre that had occurred before her.
She calmly came forward.
But when her black gaze fixed on Lian, for the first time, a small change occurred on her face.
Her eyes sparkled slightly with joy.
Her eyebrow rose very subtly.
It wasn’t fear, it wasn’t anger, but actually something like interest or excitement that had briefly emerged from behind that emotionless face.
Lian still kept his foot on Kharvek’s head, and then with a calm smile, he looked at the silver-haired woman.
"I’m glad to see you again so soon, Seris."

chapters.title: Chapter 226: Reunion With A Friend
paragraphs: "I’m glad to see you again so soon, Seris." Lian looked at the girl who had arrived and a smile appeared on his face.
That’s right, it was no one but Seris... and his guess was completely correct.
Seris stopped a few meters away from Lian.
Her long silver hair moved gently on her shoulders with the breeze passing over the Silvervein Basin.
Her completely black eyes remained fixed on Lian’s face for a few moments.
On the surface, no particular change appeared on her face, that same cold face and that same deep calmness, that same emotionless look that even a field full of corpses and blood could not disturb.
But Lian knew her well.
He saw the very slight rise of one of her eyebrows and recognized the brief pause that formed before her next move.
Seris had not expected to see him here.
Just as Lian had not expected to encounter her in this world.
His foot was still on the side of Kharvek’s skull.
The Varkesh leader was lying face down on the soil, and every time he breathed, blood would drip from the corner of his mouth onto the ground.
Around them, dozens of Varkesh soldiers lay dead or with broken bones on the silver deposits of the basin.
Nevertheless, the atmosphere between Lian and Seris did not look like a battlefield, it looked more like a meeting between two old acquaintances.
Two people who had last stood facing each other in the Vorhelm clan’s territory, between the stone walls and the fighting arenas.
"It’s been a while." Lian said with a calmer tone.
"It has." Seris answered after a short pause.
Her voice, like always, was short and calm.
There was no obvious warmth in it, nor any reluctance, just a direct sentence.
But that short answer was enough for Lian to understand that Seris was not unhappy to see him.
Behind Lian, Averian and the Lacerian soldiers were looking at the two of them in disbelief.
For them, Seris was the same creature who had defeated their leader in less than a few moves and had cut off both his hands.
Someone whose blade’s speed even Averian had not been able to fully see.
But now Lian was talking to her so casually as if none of them were standing on a ground covered with corpses.
The relationship between Lian and Seris had never been like ordinary friendships.
They did not sit next to each other for hours to talk about life, family, or their worries.
Neither of them had any interest in parties, social relationships, or the entertainment that most of their peers followed.
What had brought the two of them close was not conversation.
It was battle, growth, and power.
Seris considered most people her age either weak or boring.
Those who lost their motivation after a few defeats, those whose only goal was to gain their family’s attention or achieve a comfortable position.
But Lian was different.
He was the only person her age who had truly been able to defeat her.
Not with luck, not with help from others, but with power and skill that had forced her to reconsider her own limits.
From that time, Lian had found a different place in that girl’s mind, something between rival, friend, and a goal she did not want to fall behind.
Even if Seris never put a name to that feeling.
"When did you enter the Special Area? I didn’t see you enter at the same time as us." Lian asked.
"I entered a few hours after you all did." Seris answered.
Lian nodded.
This answer clarified part of what he had in mind.
So the Awakened ones’ entry had not been simultaneous, the transfer had probably happened in several waves or stages.
He had expected Seris to enter the Special Area from the beginning, someone like her was unlikely to miss a chance to fight, grow, and obtain unknown resources.
But the more important question still remained.
Lian gave a brief look at Kharvek and the Varkesh soldiers and then asked.
"But why with these?"
Seris also turned her gaze to the Varkesh for a moment.
"I appeared near their tribe." She paused briefly.
"They attacked me, I beat all of them, and they decided to submit to me."
For a moment, even Lian said nothing.
The way Seris described it was so simple that it was as if she was talking about crossing a river or finding a place to sleep.
Behind Lian, a few Lacerian soldiers could not hide their reaction.
Their gazes toward Kharvek changed, fear and hatred were replaced by contempt.
So the Varkesh had not made an honorable pact with Seris, they had not chosen her as a hero, they had not even offered her anything.
They had attacked an unknown girl, all of them got beaten, and then they decided to introduce themselves as her subordinates to save their lives.
Averian also gave a very faint smile.
Kharvek, who was still under Lian’s foot, clenched his teeth.
The scales around his neck darkened, his face twisted in anger, humiliation, and shame, but he still did not dare to say anything.
"I see, you did a good thing." Lian said calmly and then a faint smile appeared on his face.
For him, Seris’s behavior was not strange.
If the Varkesh had attacked first, then being defeated and becoming subordinates was a natural outcome.
He saw no reason to scold her for it.
However, his gaze became a little more serious.
"But I would appreciate it if you didn’t attack my friends."
For the first time, Seris took her gaze off Lian.
Her black eyes moved over Averian and the Lacerian warriors.
Her gaze was brief, cold, and evaluating.
The tribe leader unconsciously moved the fingers of his new hands.
The memory of both his arms being severed was still so fresh that he could not ignore Seris’s presence.
"I didn’t know they were your friends."
"It’s fine."
Seris was silent for a few moments.
It seemed she was examining something.
Maybe she was trying to understand whether Lian was upset about what had happened or not, and finally, with a completely serious tone, she asked.
"Do you want me to kill all these lizards?"
Absolute silence formed.
A few Lacerian soldiers froze, even the wounded Varkesh who did not dare to move looked at Seris in terror.
She was not joking, there was no sign of mockery on her face.
From Seris’s view, if these people had hurt Lian’s friends and Lian was upset, the simplest way to make up for it was to completely eliminate them.
"No. It’s not necessary." Lian laughed briefly.
The girl also slightly shook her head without objecting, as if the matter was resolved at that same moment.
Then the young Vorhelm took his foot off the side of Kharvek’s head.
The Varkesh leader coughed heavily and pulled himself back a few centimeters.
He placed his broken hand under his body and tried to raise his head, but still did not dare to stand.
"We came for the river." Lian said to Seris.
"I don’t care, they asked me to help them. I did." She gave a brief look at the Varkesh.
Then she looked at Lian again.
"If you want it, it’s yours."
Averian showed no reaction for a moment.
A matter that could have turned into a long and bloody war between two tribes had been resolved in less than a few sentences.
No negotiation had taken place, and not even a contract had been written, no one had even been forced to make a concession.
Seris had only said the water didn’t matter to her.
And that was enough.
Just that? A matter that had been such a big problem and a life-and-death issue for them was solved so easily?
And in fact, do creatures who don’t even belong to this world decide the fate of two tribes?
How could such a thing even make sense?
"This is the river you wanted." Lian turned his head toward the tribe leader.
Averian opened his mouth, but before he could say anything, Kharvek suddenly shouted.
"No!" His voice was harsh, broken, and mixed with madness, and all eyes turned to him.
Kharvek struggled to stand on one knee, his face was bloody, and one arm hung lifelessly by his side.
"This river is ours!" He took a heavy breath.
"We won’t give it!" He grabbed one of the fallen axes on the ground with his healthy hand.
Averian frowned, a few Lacerian soldiers raised their weapons.
Kharvek wanted to step toward him, but before his foot could fully touch the ground, Seris moved.
No one saw her sword coming out of its sheath, only a very thin silver line formed in the air.
For a fraction of a second, light broke on the edge of the blade, and then everything was over... Kharvek’s head separated from his neck.
It spun in the air for a few moments, and his eyes were still open, with anger frozen in them.
The head fell with a muffled sound on the silver deposits next to the water, and the headless body took one more step.
The axe fell from his hand, then he fell on his knee and collapsed to the side.
Warm blood splashed from the severed neck onto the soil and silver rocks.
The two tribes fell into complete silence.
Even the sound of the weak water current seemed louder for a moment.
Seris shook her blade once, the blood separated from the sword in a thin line, and she calmly returned the sword to its sheath.
"He was making too much noise." She then said with that same emotionless face.
The Varkesh’s terror was complete, they unconsciously lowered themselves.
But even the Lacerian soldiers stepped back from Seris, now they understood better why Averian had not been able to resist her.
For Seris, killing the leader of a tribe was no more important than silencing an annoying sound...

chapters.title: Chapter 227: Unwanted Guest I
paragraphs: Lian looked at Kharvek’s headless body, then turned his gaze to Seris, and this time his smile became more genuine.
"You might not believe it, but I missed you." He then laughed briefly.
This sentence, more than the field full of corpses, threats, or even anything, managed to surprise Seris.
For a moment, she remained completely still, a very faint color formed on her pale cheeks.
So faint that probably no one except Lian would notice it. Her black eyes shifted away from him for a moment.
That girl, who had an immediate response to attacks, threats, and even death, this time did not know what to say.
A few seconds passed, and finally, she answered briefly.
"Your weclome."
Lian laughed. It hadn’t been long since he had wished Seris was also here.
Crossing the Forest of Giants would be much easier with her presence.
Massive monsters, unknown areas, dangerous colonies, and paths that were deadly for one person would be less of a threat against their combined power.
And now Seris was really here.
But why? Wherever Lian went, sooner or later she would appear on the same path.
The first time he entered the Ruined Realm, in the Vorhelm clan, in the fighting arenas, and now in a world that neither of them had even heard of a few days ago.
Was this just coincidence? Or was some unknown force repeatedly pulling them toward each other?
Fate? Destiny? Or maybe something in their Talents, Bloodlines, or growth paths caused them to meet at important points?
Lian had no answer, but the number of these encounters was too many to seem completely normal.
Seris took her gaze away from him and gave it to the few surviving Varkesh soldiers.
At that same moment, their bodies tensed, and she addressed them.
"I killed your leader. Go back and tell them that the leader’s eldest daughter is now the leader."
A few Varkesh looked at each other. The name of Kharvek’s eldest daughter, Veyra, was known to them.
A powerful warrior, ambitious, and among Kharvek’s children, the only one who could replace him without the tribe completely collapsing.
No one dared to oppose Seris’s decision. Three of the healthier soldiers left Kharvek and quickly ran toward the tribe’s path. One of the wounded also followed them limping.
Seris looked at Lian again.
"So. Our work here is done." She paused briefly and added.
"Let’s go?"
"You want to come with me?" Lian said with a more sarcastic tone.
"Are we going to do anything else?" The girl answered very casually.
Lian looked around. Kharvek was dead, the Varkesh were defeated, and the river was practically under Averian’s control.
"I guess not."
Before moving, the tribe leader left part of his forces beside the Silvervein Basin.
Ten soldiers were chosen to guard the basin.

Two archers were stationed on the tall roots around to monitor the paths leading to the area, and another group removed the stone and wooden barriers that the Varkesh had built inside the Lacerians’ channel.
The logs were pulled out one after another, and the large stones were moved with ropes and the strength of several soldiers.
When the last obstacle was removed, the water that had been gathered behind the temporary dam suddenly rushed forward.
A current of water poured into the dry channel. At first it was narrow, then it became deeper.
The water moved over the shiny deposits and continued its path toward the Lacerians’ territory.
Averian watched the flow for a few moments and then said.
"No one enters Varkesh territory without my command."
"Could they attack after Kharvek’s death?" one of the commanders asked.
"Maybe." Averian answered.
His gaze stayed on Seris for a moment.
"But for now, they are more worried about their new leader than about war." He preferred that Kharvek’s death would not start a full-scale war.
The water had returned, that was enough for today. Now he was no longer worried about his tribe for a while, and as much as possible, he preferred to avoid further tension and war.
With that bastard’s death, his tribe would certainly become weaker. This was an opportunity for him and his tribe to attack the Varkesh and absorb them.

But even if they became weaker, defeating them would still cause damage, and they would also suffer many casualties. He did not want to ask Lian for help either, because that would be the height of shamelessness.
Even now, their tribe owed too much to this outsider, and he did not want this debt to grow more and more.
So it was just better to stay away from war...
The caravan returned to the tribe.
Seris also sat behind Lian on One.
And One moved at a calm speed alongside the caravan, passing over roots, slopes, and tall moss without the slightest sign of fatigue.
When they approached the Lacerians’ territory, the sound of bells was heard from a distance.
This time, not alarm bells, but victory bells. The guards on the wall saw the water flowing in the channel.
And their shouts echoed among the roots.
"Silvervein has returned!"
"The water is flowing again!"
The news spread through the entire tribe faster than the caravan. People came out of their houses, and children ran beside the channel.
Families brought containers, water skins, and skin-covered baskets. After days, water was flowing again through the tribe’s main path.
An elderly woman knelt beside the channel and dipped her hands into the water. When she raised them, tears fell from her eyes.
Another man filled a container and raised it above his head. A shout of joy rose among the crowd.
The immediate fear of thirst was gone. The crisis was not completely solved. The cause of the waterways drying up was still unknown.
But at least for a while, the Lacerians had water again.
The people’s joy increased for a few moments upon the caravan’s arrival.
But then the gazes fixed on Seris. The noise quieted down. The people had not expected to see another Otherworldly.
Seris attracted even more attention among the Lacerians than Lian.
Long silver hair, pale skin, and light dark armor that followed the lines of her body and was built for speed.
Her beauty was cold and unusual.
But Averian’s story was still fresh. Everyone knew who had cut off their leader’s hands.
As a result, the people’s curiosity was mixed with a deeper fear.
Ravian was standing near the main square. When he saw Seris, he paused for a moment.
The unusual beauty of the silver-haired girl surprised even him, but his surprise did not last more than a second.
His gaze fell on the thin sword at Seris’s waist, and then the image of his father with both hands severed came alive again in his mind.
His fingers unconsciously tightened around the spear’s handle.
Sera also stared at Seris with a cold gaze.
Nemi stayed half a step behind her sister. None of the three were happy about her presence.
Even if Averian was now completely healthy, the memory of the blood, burnt cloths, and his unconscious body would not fade from their minds so soon.
Seris noticed their gazes, but she did not care the slightest. She did not offer an explanation, nor did she apologize, nor did she even try to soften her expression.
From her view, Averian had stood against her in battle and had lost.
That was it.
But others didn’t see it that way...

Massive monsters, unknown areas, dangerous colonies, and paths that were deadly for one person would be less of a threat against their combined power.
And now Seris was really here.
But why?
Wherever Lian went, sooner or later she would appear on the same path.
The first time he entered the Ruined Realm, in the Vorhelm clan, in the fighting arenas, and now in a world that neither of them had even heard of a few days ago.
Was this just coincidence?
Or was some unknown force repeatedly pulling them toward each other?
Fate?
Destiny?
Or maybe something in their Talents, Bloodlines, or growth paths caused them to meet at important points?
Lian had no answer, but the number of these encounters was too many to seem completely normal.
Seris took her gaze away from him and gave it to the few surviving Varkesh soldiers.
At that same moment, their bodies tensed, and she addressed them.
"I killed your leader.
Go back and tell them that the leader’s eldest daughter is now the leader."
A few Varkesh looked at each other.
The name of Kharvek’s eldest daughter, Veyra, was known to them.
A powerful warrior, ambitious, and among Kharvek’s children, the only one who could replace him without the tribe completely collapsing.
No one dared to oppose Seris’s decision.
Three of the healthier soldiers left Kharvek and quickly ran toward the tribe’s path.
One of the wounded also followed them limping.
Seris looked at Lian again.
"So.
Our work here is done." She paused briefly and added.
"Let’s go?"
"You want to come with me?" Lian said with a more sarcastic tone.
"Are we going to do anything else?" The girl answered very casually.
Lian looked around.
Kharvek was dead, the Varkesh were defeated, and the river was practically under Averian’s control.
"I guess not."
Before moving, the tribe leader left part of his forces beside the Silvervein Basin.
Ten soldiers were chosen to guard the basin.

Two archers were stationed on the tall roots around to monitor the paths leading to the area, and another group removed the stone and wooden barriers that the Varkesh had built inside the Lacerians’ channel.
The logs were pulled out one after another, and the large stones were moved with ropes and the strength of several soldiers.
When the last obstacle was removed, the water that had been gathered behind the temporary dam suddenly rushed forward.
A current of water poured into the dry channel.
At first it was narrow, then it became deeper.
The water moved over the shiny deposits and continued its path toward the Lacerians’ territory.
Averian watched the flow for a few moments and then said.
"No one enters Varkesh territory without my command."
"Could they attack after Kharvek’s death?" one of the commanders asked.
"Maybe." Averian answered.
His gaze stayed on Seris for a moment.
"But for now, they are more worried about their new leader than about war." He preferred that Kharvek’s death would not start a full-scale war.
The water had returned, that was enough for today.
Now he was no longer worried about his tribe for a while, and as much as possible, he preferred to avoid further tension and war.
With that bastard’s death, his tribe would certainly become weaker.
This was an opportunity for him and his tribe to attack the Varkesh and absorb them.
But even if they became weaker, defeating them would still cause damage, and they would also suffer many casualties.
He did not want to ask Lian for help either, because that would be the height of shamelessness.
Even now, their tribe owed too much to this outsider, and he did not want this debt to grow more and more.
So it was just better to stay away from war...
The caravan returned to the tribe.
Seris also sat behind Lian on One.
And One moved at a calm speed alongside the caravan, passing over roots, slopes, and tall moss without the slightest sign of fatigue.
When they approached the Lacerians’ territory, the sound of bells was heard from a distance.
This time, not alarm bells, but victory bells.
The guards on the wall saw the water flowing in the channel.
And their shouts echoed among the roots.
"Silvervein has returned!"
"The water is flowing again!"
The news spread through the entire tribe faster than the caravan.
People came out of their houses, and children ran beside the channel.
Families brought containers, water skins, and skin-covered baskets.
After days, water was flowing again through the tribe’s main path.
An elderly woman knelt beside the channel and dipped her hands into the water.
When she raised them, tears fell from her eyes.
Another man filled a container and raised it above his head.
A shout of joy rose among the crowd.
The immediate fear of thirst was gone.
The crisis was not completely solved.
The cause of the waterways drying up was still unknown.
But at least for a while, the Lacerians had water again.
The people’s joy increased for a few moments upon the caravan’s arrival.
But then the gazes fixed on Seris.
The noise quieted down.
The people had not expected to see another Otherworldly.
Seris attracted even more attention among the Lacerians than Lian.
Long silver hair, pale skin, and light dark armor that followed the lines of her body and was built for speed.
Her beauty was cold and unusual.
But Averian’s story was still fresh.
Everyone knew who had cut off their leader’s hands.
As a result, the people’s curiosity was mixed with a deeper fear.
Ravian was standing near the main square.
When he saw Seris, he paused for a moment.
The unusual beauty of the silver-haired girl surprised even him, but his surprise did not last more than a second.
His gaze fell on the thin sword at Seris’s waist, and then the image of his father with both hands severed came alive again in his mind.
His fingers unconsciously tightened around the spear’s handle.
Sera also stared at Seris with a cold gaze.
Nemi stayed half a step behind her sister.
None of the three were happy about her presence.
Even if Averian was now completely healthy, the memory of the blood, burnt cloths, and his unconscious body would not fade from their minds so soon.
Seris noticed their gazes, but she did not care the slightest.
She did not offer an explanation, nor did she apologize, nor did she even try to soften her expression.
From her view, Averian had stood against her in battle and had lost.
That was it.
But others didn’t see it that way...

chapters.title: Chapter 228: Unwanted Guest II
paragraphs: Lian sensed the tension, but decided to ignore it. Forcing Seris to apologize was almost impossible.
Forcing Ravian and his sisters to accept her was also pointless. Time might solve the problem, or at least make her presence more tolerable for them.
Besides, it wasn’t like the hostility had anything to do with him or could have any effect, and as far as he knew, Seris was not the type of person who cared the slightest about such matters.
"Why is this creature here?" Ravian asked with a defensive tone.
Seris gave him a brief look, but before she could say anything, Averian answered.
"She is Mr. Lian’s friend." His way of addressing had changed. He no longer only said Lian’s name.
After saving his children, healing his hands, and restoring the water, the tribe leader’s respect had deepened, and he continued.
"She will stay here for a while."
Ravian first looked at his father, then at Lian. He opened his mouth, as if he wanted to object.
"Well... then nothing." But in the end, he only said that.
Lian gave a very faint smile. This boy’s trust in him was ultimately greater than his anger toward Seris.
Averian and the elders went to the council house to assess the water situation, Kharvek’s death, and the future relationship with the Varkesh.
Lian also led Seris away from the crowded square. They sat on a high platform in a quieter part of the tribe, where a large part of the Forest of Giants could be seen.
The roots stretched like natural walls in all directions. Green mist moved among the giant trunks, and creatures could be seen crawling on the branches in the distance.
The sound of an unknown roar came from deep within the forest.
"This forest is too gigantic." Seris watched the view for a while and then said.
"I agree." Lian answered, pointing at a root so large that whole houses of the tribe were built inside it.
"According to what I’ve understood, the Forest of Giants is more of a wild area."
The girl gave her gaze to him, and he continued.
"It has many monsters and resources, but I haven’t found any special opportunity worth staying long for."
"The other two forests?"
"Emberroot and Glassthorn."
"Emberroot is full of fire and heat-related resources. Some reports even say the forest itself awakens periodically, plus they have a kingdom"
Based on the reports he had read, among all three forests, Emberroot could have the most value and opportunities for the awakened ones.
The civilization that existed there was simply the largest known civilization in this world, and unlike the other two forests that had a tribal system, they had a kingdom system.
Of course, not in the sense that there was no trace of a tribal system among them... more precisely, it was like this: several tribes had come together to form a kingdom.
Of course, the fact that the civilization was more advanced could also mean greater danger.
And unfortunately, going there is not easy because at least from where they are, there is no direct way.
"Glassthorn?"
"Colder and more dangerous." Lian explained.
"Crystal trees, constant mist, invisible thorns, and monsters that use reflections." He paused.
"But there’s probably a crystalline city there. Also, its path to the Forgotten Tree seems closer."
"Better opportunities." Seris added.
"Probably."
"The lizards said there is no exit path from this forest." That girl also mentioned another point she had heard.
She had naturally forced the Varkesh to provide any information they had. She was also looking for a way out of this forest.
This forest was too dangerous even for her, but she had not been able to find a way. All paths ended in death.
Even though she loved battle, she was not crazy enough to dig her own grave with her own hands.
"That’s almost correct." Lian answered.
"But there is one way."
"Where?"
"It’s called the Giants’ Graveyard, there’s a valley there that connects to Glassthorn Forest."
Then he explained the path’s dangers, the skeletons of giant creatures that filled the valley.
High-level monsters that had made nests inside the bones.
A crystalline mist that came from the Glassthorn side and distorted directions.
Reports that said no normal group had ever been able to cross the entire path. In the past, based on what he had read, the three tribes would occasionally send groups to try to cross.
But the result was always the same, either they returned alive and wounded, or everyone was killed and never returned.
"Going alone wasn’t logical." Lian said. He had planned to go alone but knew it would be dangerous, even though he had no choice.
He gave his gaze to Seris. Now with this girl’s presence, his worries would decrease.
"But now that you’re here, it shouldn’t be a problem."
"We can leave whenever you want." She also nodded.
"Three days."
"Why three days?"
"I have some things to do.
Seris waited for an explanation.
"To gather food and resources for the path, prepare One, and also take a closer look at the maps to see if I missed anything." He paused briefly.
"Besides, I promised to help Ravian become stronger."
"Three days isn’t much. How are you going to make him stronger in three days?"
"For a start, it’s enough. The boy is talented, I’m sure three days will be enough." Lian nodded and added.
In three days, he couldn’t turn that boy into a prodigy, but enough to teach him the basics and give him exercises that could put him far ahead.
Then the conversation turned to the other Awakened ones. Seris said that since her arrival, she had not directly seen anyone else.
Although she had ordered the Varkesh to find any signs they could, and they had found a few.
A blade mark on a monster’s shell that was not natural. Burned soil that did not resemble a forest fire.
The remains of a small camp.
And at a distance from the Varkesh territory, the body of a young Awakened who had probably been killed less than a day after entering... more precisely, the remains of a body.
"Did anything of his belongings remain?" Lian asked. He was not very surprised by the death of an Awakened one.
This forest was too dangerous for the Awakened ones who had entered. The risk of death was almost certain.
In fact, if any Awakened other than him and Seris could survive, he would be surprised.
"No."
Lian looked at the forest.
"So everyone is scattered across all three forests."
"The strong go after opportunities." Seris said.
"And the weak go after safety."
Survivors in the Forest of Giants would probably head toward waterways or areas with weaker monsters, of course, if they could survive long enough to reach them.
In Emberroot, caves, Salamander territory, and hot rivers could be gathering places.
In Glassthorn, only areas protected from the mist or the crystalline city had a good chance.
But the danger was not only monsters. Other Awakened ones might also fight each other for resources, Skills, and opportunities.
In a world with no clear laws, power could very quickly replace morality.
"If they find a good opportunity, they’ll compete, or kill each other." Seris said.

chapters.title: Chapter 229: A Map I
paragraphs: "Naturally." Lian did not disagree.
Each of those Awakened ones came from different backgrounds.
Normally, in the Ruined Realm and their own world, they have to follow the laws.
The crime of killing other Awakened ones is very serious... but here? There were no laws here, and anything could happen.
"If we had a complete map, it would be much better." He said after a while, his mind returning to Averian’s documents.
"Maybe I should ask the tribe leader."
The two came down from the platform and went to the council house. The elders’ meeting had just ended, and Averian and a few of the elders were leaving.
When he saw Lian and Seris, he stopped.
"We’ll be leaving this place soon." Lian said and gave a brief look at Seris.
"We want to go to the Giants’ Graveyard and then Glassthorn."
The faces of a few elders changed, and one of them whispered under his breath.
"That’s madness."
Another looked at Seris cautiously and said nothing.
Despite the power of those two, the name of the Giants’ Graveyard still had a terrifying meaning for the forest’s inhabitants.
"When are you leaving?" Averian asked.
He was not that surprised. He knew that these two were not going to stay here forever.
"In three days. Before that, we need something."
"What? I’ll help however I can."
"A map." Lian continued.
"Do you have a map of the Giants’ Graveyard or this entire world?"
Averian was silent for a moment, his gaze went to the elders, then he said.
"There is a map... but..."
He didn’t finish his sentence, so Lian asked.
"But what?"
"It’s better if you see it yourselves."
He took them to the old section of the tribe’s archive. The library was built inside a very old root.
Unlike Averian’s private hut, the space was larger but more disorganized. The shelves were carved directly into the root’s wood.
Scrolls were piled on top of each other. Bone inscriptions, skin maps, stone tablets, and containers of dried ink were placed in various spots.
The smell of old wood, dust, and dried plants was in the air.
Averian went to the back of the library, knelt in front of a short and dark chest.
Three bone locks were on it. He opened them one after another, and the chest’s lid rose with a quiet sound.
From inside, he brought out a piece of a map. At first glance, its material was different from all the tribe’s documents.
It was not monster skin, nor woven fabric. Its surface resembled thick and very resistant paper, but thin strands of mana were flowing inside it.
Its edges, despite their age, had not decayed. The lines on the map were precise, thin, and orderly.
The symbols were different from the script used by the Lacerians. A large part of the Forest of Giants could be seen on it.
The territory of the three tribes was marked with distinct symbols. Paths among the roots, old waterways, and dangerous areas were recorded on it.
In the northern section, the Giants’ Graveyard was marked with a symbol resembling a massive skull.
A line extended from the Lacerians’ territory to the edge of the graveyard.
But right where the valley path and the entrance to Glassthorn should have been shown, the map was cut off.
Its edge was not naturally torn. The cuts were precise and had been deliberately divided into separate pieces.
"The map is not complete." Averian spread the map on the table.
Lian touched its surface with his finger. A weak reaction of mana was felt under his skin, and also, some of the words used on this map seemed familiar to him.
Not that he understood their meaning, but he felt he had seen this script somewhere before...
"Where is the rest?" he then asked.
"I saw another piece with the red lizards." Before Averian could answer, Seris said.
The tribe leader nodded.
"That’s right." He placed his finger on one of the cut edges.
"Each piece is with one of the three tribes." He pointed at the map.
"This piece belongs to the Lacerians, the second piece is with the Varkesh." Then his gaze became more serious.
"And the third piece is held by the Mireclaws."
"Why did you divide it?" Lian examined the map more carefully and asked.
With just one look, he could say the details of this piece were truly unique.
"We didn’t divide it." The tribe leader said and then paused briefly.
"Previous generations did." Then he explained the story of how the map was found.
Years ago, or according to some accounts, several generations ago, members of all three tribes, while exploring an area near the Giants’ Graveyard, had come across an unknown ruin.
The building did not belong to any of the tribes. It had metal doors, and its walls were too smooth.
Symbols were carved on it that no elder or priest could read.
Inside the ruin, there were items that once worked with mana or an unknown power, but had been inactive for a long time.
They found the map inside a metal container.
When the three tribes disagreed over its ownership, a short war broke out.
In the end, the elders of the time decided to divide the map into three parts so that no tribe could use it alone.
Averian continued.
"Some think the map belonged to one of your kind."
"Or at least came into the hands of an Otherworldly in some way."
Lian touched the map’s material again. Its structure was too precise for the Lizardmen of this forest.
But it didn’t necessarily seem like it was made by an Earth human either. It could have been made by a native of the Ruined Realm.
Someone who had come to this world in the previous cycle, explored the paths of the Forest of Giants, and had been able to record the route to Glassthorn.
’Now that I look closely, these words are exactly like the writing language on the pillars of the ruin from one of the Divine Of Light temples.’ He thought for a moment.
The words were not exactly the same, but they seemed to be from the same root and form, similar to the writing on the pillars of the ruin where he had saved Kain.
But at that same moment, a troubling contradiction formed in his mind.
According to the information he had, the natives of the Ruined Realm had entered this world twenty-five years ago.
Only one cycle before.
But Averian spoke of the map’s discovery as if the event belonged to generations or even hundreds of years ago.
Was time in this world different from Earth?
Or maybe the tenth Ruined Realm was not the first world whose inhabitants had been transferred here.
Of course, this 25-year cycle was something Ravian had told him based on the legends of this world, and he had connected it to the cycle of a new Ruined Realm appearing every 25 years.
Or maybe the lifespan of these natives here is different? Which would make 25 years seem like a long time to them.
Lian didn’t ask for now.
But he made a mental note to ask Ravian or Averian later about the actual duration of the tribe’s history.
Then he fully opened the map piece on the table. The existing section showed the approximate path from the Lacerians to the edge of the Giants’ Graveyard.
Several dangerous areas were also marked with various symbols.
But the main path through the valley, the entrance to Glassthorn, and probably parts of Emberroot were on the missing pieces.
"We need to get all three pieces."
"I’ll get the second piece from the red lizards." Seris answered without pausing.
Her tone was so casual that it was as if she was going to bring an item from another room.
Not a valuable map from a tribe whose leader she had killed a few hours ago.
"After today’s events, the Varkesh will probably hand it over without resistance." Averian sighed.
Seris said nothing. For her, resistance or lack of resistance would not change the outcome.
The tribe leader then fixed his gaze on the other missing piece.
"But the third piece is with the Mireclaws. Dealing with that tribe will not be easy." His face became a little serious.
"Does it matter? If they don’t give it, we’ll kill them all." Seris said lazily.
