Lian touched its surface with his finger.
A weak reaction of mana was felt under his skin, and also, some of the words used on this map seemed familiar to him.
Not that he understood their meaning, but he felt he had seen this script somewhere before...
"Where is the rest?" he then asked.
"I saw another piece with the red lizards." Before Averian could answer, Seris said.
The tribe leader nodded.
"That’s right." He placed his finger on one of the cut edges.
"Each piece is with one of the three tribes." He pointed at the map.
"This piece belongs to the Lacerians, the second piece is with the Varkesh." Then his gaze became more serious.
"And the third piece is held by the Mireclaws."
"Why did you divide it?" Lian examined the map more carefully and asked.
With just one look, he could say the details of this piece were truly unique.
"We didn’t divide it." The tribe leader said and then paused briefly.
"Previous generations did." Then he explained the story of how the map was found.
Years ago, or according to some accounts, several generations ago, members of all three tribes, while exploring an area near the Giants’ Graveyard, had come across an unknown ruin.
The building did not belong to any of the tribes.
It had metal doors, and its walls were too smooth.
Symbols were carved on it that no elder or priest could read.
Inside the ruin, there were items that once worked with mana or an unknown power, but had been inactive for a long time.
They found the map inside a metal container.
When the three tribes disagreed over its ownership, a short war broke out.
In the end, the elders of the time decided to divide the map into three parts so that no tribe could use it alone.
Averian continued.
"Some think the map belonged to one of your kind."
"Or at least came into the hands of an Otherworldly in some way."
Lian touched the map’s material again.
Its structure was too precise for the Lizardmen of this forest.
But it didn’t necessarily seem like it was made by an Earth human either.
It could have been made by a native of the Ruined Realm.
Someone who had come to this world in the previous cycle, explored the paths of the Forest of Giants, and had been able to record the route to Glassthorn.
’Now that I look closely, these words are exactly like the writing language on the pillars of the ruin from one of the Divine Of Light temples.’ He thought for a moment.
The words were not exactly the same, but they seemed to be from the same root and form, similar to the writing on the pillars of the ruin where he had saved Kain.
But at that same moment, a troubling contradiction formed in his mind.
According to the information he had, the natives of the Ruined Realm had entered this world twenty-five years ago.
Only one cycle before.
But Averian spoke of the map’s discovery as if the event belonged to generations or even hundreds of years ago.
Was time in this world different from Earth?
Or maybe the tenth Ruined Realm was not the first world whose inhabitants had been transferred here.
Of course, this 25-year cycle was something Ravian had told him based on the legends of this world, and he had connected it to the cycle of a new Ruined Realm appearing every 25 years.
Or maybe the lifespan of these natives here is different?
Which would make 25 years seem like a long time to them.
Lian didn’t ask for now.
But he made a mental note to ask Ravian or Averian later about the actual duration of the tribe’s history.
Then he fully opened the map piece on the table.
The existing section showed the approximate path from the Lacerians to the edge of the Giants’ Graveyard.
Several dangerous areas were also marked with various symbols.
But the main path through the valley, the entrance to Glassthorn, and probably parts of Emberroot were on the missing pieces.
"We need to get all three pieces."
"I’ll get the second piece from the red lizards." Seris answered without pausing.
Her tone was so casual that it was as if she was going to bring an item from another room.
Not a valuable map from a tribe whose leader she had killed a few hours ago.
"After today’s events, the Varkesh will probably hand it over without resistance." Averian sighed.
Seris said nothing.
For her, resistance or lack of resistance would not change the outcome.
The tribe leader then fixed his gaze on the other missing piece.
"But the third piece is with the Mireclaws.
Dealing with that tribe will not be easy." His face became a little serious.
"Does it matter?
If they don’t give it, we’ll kill them all." Seris said lazily.

chapters.title: Chapter 230: Training A Little Boy I
paragraphs: "Dealing with the Mireclaws will not be easy." Averian kept his gaze on the incomplete map and said with a quiet voice.
Seris looked at the map piece without the slightest change in her face.
The thin silver lines inside the strange fabric of the map were shining in the green light of the library.
Its cut edge was completely smooth and clearly showed that the map had been intentionally divided into several parts.
"It doesn’t matter." Then she moved her hand forward and picked up the piece belonging to the Lacerians from the table.
Averian leaned his body forward for a moment, as if he wanted to stop her, but before he could show any other reaction, Seris only examined the edges of the map.
Her fingers moved over its resistant and cold fabric.
The mana strands inside the map showed a faint light with her touch, but no new part was revealed.
The map was really strange, even the paper used for it was special.
It was clear whoever was responsible for the mapping was a professional.
"When the other two parts are found, we will put all three pieces at Mr. Lian’s disposal for the necessary time."
Seris put the map back on the table.
She had no interest in arguing over its ownership.
What mattered to her was the result.
"Which one first?"
"The Varkesh are closer." Lian, who was standing next to the table, looked at the marked paths on the map.
Then he gave his gaze to Seris.
"That piece should be easy."
"It is." That girl also nodded.
Her answer was so confident that no one doubted she did not mean negotiation by easy.
She moved her gaze to Averian.
"The way to the Mireclaws?"
Averian was silent for a few moments.
Then he placed his hand on one of the old skin maps that was next to the table and opened it.
"The direct path passes through the south of the Varkesh territory." He moved his finger over the map’s faint lines.
"After that, the ground starts to sink, the roots disappear into the swamp, and most of the path is covered with black water."
"Poisonous gases come out of the ground, and some parts are not even ground; they are fungal layers that tear under body weight."
Seris listened without any particular reaction.
"The path signs are not clear either. The Mireclaws deliberately mark the routes so that only they or those who have been there before can find them."
"My daughter knows the Mireclaws’ path, she can help you." And then he called one of the soldiers to go and tell his daughter to come here.
They waited until the tribe leader’s eldest daughter arrived, and fortunately, it took no more than a few minutes, and when she came, Averian directly stated his goal.
"You want me to go with her?" Sera answered at that same moment.
There was no attempt to hide the dissatisfaction in her voice, it was clear she did not want to go with that otherworldly girl.
Seris did not even turn her head toward her.
"You know that path better than anyone, you have gone to their territory twice with the exchange groups." The tribe leader added.
Then his gaze became more serious.
"And if the Mireclaws are willing to talk, someone needs to explain from our side why we want the map."
Sera fixed her gaze on the thin sword at Seris’s waist.
The same blade that had cut off her father’s two hands, then she moved her gaze to her cold and emotionless face.
"And if they are not willing to talk?"
"I’ll force them." Seris answered briefly.
A short silence formed, Sera clenched her teeth, being with Seris was unpleasant for her from the start.
But that simple answer made her dissatisfaction greater, not because she doubted Seris’s power, but because she knew this girl would really do what she said.
"Aren’t you coming?" Seris gave her gaze to Lian.
"Well, I promised someone I would help him become stronger." Her completely black eyes paused on him for a moment.
It was simple and acceptable logic, she said nothing more, it was not like she needed help doing such an easy task.
"Besides, I’m sure you can get those two pieces. My presence won’t change anything either." Lian continued.
This sentence was not just a practical decision, it was direct trust in Seris’s power, and the girl’s eyes remained on Lian for a moment longer than usual.
She did not smile, but her gaze softened slightly.
"I’ll try to get them within three days." She said and then looked at Sera.
"We’re moving."
"Right now?" Sera asked in disbelief.
"Yes."
"I haven’t even packed my things."
Seris, without waiting, moved toward the library exit.
"Pack."
Sera looked at her back with anger for a few moments.
Then she turned to her father, as if she expected Averian to say something, but the tribe leader only gave her a meaningful look.
His daughter let out her breath with pressure.
"Great." Then she left the library with nervous steps.
Less than half an hour later, Seris and Sera left the tribe’s gate.
Sera had a light bag of food, water, and essential tools.
A knife was tied at her waist, and a short spear was on her back.
Seris only carried her sword.
No food, no water, and no extra items, as if she was not going on a multi-day trip, but only intended to walk to another part of the tribe.
Of course, naturally, she had everything she needed in her storage space, she did not need to hold them in her hands.
Lian came with them to near the gate.
Sera gave a brief look at her brother and sister.
Nemi waved at her, and Ravian also lowered his head.
Seris passed through the gate without any special farewell.
Sera was forced to take a few faster steps to not fall behind her.
When those two disappeared among the roots, Lian looked at Ravian.
"Let’s go, I want to fulfill my promise."
"The training ground?" Ravian held his spear tighter, excitement was visible in his eyes.
"Yeah, let’s see if you can handle my training or not." And a grin appeared on his face.
A few minutes later, the two were standing in the Lacerians’ training ground.
The ground was still not empty of the warriors’ training, a few people were striking on the stone pillars.
A group was working on the obstacle courses, but when Lian and Ravian entered, many turned their gaze toward them.
Ravian raised his spear, expectation and excitement could be seen in his eyes.
He probably imagined Lian would teach him a complex technique or a powerful move from the start, but Lian only moved his hand forward.
"Give me the spear."
Ravian paused briefly, then gave him the weapon.
Lian weighed it, the spear was made of compressed wood and had a bone tip, it was not a bad weapon for a warrior at Ravian’s level.
"We start from the beginning, you have to learn everything from the basics."
"I have been training with a spear for years, why should I train from the basics?" Ravian frowned at that same moment.
Lian took the spear in his hand.
"That’s your problem." Before Ravian could answer, Lian stood in a fighting stance.
He spread his legs too wide, put a lot of pressure on his front shoulder, held the spear straight, and tensed his entire body before the attack.
This was exactly the same stance Ravian used during training.
Lian made a direct strike, then he himself showed with a simple movement how the enemy could deflect the spear’s tip.
He turned his body half a step, moved the spear’s shaft off the path, and showed the completely open space of the chest.
"Here." He pointed at his own chest with two fingers.
"After the first strike, this part remains completely open."
"My movement is not that bad." Ravian felt a little humiliated upon seeing the exact imitation of his own movements.
Lian returned the spear to him.
"Against someone weaker than you, no." Then he looked directly into his eyes.
"Against someone at your level or stronger, you die before the second strike."
A few young warriors who were watching from a distance fell silent, they never thought anyone would dare to say such things to their tribe’s heir.
Ravian clenched his teeth, but did not object.
"What I’m going to teach you comes from two places." He pointed with his first finger.
"My clan’s training." He continued with his second finger.
"And my own real experience."
"My clan never only taught raw power."
"Before you control the weapon, you must control your own body." Then he stood behind Ravian and reduced the distance between his steps with his foot.
"The first principle, Rooted Step." Ravian looked at the position of his feet.
"The feet should not be fixed, but every step must maintain the center of gravity."
He pressed Ravian’s shoulder with his hand, he immediately lost his balance a little, and then Lian said.
Your weight is too far forward." Then he moved his back foot a few centimeters.

"When you attack, the weight transfers from back to front. But not so much that you have no way back." He performed the movement himself, a short step, hip rotation, weight transfer, and the spear went forward with speed, but his body remained completely balanced even at the end of the strike.
Ravian watched carefully.
The second principle was Three-Point Alignment.

chapters.title: Chapter 231: Training A Little Boy II
paragraphs: Lian corrected his hand on the spear.
"The wrist, elbow, and shoulder must be in one line." He tapped his elbow gently.
"This is too far out." Then he turned his wrist.
"This is also weak." He pointed at the shoulder.
"If one of these three points deviates, part of your power is wasted."
The third principle was Hidden Reach. He pulled the spear back slightly.
Its apparent range seemed shorter.
But at the moment of the attack, the shoulder rotated, the front foot slid half a step, and the spear’s tip suddenly went forward several centimeters more than expected...
The weapon’s tip stopped right in front of Ravian’s throat, he unconsciously stepped back.
"A good spearman doesn’t show his attack’s true range from the start." Lian said.
The fourth principle was Returning Point. Lian made a strike and immediately returned the spear’s tip to the center of defense.
His movement was so fast and natural that no gap was visible between attack and defense.
"More important than striking is returning. Most spearmen are left open for a moment after an attack." Then he gave the spear back to Ravian.
"Do a thousand strikes for practice."
"A thousand?" Ravian looked at him in disbelief.
"Each strike must return to the center."
Ravian wanted to say something, but Lian’s look stopped him.
He started.
First strike.
Return.
Second strike.
Return.
At the twentieth strike, his shoulder started to feel heavy.
At the hundredth, his breathing increased.
At the two hundredth, the spear’s tip no longer returned to the center exactly every time.
"Again." Lian said every time he made a mistake.
Ravian continued with anger.
The fifth principle seemed simpler, but was the hardest of all.
"The spear is not just wood." Lian said.
The boy looked at him breathlessly, and he took the weapon.
"The tip is for piercing." He pierced the training dummy with the tip.
"The edge is for cutting." He made a diagonal move and split the target’s side.
"The shaft is for deflecting." He pushed aside a warrior’s hypothetical strike with the spear’s body.
"The butt of the spear is for close range." He struck a hypothetical point under the enemy’s chin with the back of the weapon.
"And the whole body is for locking the enemy’s weapon."
He trapped another warrior’s spear between the body and his arm, and with a small twist, pulled it out of his hand.
Then he gave the weapon to Ravian.
"If you only use the tip, you have thrown away most of your weapon."
Real training began from that moment. Lian asked Ravian to stand in a basic stance.
Without moving, the spear at a specific height, for one hour.
In the first ten minutes, Ravian was sure it was an easy exercise. Then the muscles in his shoulder and arm started burning.
At twenty minutes, his legs trembled. At thirty minutes, the spear’s tip lowered a few centimeters, and a light hit from Lian’s spear shaft struck his forearm.
"Higher."
Ravian raised the weapon again. By the end of the hour, his clothes were soaked with sweat.
But Lian did not allow him to rest. He took him to a narrow root, the surface of the root was less than the width of two feet and located a few meters above the ground.
"The same stance."
"On this?" Ravian asked in disbelief.
"Yes."
He took the first step, his balance broke, a strike from Lian’s spear shaft hit his shin, not hard enough to cause serious damage, but enough to remember the pain.
"This is not spear training." Ravian said angrily, this seemed more like punishment than training.
"If you can’t stand on your feet, your weapon is worthless." Lian answered without changing his expression.

These were basic exercises that the children of the Vorhelm clan had to do from childhood, and now a member of a different species that must have a body more powerful than a normal human says this training is hard?
Truly pathetic.
Ravian continued.
Every mistake, a hit to his shin or thigh, every time his weight went too far forward, Lian would break his balance with a push.
After a while, his steps became shorter and more controlled. The next stage was reaction.
Lian picked up a few pebbles from the ground.
"Just deflect them with the spear’s body."
The first stone hit Ravian’s forehead directly, the second hit his shoulder, the third hit his stomach.
He shook the spear in anger, but it was too late. The fourth stone hit the side of his head.
The warriors watching from a distance hid their smiles.
But after a few hours, Ravian managed to deflect the first stone.

The spear’s body hit the stone with a short sound and pushed it aside. He missed the second one, deflected the third one again, and finally, when he managed to deflect three stones in a row, Lian said.
"Better."
Only two words, but Ravian forgot his exhaustion for a moment.
At the end of the first day, Lian picked up a wooden spear.
"Hit me."
Ravian gave a tired smile, finally something like a fight. He attacked with all his might.
The spear’s tip went straight toward Lian’s chest. He deflected it with minimal movement, and the shaft of his wooden spear hit the side of Ravian’s neck.
The second strike, and the boy changed his path.
Lian did not step back, he locked the tip with the shaft of his weapon and struck the end of the spear into his ribs.
Third strike.
Ravian tried to keep his feet better. Lian pushed the spear tip aside with one move and struck behind his knee.
Ravian fell on one knee, he got up again.
He attacked and lost... again, a hit to the wrist, a hit to the stomach, a hit to the shoulder, and after dozens of attempts, Ravian fell to the ground and breathed heavily.
Lian stood over him.
"Do you know why you lost?"
"Because you are faster." Ravian said with heavy breaths.
"No." Lian shook his head and aimed the wooden spear’s tip at Ravian’s shoulder.
"Because before every attack, you tell me what you’re going to do. Your eyes reveal the target." He pointed at the front foot.
"This shows the direction." Then he pointed at his shoulder.
"This tightens before the strike." Lian lowered the spear.
"Tomorrow you will learn to hide your intention. For today, you can go rest." Then he threw the spear on the ground.
"Oh, also, how long is the lifespan of your kind?" Then he asked the question that had been on his mind.
"Huh? Maximum eight years..." Ravian answered while enduring the muscle pain.
"Eight years? How old are you?"
"I just turned two... my father is six."
Lian fell silent, he now understood why these people talked about 25 years as if it were hundreds of years and several generations ago.
For them, it really is like that. 25 years ago for them is at least three to four generations ago.
’So my guess was correct.’ And he turned to leave.
Ravian was still lying on the ground like a dead man, staring at the endless sky. All the decisions of his life passed before his eyes.
And he thought to himself, was it a mistake to want to become stronger? Was it a wrong decision to want to protect his tribe?
He was slowly becoming sure that asking for help from Lian was a mistake. That man was a creature that monsters were afraid of...
He slaughtered giant ants and their Queen with his bare hands, and even an army of them couldn’t stop him...
At first, he thought training under such a person would make him the strongest Lizardman among all his species...
But now he realized that asking for training might have been a very wrong decision...!
His muscles had never hurt this much before. He was so soaked in sweat that it was as if a flood of rain had soaked him.
His bones were burning with such pain that he couldn’t even move...
"Can I survive three days and stay alive?"
In the end, he sighed... if the price of becoming stronger is this pain... he has no choice but to endure it. Only this way could he protect his family and his tribe.
And then he struggled to get up from his spot... but suddenly, as if an electric shock had hit him, his entire body felt a terrible pain, and he fell on the ground like a dead man.
"Damn it, ughhhhh"
The other warriors, upon seeing this scene, could barely hold back their laughter for a moment.
"Come help, right now!" Ravian looked at them and shouted.

"Each strike must return to the center."
Ravian wanted to say something, but Lian’s look stopped him.
He started.
First strike.
Return.
Second strike.
Return.
At the twentieth strike, his shoulder started to feel heavy.
At the hundredth, his breathing increased.
At the two hundredth, the spear’s tip no longer returned to the center exactly every time.
"Again." Lian said every time he made a mistake.
Ravian continued with anger.
The fifth principle seemed simpler, but was the hardest of all.
"The spear is not just wood." Lian said.
The boy looked at him breathlessly, and he took the weapon.
"The tip is for piercing." He pierced the training dummy with the tip.
"The edge is for cutting." He made a diagonal move and split the target’s side.
"The shaft is for deflecting." He pushed aside a warrior’s hypothetical strike with the spear’s body.
"The butt of the spear is for close range." He struck a hypothetical point under the enemy’s chin with the back of the weapon.
"And the whole body is for locking the enemy’s weapon."
He trapped another warrior’s spear between the body and his arm, and with a small twist, pulled it out of his hand.
Then he gave the weapon to Ravian.
"If you only use the tip, you have thrown away most of your weapon."
Real training began from that moment.
Lian asked Ravian to stand in a basic stance.
Without moving, the spear at a specific height, for one hour.
In the first ten minutes, Ravian was sure it was an easy exercise.
Then the muscles in his shoulder and arm started burning.
At twenty minutes, his legs trembled.
At thirty minutes, the spear’s tip lowered a few centimeters, and a light hit from Lian’s spear shaft struck his forearm.
"Higher."
Ravian raised the weapon again.
By the end of the hour, his clothes were soaked with sweat.
But Lian did not allow him to rest.
He took him to a narrow root, the surface of the root was less than the width of two feet and located a few meters above the ground.
"The same stance."
"On this?" Ravian asked in disbelief.
"Yes."
He took the first step, his balance broke, a strike from Lian’s spear shaft hit his shin, not hard enough to cause serious damage, but enough to remember the pain.
"This is not spear training." Ravian said angrily, this seemed more like punishment than training.
"If you can’t stand on your feet, your weapon is worthless." Lian answered without changing his expression.

These were basic exercises that the children of the Vorhelm clan had to do from childhood, and now a member of a different species that must have a body more powerful than a normal human says this training is hard?
Truly pathetic.
Ravian continued.
Every mistake, a hit to his shin or thigh, every time his weight went too far forward, Lian would break his balance with a push.
After a while, his steps became shorter and more controlled.
The next stage was reaction.
Lian picked up a few pebbles from the ground.
"Just deflect them with the spear’s body."
The first stone hit Ravian’s forehead directly, the second hit his shoulder, the third hit his stomach.
He shook the spear in anger, but it was too late.
The fourth stone hit the side of his head.
The warriors watching from a distance hid their smiles.
But after a few hours, Ravian managed to deflect the first stone.
The spear’s body hit the stone with a short sound and pushed it aside.
He missed the second one, deflected the third one again, and finally, when he managed to deflect three stones in a row, Lian said.
"Better."
Only two words, but Ravian forgot his exhaustion for a moment.
At the end of the first day, Lian picked up a wooden spear.
"Hit me."
Ravian gave a tired smile, finally something like a fight.
He attacked with all his might.
The spear’s tip went straight toward Lian’s chest.
He deflected it with minimal movement, and the shaft of his wooden spear hit the side of Ravian’s neck.
The second strike, and the boy changed his path.
Lian did not step back, he locked the tip with the shaft of his weapon and struck the end of the spear into his ribs.
Third strike.
Ravian tried to keep his feet better.
Lian pushed the spear tip aside with one move and struck behind his knee.
Ravian fell on one knee, he got up again.
He attacked and lost... again, a hit to the wrist, a hit to the stomach, a hit to the shoulder, and after dozens of attempts, Ravian fell to the ground and breathed heavily.
Lian stood over him.
"Do you know why you lost?"
"Because you are faster." Ravian said with heavy breaths.
"No." Lian shook his head and aimed the wooden spear’s tip at Ravian’s shoulder.
"Because before every attack, you tell me what you’re going to do.
Your eyes reveal the target." He pointed at the front foot.
"This shows the direction." Then he pointed at his shoulder.
"This tightens before the strike." Lian lowered the spear.
"Tomorrow you will learn to hide your intention.
For today, you can go rest." Then he threw the spear on the ground.
"Oh, also, how long is the lifespan of your kind?" Then he asked the question that had been on his mind.
"Huh?
Maximum eight years..." Ravian answered while enduring the muscle pain.
"Eight years?
How old are you?"
"I just turned two... my father is six."
Lian fell silent, he now understood why these people talked about 25 years as if it were hundreds of years and several generations ago.
For them, it really is like that.
25 years ago for them is at least three to four generations ago.
’So my guess was correct.’ And he turned to leave.
Ravian was still lying on the ground like a dead man, staring at the endless sky.
All the decisions of his life passed before his eyes.
And he thought to himself, was it a mistake to want to become stronger?
Was it a wrong decision to want to protect his tribe?
He was slowly becoming sure that asking for help from Lian was a mistake.
That man was a creature that monsters were afraid of...
He slaughtered giant ants and their Queen with his bare hands, and even an army of them couldn’t stop him...
At first, he thought training under such a person would make him the strongest Lizardman among all his species...
But now he realized that asking for training might have been a very wrong decision...!
His muscles had never hurt this much before.
He was so soaked in sweat that it was as if a flood of rain had soaked him.
His bones were burning with such pain that he couldn’t even move...
"Can I survive three days and stay alive?"
In the end, he sighed... if the price of becoming stronger is this pain... he has no choice but to endure it.
Only this way could he protect his family and his tribe.
And then he struggled to get up from his spot... but suddenly, as if an electric shock had hit him, his entire body felt a terrible pain, and he fell on the ground like a dead man.
"Damn it, ughhhhh"
The other warriors, upon seeing this scene, could barely hold back their laughter for a moment.
"Come help, right now!" Ravian looked at them and shouted.

chapters.title: Chapter 232: A Map II
paragraphs: At the same time, Seris and Sera were moving quickly through the Forest of Giants.
Seris was moving ahead, her steps seemed calm, but each time she covered a great distance.
Sera had to keep her speed high to not fall behind. They passed through tall roots, thick moss, and narrow paths.
Seris asked no questions about the path, she already knew the Varkesh’s route.
The silence between the two was heavy. Sera repeatedly looked at the sword at her waist.
Each time, the image of her father’s severed hands came alive in her mind. Finally, she could not bear it anymore.
"Don’t you regret what you did to my father at all?"
"No." Seris answered without looking back.
Sera had expected a cold answer, but its directness still made her angry.
"You could have killed him!"
"But I didn’t."
"That’s not going to make me thank you."
"I didn’t ask you to."
Sera looked at her back with anger for a few moments. Arguing with Seris was like hitting a wall.
She neither defended herself, nor explained, nor even tried to show herself in a better light. For her, Averian had been in her way.
She had defeated him, and that was the end of it.
When they reached the Varkesh territory, a few guards on the stone towers raised their weapons.
But only a moment later, they recognized Seris. Their faces changed, and a few lowered their heads.
"Why did you come back?" one of the guards asked with a trembling voice. They could not understand why this hellish demon had returned!
"The map." Seris said.
The guard was confused for a moment.
"The piece of the map you obtained from the ruin near the Giants’ Graveyard." Sera explained impatiently.
"We need permission from the new leader." the guard said.
Seris only took one step forward, her hand did not even go near her sword, but that small movement was enough to make all the guards step back.
"Bring it." Her tone was cold, emotionless, and extremely warning.
The soldiers panicked and immediately went to inform.
A few minutes later, Veyra appeared. Kharvek’s eldest daughter and the new leader of the Varkesh.
She had dark red scales and heavy armor tied on her shoulders and chest.
Her body was burly, and controlled anger could be seen in her gaze. She was upset about her father’s death but was not a fool.
She knew attacking Seris was no different from suicide.
"I want the map piece."
"If I don’t give it?" Veyra looked at her for a few moments.
"I’ll take it." Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt.
A brief silence formed, no additional threat was needed. Veyra took a deep breath and turned to one of the guards.
"Bring it."
A few minutes later, the second map piece was brought in a thick cloth.
Veyra personally handed it to Seris, but before letting go, she said.
"One day, I will find the power to not be afraid of you."
"Then become stronger." Seris took the piece from her hand. There was no mockery in her voice, nor humiliation, only a direct recommendation.
But this answer wounded Veyra’s pride more than any other sentence.
"Let’s go." Taking the second piece did not even require a minute of real negotiation.
The Varkesh’s fear had done the work before it even started. After leaving their territory, Sera took over as the guide.
The next destination was somewhere Seris did not know, and a guide was needed.
The path gradually changed. The bright green moss decreased, and dark and purple plants grew around.
The ground became softer, each step sank slightly into the soil, and the roots lowered from the surface and disappeared into the black swamp water.
Large bubbles rose from the water’s surface, and upon bursting, they released yellow or purple gas.
"Don’t step on the light-colored parts." Sera said, pointing at a yellow spot on the ground.
"Some of them are mushroom skin, not ground."
Seris followed the given path without answering. Sera noticed that despite her coldness and indifference, she did not ignore useful instructions.
She only eliminated unnecessary words.
In one section of the path, the swamp’s surface suddenly exploded. A crocodile-like creature jumped out of the water.
Its body was over ten meters long, and it had a black and slimy shell on its back. Its massive jaw opened directly toward Sera.
Sera raised her weapon, but before she could strike, Seris drew her sword.
One move.
Only one line formed in the air, and the creature was still moving through the air for a moment.
Then its body split from head to the end of its belly. The two halves of the corpse fell into the swamp on both sides of them.
The black water and dark blood splashed around.
Seris, without looking at the corpse, sheathed her sword and continued moving.
Sera remained motionless for a few moments. This was the first time she saw Seris’s power up close, without the chaos, blood, and fear of her father’s battle.
The move was so fast and precise that the monster did not even have time to complete its attack.
At that moment, Sera understood that Averian really had had no chance.
The Mireclaws’ territory appeared a few hours later. The houses were built on suspended platforms above the swamp.
Some were carved into sunken roots. Narrow rope bridges connected the platforms, and dark green mist covered the entire area.
Purple lights shone inside lanterns made of insect skin.
The Mireclaws had thinner bodies, their scales were dark green, purple, or black. Their clothes were made of plant fibers, snake skin, and parts of swamp creatures.
Their weapons were also different. Short spears with green tips, blow tubes, curved blades, and bags full of powder and gas.
Even poisonous insects were kept in small cages on some platforms. When Sera announced her identity, the guards allowed limited entry.
But their gaze on Seris was full of suspicion. They were taken to a hall on a hollow root.
Maelith, the leader of the Mireclaws, was waiting there. An elderly woman with dark purple scales and very thin antennae.
Her body seemed weak, but her eyes were sharp and alert.
"We need the map piece." Sera explained the request.
"Our piece has been with the tribe for generations." Maelith answered without haste, giving her gaze to Seris.
"We have no reason to give it to two strangers."
"They need it to leave the Forest of Giants." Sera said.
"That is not our problem." the tribe leader answered.
"Where is it?" Seris asked briefly.
The hall’s atmosphere cooled. A few guards placed their hands on their weapons, and Maelith gave a thin smile.
"You are in my territory, Otherworldly girl." It was clear she had recognized Seris’s species.
In fact, this was not the first time they had seen an Otherworldly... just a few days ago, they had hunted two of them...
That was why they were not afraid at all.
"I know." Seris said.
"Then you should know that power is not the only thing that matters here." the tribe leader added sarcastically.
"For me, it is." the young Pendragon added.
Maelith’s smile faded, but she clearly did not order an attack. Instead, she said.
"The map is kept in the inner section." She stood up.
"Follow me."
Sera hesitated for a moment, but Seris followed her without worry.
They passed through a narrow corridor, then entered a larger space.
At that same moment, the doors behind them closed with a heavy sound, but the tribe leader had not entered with them!
"Haha, you fools really thought we would give you anything?"
"You brainless idiots! Didn’t anyone tell you not to follow strangers?"
"This will be the grave for both of you! Especially you, wild and predatory Otherworldly!"
Suddenly, green gas came out from the cracks in the walls. Several Mireclaws appeared on the upper platforms, aiming blow tubes and short spears at them.
Sera smelled the poison sooner and shouted.
"Hold your breath!" A rain of poison needles was shot at them.
Seris did not rush. A dense dark aura formed around her body, and her sword came out of its sheath.
The first move was only a horizontal cut.
[Silent Divide]
An invisible wave passed through the hall. No warrior was wounded.
But all the poison tubes, spears, trap ropes, and tools in front of them were cut in half in one line.
For a few seconds, the Mireclaws still did not understand what had happened.
Then half of the weapons fell on the ground.
Seris took a step forward, the poisonous mist swirled around her.
Her body did not disappear, but split into short, dark shadows. Each shadow covered part of the path.
And every time one of the shadows faded, a warrior fell on the ground.
The tendon behind the first person’s foot was cut, and he fell on his knee with a scream.
The second one’s wrist was severed, and the weapon fell from his hand. The third one wanted to step back, but the hilt of Seris’s sword hit his temple, and he lost consciousness.
The fourth one did not even see her move, only when he fell on the ground did he realize his knees could no longer bear his weight.
Seris did not kill most of them, there was no need. With ruthless precision, she incapacitated them.
A second wave of needles was shot from the upper platforms.
[Severed Rain]
Seris’s sword moved several times in an instant. To Sera’s eyes, the blade turned into dozens of silver lines.
All the poison needles were cut in half in the air. The bone and metal pieces fell around Seris like rain on the ground.
None of them even reached her armor.
"Release the swamp guardian!" one of the guards shouted in terror.
A large hatch at the end of the hall opened. The sound of a moist and heavy roar was heard.
A multi-headed creature crawled out of the darkness. Its body resembled a massive snake, but thick armor plates were on its back.
Four heads came out of a wide neck. Green and swollen glands were trembling on both sides of its jaws.
The panel appeared before Seris’s view for a moment.
[Venom-Crowned Marsh Hydra]
[Rank: Normal]
[Level: 25]

chapters.title: Chapter 233: A Map ( Final )
paragraphs: "Be careful! This is dangerous!" Sera screamed in terror upon seeing that monster.
She had not expected those damn bastards to go that far and actually try to kill them... was their tribe leader insane?
She was the daughter of a tribe leader! If she was killed here, it could lead to war!
Or maybe not...
’The distance between our tribe and this place is great. The environmental advantage is with them. If a war starts because of my death, our tribe will definitely be the loser.’ She sighed.
The power difference between the three tribes is not much, but each has a decisive advantage in their own environment, and this advantage is even more obvious in such a swamp environment.
"Don’t worry." Seris said lazily and did not seem worried at all...
The monster’s four mouths opened at the same time, streams of green and purple poison were thrown at her.
Sera jumped back, but Seris moved straight forward.
The dark mana around her body pushed the poison aside. She ran up the wall with one step, her body rose, and she landed on one of the Hydra’s heads.
The sword moved, one diagonal cut, and all four heads were severed from the neck in one path.
Before the massive body could fall to the ground, Seris sank the blade into the center of the neck.
The monster’s vital core was split open, and the green light inside its body went out.
The Hydra fell to the ground with a loud crash. The entire battle had taken less than a few seconds.
Sera looked at the massive corpse.
Then at Seris.
"How?" Her eyes sparkled with disbelief.
A monster she considered invincible had been killed that easily in a few moves...?
Are all Otherworldlies that powerful? Why is killing a monster that could destroy their tribes so easy for these outsiders?
Is their species that powerful? Or is there another reason?

And it wasn’t just Seris. Even Lian, from her view, was a monster. The battle against the Black Brood Matriarch was something different, an exceptional enemy, a calamity... but he had managed to kill that monster with his bare hands...
Most creatures, in front of people like Lian or Seris, don’t even have the chance to turn a conflict into a real battle.
The poisonous mist in the hall became thicker.
"How? Damn it!" Maelith appeared from within it. She was horrified for a moment upon seeing that the swamp guardian had been killed so easily.
Why weren’t any of the traps working? Why couldn’t any of the soldiers kill this predatory outsider?
Why? Why? Why?
"No! It’s not possible that I lose!" A green and purple aura spun around her body.
[Poison Matriarch]
Different poisons in the air combined with each other.
A mist formed that not only disrupted vision but also slowed mana flow and deceived the senses.
"Die, you foreign bitch! Die! Die! Die!"
"Even the strongest bodies need time to break down poison." Maelith said with confidence.
Seris came forward from within the mist, without coughing and without slowing down.
The dark mana moved around her skin and kept the poison particles away from her body.
"You!- you? What are you?" Maelith was truly scared for the first time, all her plans had failed so easily.
The other Otherworldlies they had killed were not that hard!
What the hell was this damn thing?
"I’m in a hurry." Seris answered and then attacked.
Maelith did not even have time to step back. Seris appeared in front of her, and the tip of her sword was placed on her throat.
The pressure was very light, only a single drop of blood fell from under the blade.
"The map." the young Pendragon said.
Maelith looked around, her warriors were on the ground, the traps were destroyed.
The poisons had no effect. The guardian monster had been killed in a few seconds, and the girl in front of her had not even been forced to fight seriously.
With her skill, she had pushed aside all the poison and the area returned to normal.
"Bring it." Finally, with fear and having no other choice, she said.
One of the remaining people moved in fear, a few minutes later the third map piece was brought in a wooden box.
Maelith handed it to Seris, but before letting go, she said.
"By taking this map, you will become enemies of things that even we avoid."
"Doesn’t matter." Seris took the piece.
She removed her sword from Maelith’s throat and then turned back without another look.
"Let’s go."
On the way back, Sera remained silent for a long time. Her hostility had not gone away.
She still could not forgive what Seris had done to her father, but now she had a different understanding of her.
Seris did not enjoy torture or pain. She had incapacitated Averian in the simplest and fastest way.
Not out of hatred and not out of anger, but only because at that moment he was her enemy. This truth did not make her actions right.
But it showed that she was not dealing with an evil creature in the usual sense.
Seris was more like a blade. A blade does not make moral distinctions between friend and enemy.
It only acts based on who stands in front of it.
"Do you always fight like that?" Sera finally asked.
"Like what?" Seris said.
"As if nothing can touch you."
"Lian can." Seris thought for a few moments and then said.
Sera gave her gaze to her. This was the first time Seris had mentioned Lian’s name without being directly asked.
She had realized that this girl behaved very differently with Lian... her feminine intuition told her that.
Even though she had only seen them together once or twice, just by comparing this girl’s behavior with herself and others, and then her behavior when standing next to Lian, it was completely clear.
When she stands next to him, she gives off a completely different vibe. She didn’t know how to describe it... but her vibe was different from her current vibe.

Right now, she gave off more of a goddess of war and destruction vibe, bringing war and destruction with her wherever she went, so much so that even standing next to her made it hard to breathe and caused terror.
"He has defeated you?" Sera asked quietly.
"Yes, he is the only one." The silver-haired girl answered, there was no shame in her voice, nor sadness, but more like an admission of an important truth.
At that moment, Sera understood better why Seris behaved differently with Lian.
In a world where almost no one was worth her attention, Lian was the only one who had been able to force her to get serious.
She fell silent... maybe that’s why her behavior with Lian is different... because that boy is the only one who has managed to defeat this dangerous goddess...
And that’s why this girl becomes tamer and calmer around him... or maybe she just cares about what Lian thinks of her.
After thinking for a while, she just let it go. Both of these Otherworldlies were too strange, and it was impossible to understand their thoughts and feelings
At the same time their work was done and they had finally obtained both pieces and were returning to the tribe... things were not going well for everyone.
For example, Ravian... who felt like he was trapped in the depths of hell and the devil was torturing him ...

sentences.text: "Be careful!
This is dangerous!" Sera screamed in terror upon seeing that monster.
She had not expected those damn bastards to go that far and actually try to kill them... was their tribe leader insane?
She was the daughter of a tribe leader!
If she was killed here, it could lead to war!
Or maybe not...
’The distance between our tribe and this place is great.
The environmental advantage is with them.
If a war starts because of my death, our tribe will definitely be the loser.’ She sighed.
The power difference between the three tribes is not much, but each has a decisive advantage in their own environment, and this advantage is even more obvious in such a swamp environment.
"Don’t worry." Seris said lazily and did not seem worried at all...
The monster’s four mouths opened at the same time, streams of green and purple poison were thrown at her.
Sera jumped back, but Seris moved straight forward.
The dark mana around her body pushed the poison aside.
She ran up the wall with one step, her body rose, and she landed on one of the Hydra’s heads.
The sword moved, one diagonal cut, and all four heads were severed from the neck in one path.
Before the massive body could fall to the ground, Seris sank the blade into the center of the neck.
The monster’s vital core was split open, and the green light inside its body went out.
The Hydra fell to the ground with a loud crash.
The entire battle had taken less than a few seconds.
Sera looked at the massive corpse.
Then at Seris.
"How?" Her eyes sparkled with disbelief.
A monster she considered invincible had been killed that easily in a few moves...?
Are all Otherworldlies that powerful?
Why is killing a monster that could destroy their tribes so easy for these outsiders?
Is their species that powerful?
Or is there another reason?
And it wasn’t just Seris.
Even Lian, from her view, was a monster.
The battle against the Black Brood Matriarch was something different, an exceptional enemy, a calamity... but he had managed to kill that monster with his bare hands...
Most creatures, in front of people like Lian or Seris, don’t even have the chance to turn a conflict into a real battle.
The poisonous mist in the hall became thicker.
"How?
Damn it!" Maelith appeared from within it.
She was horrified for a moment upon seeing that the swamp guardian had been killed so easily.
Why weren’t any of the traps working?
Why couldn’t any of the soldiers kill this predatory outsider?
Why?
Why?
Why?
"No!
It’s not possible that I lose!" A green and purple aura spun around her body.
[Poison Matriarch]
Different poisons in the air combined with each other.
A mist formed that not only disrupted vision but also slowed mana flow and deceived the senses.
"Die, you foreign bitch!
Die!
Die!
Die!"
"Even the strongest bodies need time to break down poison." Maelith said with confidence.
Seris came forward from within the mist, without coughing and without slowing down.
The dark mana moved around her skin and kept the poison particles away from her body.
"You!- you?
What are you?" Maelith was truly scared for the first time, all her plans had failed so easily.
The other Otherworldlies they had killed were not that hard!
What the hell was this damn thing?
"I’m in a hurry." Seris answered and then attacked.
Maelith did not even have time to step back.
Seris appeared in front of her, and the tip of her sword was placed on her throat.
The pressure was very light, only a single drop of blood fell from under the blade.
"The map." the young Pendragon said.
Maelith looked around, her warriors were on the ground, the traps were destroyed.
The poisons had no effect.
The guardian monster had been killed in a few seconds, and the girl in front of her had not even been forced to fight seriously.
With her skill, she had pushed aside all the poison and the area returned to normal.
"Bring it." Finally, with fear and having no other choice, she said.
One of the remaining people moved in fear, a few minutes later the third map piece was brought in a wooden box.
Maelith handed it to Seris, but before letting go, she said.
"By taking this map, you will become enemies of things that even we avoid."
"Doesn’t matter." Seris took the piece.
She removed her sword from Maelith’s throat and then turned back without another look.
"Let’s go."

chapters.title: Chapter 234: Training A Ltitle Boy ( Finale )
paragraphs: The second day of Ravian’s training began with hiding intent.
"A good fighter doesn’t just see the enemy’s body." Lian said, pointing at Ravian’s eyes.
"He reads the mind." Then he pointed at the spear.
"You need to make sure there’s nothing to read." This was one of the most important principles of combat, especially against professionals.
Professional fighters, with the help of experience and body language, can easily tell where average or novice fighters are going to attack.
Even some monsters with high intelligence and awareness can easily figure out attack patterns.
He taught Ravian to start a strike and change it in the middle.
The spear’s tip first went toward the throat, but halfway there, the wrist turned and the strike changed to the side.
Then he learned to threaten with the spear’s tip, but use the butt of the shaft at close range.
Lian broke the attack rhythm. Two quick strikes, a pause, and a third strike.
At first, Ravian gave himself away during the pause many times, but gradually he understood that the silence between strikes was also part of the attack.
He learned to separate his gaze from the real target, looking at Lian’s left shoulder but moving the spear’s tip toward the right leg.
He failed many times.
He fell on the ground many times.
But at the end of the second day, for the first time, the tip of his spear came close to Lian’s clothes, and Lian was forced to move half a step.
"Did you see?" Ravian asked excitedly.
"I saw."
The next moment, the end of Lian’s wooden spear hit Ravian’s stomach, and he fell on the ground.
"But then you died." Lian continued. He did not intend to kill this boy’s excitement, but he didn’t want him to delude himself either.
"Did you really have to do that?" Ravian said with difficulty while enduring the pain.
His instructor was truly a sadist!
The third day was about decision-making. Lian chose three young warriors from the tribe.
Ravian had to fight all three in a row. In the first attempt, he tried to quickly defeat one.
The other two surrounded him from both sides. Less than a minute later, he was on the ground. In the second attempt, he maintained distance better.
He targeted one’s leg with the spear’s tip, then pushed the second one back with the butt of the shaft and managed to defeat one.
But against the remaining two, he ran out of breath.
In the third attempt, his movements had changed. He no longer attacked directly. He didn’t view retreat as defeat.
He forced one of the warriors to move ahead of the other two, locked his weapon with the spear’s body, and knocked him to the ground with a strike to the shin.
The second one attacked from the side. Ravian aimed the spear’s tip at his chest, but at the last moment, he changed the move and struck his jaw with the butt of the shaft.
The third one tried to circle around him.
Ravian stayed on Rooted Step, turned, kept the distance, struck three short strikes, two to deflect the defense and a third to hit the shoulder.
The third warrior also left the field.
At the end, Ravian fell on one knee, his entire body trembling from exhaustion, but all three of his opponents were on the ground.
The surrounding warriors looked at him in surprise. Only three days ago, his movements were straightforward, raw, and predictable.
Now he was still not a master, not even close, but a real foundation had formed in him.
Lian knew Ravian’s body and experience were still limited.
But the foundation that the Vorhelm clan built over years in their students had now been planted in him, although he still had a long way to go to reach a significant level.
On the evening of the third day, Hive Link reacted in Lian’s mind.
One had detected the presence of two people near the tribe. Lian turned his head toward the gate.
A few minutes later, Seris and Sera entered.
Sera was tired, her clothes were covered with dark mud, part of her sleeve was torn, and the edge of her armor had traces of poison burns.
But Seris looked almost the same as when she had left. Her silver hair was still neatly falling over her shoulders, her dark armor had only a few small bloodstains.
And that was not her own blood.
Ravian, upon seeing the difference between the two, understood their journey had not been easy.
Sera went straight to her family, and Seris approached Lian.
Without introduction, she moved her hand forward. Two pieces of the map were on her palm. One was cleaner, belonging to the Varkesh, and the other was darker, damp, and smelling of swamp plants.
"I got them."
"Was there trouble?" Lian looked at Sera, with just one look, he could tell the journey had not been peaceful.
Although for the young Pendragon, it was probably just a short amusement, but there had definitely been conflicts.
"For me, yes." Sera answered before Seris.
"Not much." And the silver-haired girl said calmly.
Sera looked at her in disbelief, but then decided not to argue.
Everyone went to the library.
Averian brought out the first piece from the chest, and Seris placed the other two pieces on the table.
When the edges of the three sections came together, the magical threads inside the map lit up.
The three pieces slowly moved, the edges were pulled toward each other, and silver light flowed through the cracks.
The separated fabrics locked together, the incomplete lines were completed, and the symbols lit up one after another.
For the first time in generations, the map became whole. The complete path of the Giants’ Graveyard was revealed.
The valley connecting to Glassthorn was marked. A side path to Emberroot could be seen. Several ruins with strange symbols were recorded.
Red areas with unknown warnings were in several sections.
And in the distant center of the map, a large symbol resembling a tree with three roots could be seen.
Probably the Forgotten Tree.
But more importantly, around the path between Glassthorn and Emberroot, a specific symbol lit up. A shape between a gate, an eye, and a heart inside a giant’s skull.
"This symbol wasn’t on our piece before." Averian came forward upon seeing it.
"Could it be what the map’s creator was looking for?" Seris looked at the symbol.
Lian examined it for a few moments. The symbol was exactly in the section connecting to Glassthorn.
"Maybe. It’s inside Glassthorn. When we get there, we can check it." Lian kept his hand on the complete map.
Three days before, they only had rumors about an exit path. Now the full path was in front of them.
The Giants’ Graveyard.
Ravian, with a battered body but curious eyes, was standing next to the table. He would also have liked to go on such adventures... but he knew he didn’t have the ability.
"You said three days. When are we leaving?" Seris looked at Lian and asked.
"Three days are over." Then he placed his finger on the Giants’ Graveyard path.
"We leave in the morning."

chapters.title: Chapter 235: Leaving The Tirbe
paragraphs: Morning had not fully arrived when the Lacerians’ gate opened.
The faint light of dawn was passing through the massive roots of the Forest of Giants and falling on the tribe’s walls.
The green and blue night lamps were still not extinguished, and a thin mist was moving along the main path.
Most of the tribe was still not awake. The sound of the craftsmen’s hammers was not heard, and the children were in their homes.
Only the guards on the walls, a few soldiers near the gate, and the small group that had come to see them off were present in that section.
One was standing near the entrance.
Its massive body had taken on a darker color under the weak morning light. Its six legs were firmly planted on the ground, and its long antennae were scanning the environment with slow movements.
Lian had placed all the necessary items in his storage space the night before. He had taken a little extra food and water in case of an emergency.
He had also taken ropes made from the sturdy leaves and stems of the giant trees, just in case they might be needed.
A few extra weapons and some of the resources that Averian had insisted on providing.
He had spent the entire night re-examining the documents related to the Giants’ Graveyard and Glassthorn Forest, and the completed map.
They were about to enter one of the most dangerous areas of this world, and he needed to gather as much information as possible before entering such a place.
But unfortunately, there was not much information. The Giants’ Graveyard was a deadly and abandoned area that no one had entered for years.
The mortality rate there was 100 percent, and anyone who had entered had not been able to return alive, so there was no information either.
Compared to him, Seris carried almost no items.
She wore her light dark armor, and her thin sword was at her waist.
Her appearance looked more like someone leaving home for a short practice session, not someone intending to enter an area from which no tribal group had ever returned alive.
But Lian’s gaze was mostly on the three people standing in front of him.
Ravian.
Sera.
And Nemi.
Nemi had stayed close to Lian from the moment he had come out of his house.
She said nothing, just followed a few steps behind him wherever he went. She had known since last night that he was going to leave the tribe.
But until One was ready to move by the gate, she had not fully felt the reality of his departure.
During the days they were lost in the Forest of Giants, Lian was not just a companion for Nemi.
Every time the roar of a monster was heard in the distance, her gaze would unconsciously go to him.
Every time the path became dangerous, she would move closer to him.
Even when the Black Brood Matriarch had controlled the entire colony and there was no escape left, Lian’s presence for her meant that there was still hope.
During all this time, without even realizing it herself, she had become attached to this outsider, so attached that she could not imagine the rest of her life without him.
Her father and sister had realized this truth much earlier, but there was nothing they could do. The attachment had already formed, and there was no way to remove it.
They could only hope that Nemi would gradually come to terms with it.
For Nemi herself, Lian was a pillar of support, and now that same person wanted to enter the most dangerous part of the forest.
And this time, she was not with him.
Lian was also ready to slowly leave, but when he raised his head, he noticed that Nemi was still looking at him.
The younger girl’s eyes were slightly wet, but she was trying not to cry, and finally, with a quiet voice, she asked.
"Do you really have to go?"
"Yeah." Lian looked at her for a few moments and answered. He was not foolish enough not to notice this girl’s attachment.
"Can’t you go later?" Nemi pressed her lips together.
"If I wait, others will get ahead of me."
That girl did not understand the real meaning of competition among Awakened ones. She did not know why a few days of delay could matter to someone like Lian.
For her, the only thing that mattered was that the Giants’ Graveyard was dangerous, and whoever entered it might never return.
"But it’s very dangerous there."
"That’s why I’m not going alone." Lian said and gave his gaze to Seris.
Nemi also looked at the silver-haired girl.
She still did not like her. The image of her father’s severed hands and the blood on Averian’s body had not faded from her mind.
But she also knew Seris’s power. She knew that if anyone could enter that valley with Lian and survive, it was probably that cold and emotionless girl.
Nevertheless, her anxiety did not completely go away. Nemi reached her hand into her clothes’ small pocket.
She brought out a thin blue band. This was a band that, in their tradition, meant that whoever had it would be protected by the Forgotten Tree.
It was a kind of tradition, not a magical item or anything like that.
She held the band out to Lian.
"Keep this."
"What is it for?" Lian took it from her hand.
"So that you come back." Nemi lowered her gaze.
Lian looked at the band for a few moments. He did not make any jokes or light comments. He tied it around his left wrist and tightened the knot so it would not come undone on the path.
Then he raised his hand for Nemi to see.
"Thank you. With this, I’m sure nothing will happen." They were simple sentences.
But Nemi needed that. She blinked a few times to keep the tears from falling and nodded.
Sera was standing a little further away. Unlike Nemi, she did not show her feelings openly.
She was standing next to her mother and pretending to be more focused on checking the guards and the exit path than on saying goodbye.
But when Lian went to her, before he could say anything, she said.
"You better not think that because you survived the Ants Queen and the Sky Giant Bird, this path will also be easy." Her tone was a little sharp.
But Lian had gotten to know her well enough to understand the hidden worry beneath it.
"Father said no group has ever returned from inside the Giants’ Graveyard." Sera continued.
"I am not normal either." Lian answered.
"I know that." Sera gave a brief look at Seris.
Then she was silent for a few moments, her antennae made a short movement, and finally her voice became a little softer.
"Just... take care of yourself." For Sera, this sentence was almost equivalent to an open admission of worry.
"You too, take care of yourself and Nemi and Ravian." Lian nodded.
Sera then turned to Seris. The hostility between the two had still not completely faded.
Three days of shared travel had made Sera understand her better, but that understanding did not mean forgiveness.
"If something happens—"
"It won’t." Seris cut her off. She didn’t understand why everyone was making such a drama out of everything.
Was it really necessary? This was just a normal trip, nothing more and nothing less. She couldn’t understand why these lizards were so emotional.
Besides, it wasn’t like this was her and Lian’s first trip together.
"I was going to say take care of him." Sera frowned.
Seris looked at her for a few moments, her eyes remained on Sera’s face without any obvious emotion.
"He doesn’t need protection." She then said and paused briefly.
"But okay."
For a moment, Sera had no answer. Maybe she had expected Seris to ignore her words, but that short answer made her feel a little more at ease about Seris being with Lian.
Ravian was the last one. He stood straight in front of Lian.
He had brought his spear and was holding it with both hands. His body was still aching from the three days of training.
His palms were blistered, dark bruises could be seen on his shins, and his shoulders were tired.
But his stance was different from three days ago. His legs were no longer too wide apart.
His weight was better distributed, and the spear’s tip was exactly in the center of defense.
"Three days was too short." Ravian said.
"For you to become stronger? Yeah." Lian answered simply.
"You said you would help me, but you’re leaving so soon." Ravian gripped the spear’s shaft tighter, as if trying to hide his real feelings.
"I did help you."
"I didn’t mean just three days of training." Ravian frowned, frustration was clear in his voice.
But beneath it, there was another fear, perhaps the fear that Lian might never return.
The young Vorhelm looked at him for a few moments, then pointed at the spear.
"What I taught you was not for three days. Every day, a thousand Returning Points. Every day, Rooted Step on the narrowest root you can find."
"And once a week, fight three people at the same time."
Ravian listened carefully.
"Keep your gaze separate from the real target. Every strike must have a way back. And if you feel the training has become easy, that means you’re doing it wrong." Lian added in the end.
"When I come back, if you’re still making the same mistakes as before, we’ll start your training from the beginning."

sentences.text: Morning had not fully arrived when the Lacerians’ gate opened.
The faint light of dawn was passing through the massive roots of the Forest of Giants and falling on the tribe’s walls.
The green and blue night lamps were still not extinguished, and a thin mist was moving along the main path.
Most of the tribe was still not awake.
The sound of the craftsmen’s hammers was not heard, and the children were in their homes.
Only the guards on the walls, a few soldiers near the gate, and the small group that had come to see them off were present in that section.
One was standing near the entrance.
Its massive body had taken on a darker color under the weak morning light.
Its six legs were firmly planted on the ground, and its long antennae were scanning the environment with slow movements.
Lian had placed all the necessary items in his storage space the night before.
He had taken a little extra food and water in case of an emergency.
He had also taken ropes made from the sturdy leaves and stems of the giant trees, just in case they might be needed.
A few extra weapons and some of the resources that Averian had insisted on providing.
He had spent the entire night re-examining the documents related to the Giants’ Graveyard and Glassthorn Forest, and the completed map.
They were about to enter one of the most dangerous areas of this world, and he needed to gather as much information as possible before entering such a place.
But unfortunately, there was not much information.
The Giants’ Graveyard was a deadly and abandoned area that no one had entered for years.
The mortality rate there was 100 percent, and anyone who had entered had not been able to return alive, so there was no information either.
Compared to him, Seris carried almost no items.
She wore her light dark armor, and her thin sword was at her waist.
Her appearance looked more like someone leaving home for a short practice session, not someone intending to enter an area from which no tribal group had ever returned alive.
But Lian’s gaze was mostly on the three people standing in front of him.
Ravian.
Sera.
And Nemi.
Nemi had stayed close to Lian from the moment he had come out of his house.
She said nothing, just followed a few steps behind him wherever he went.
She had known since last night that he was going to leave the tribe.
But until One was ready to move by the gate, she had not fully felt the reality of his departure.
During the days they were lost in the Forest of Giants, Lian was not just a companion for Nemi.
Every time the roar of a monster was heard in the distance, her gaze would unconsciously go to him.
Every time the path became dangerous, she would move closer to him.
Even when the Black Brood Matriarch had controlled the entire colony and there was no escape left, Lian’s presence for her meant that there was still hope.
During all this time, without even realizing it herself, she had become attached to this outsider, so attached that she could not imagine the rest of her life without him.
Her father and sister had realized this truth much earlier, but there was nothing they could do.
The attachment had already formed, and there was no way to remove it.
They could only hope that Nemi would gradually come to terms with it.
For Nemi herself, Lian was a pillar of support, and now that same person wanted to enter the most dangerous part of the forest.
And this time, she was not with him.
Lian was also ready to slowly leave, but when he raised his head, he noticed that Nemi was still looking at him.
The younger girl’s eyes were slightly wet, but she was trying not to cry, and finally, with a quiet voice, she asked.
"Do you really have to go?"
"Yeah." Lian looked at her for a few moments and answered.
He was not foolish enough not to notice this girl’s attachment.
"Can’t you go later?" Nemi pressed her lips together.
"If I wait, others will get ahead of me."
That girl did not understand the real meaning of competition among Awakened ones.
She did not know why a few days of delay could matter to someone like Lian.
For her, the only thing that mattered was that the Giants’ Graveyard was dangerous, and whoever entered it might never return.
"But it’s very dangerous there."
"That’s why I’m not going alone." Lian said and gave his gaze to Seris.
Nemi also looked at the silver-haired girl.
She still did not like her.
The image of her father’s severed hands and the blood on Averian’s body had not faded from her mind.
But she also knew Seris’s power.
She knew that if anyone could enter that valley with Lian and survive, it was probably that cold and emotionless girl.
Nevertheless, her anxiety did not completely go away.
Nemi reached her hand into her clothes’ small pocket.
She brought out a thin blue band.
This was a band that, in their tradition, meant that whoever had it would be protected by the Forgotten Tree.
It was a kind of tradition, not a magical item or anything like that.
She held the band out to Lian.
"Keep this."
"What is it for?" Lian took it from her hand.
"So that you come back." Nemi lowered her gaze.
Lian looked at the band for a few moments.
He did not make any jokes or light comments.
He tied it around his left wrist and tightened the knot so it would not come undone on the path.
Then he raised his hand for Nemi to see.
"Thank you.
With this, I’m sure nothing will happen." They were simple sentences.
But Nemi needed that.
She blinked a few times to keep the tears from falling and nodded.
Sera was standing a little further away.
Unlike Nemi, she did not show her feelings openly.
She was standing next to her mother and pretending to be more focused on checking the guards and the exit path than on saying goodbye.
But when Lian went to her, before he could say anything, she said.
"You better not think that because you survived the Ants Queen and the Sky Giant Bird, this path will also be easy." Her tone was a little sharp.
But Lian had gotten to know her well enough to understand the hidden worry beneath it.
"Father said no group has ever returned from inside the Giants’ Graveyard." Sera continued.
"I am not normal either." Lian answered.
"I know that." Sera gave a brief look at Seris.
Then she was silent for a few moments, her antennae made a short movement, and finally her voice became a little softer.
"Just... take care of yourself." For Sera, this sentence was almost equivalent to an open admission of worry.
"You too, take care of yourself and Nemi and Ravian." Lian nodded.
Sera then turned to Seris.
The hostility between the two had still not completely faded.
Three days of shared travel had made Sera understand her better, but that understanding did not mean forgiveness.
"If something happens—"
"It won’t." Seris cut her off.
She didn’t understand why everyone was making such a drama out of everything.
Was it really necessary?
This was just a normal trip, nothing more and nothing less.
She couldn’t understand why these lizards were so emotional.
Besides, it wasn’t like this was her and Lian’s first trip together.
"I was going to say take care of him." Sera frowned.
Seris looked at her for a few moments, her eyes remained on Sera’s face without any obvious emotion.
"He doesn’t need protection." She then said and paused briefly.
"But okay."
For a moment, Sera had no answer.
Maybe she had expected Seris to ignore her words, but that short answer made her feel a little more at ease about Seris being with Lian.
Ravian was the last one.
He stood straight in front of Lian.
He had brought his spear and was holding it with both hands.
His body was still aching from the three days of training.
His palms were blistered, dark bruises could be seen on his shins, and his shoulders were tired.

Yeah." Lian answered simply.
"You said you would help me, but you’re leaving so soon." Ravian gripped the spear’s shaft tighter, as if trying to hide his real feelings.
"I did help you."

The young Vorhelm looked at him for a few moments, then pointed at the spear.

Every day, Rooted Step on the narrowest root you can find."
