chapters.title: Chapter 236: The Graveyard Of Giants I
paragraphs: "Whatever you see inside the Giants’ Graveyard, don’t trust it." Averian said quietly.
"What do you mean? I also saw that mentioned in the documents, but there was no reason given." Lian raised an eyebrow.
"I don’t know. The stories say sounds are heard there, and it’s not clear who they belong to."
"And sometimes the path behind you disappears."
Seris showed no reaction, but Lian remembered the sentence.
He sat on One’s back, and the silver-haired girl also jumped up lightly and sat behind him.
The space on One’s massive body was enough for both of them. The ant raised its antennae and waited for the command.
Nemi stood near the gate until the last moment. When One moved, she followed them a few steps.
Sera placed her hand on her younger sister’s shoulder and held her back gently.
Ravian raised his spear, and Averian placed his hand on his chest.
Lian turned back for the last time. The Lacerians were standing among the massive roots and green lights.
The blue band on his wrist moved with the airflow, then the path curved, and the root walls came between them.
And the tribe disappeared from view.
A few minutes passed in silence. He had finally left the place he had lived in for these few days.
"Did you get attached to them?" Seris, who was sitting behind Lian, finally asked.
"Maybe, but attachment is not the right word. Leaving them is neither hard nor a problem for me. It’s just that I won’t see them again, which feels strange." Lian thought for a moment.
"It was fast." Seris said.
"When you go to the brink of death with someone a few times, relationships naturally form quickly."
Seris was silent for a few moments, then nodded.
She understood this logic better than most ordinary emotions, because her own relationship with Lian was also formed based on exactly this logic.
Those two had also gone to the brink of death several times and had even fought an Unholy together, which is why they now have such a close relationship.
In the first hours of the journey, the Forest of Giants was no different from previous days.
Roots as large as fortress walls stretched in all directions, green mist moved among them.
Luminous plants glowed on the trunks, and the sound of giant insects was heard from a distance.
Sometimes the shadow of a large bird passed through the mist.
Smaller monsters changed their path upon sensing the presence of One and Seris.
One moved at a steady speed, its six legs easily crossing the uneven ground, thick moss, and gaps between the roots.

Lian took out the map several times and checked the direction. The path was initially simple. They had to follow a white root, then pass by a dry waterway, and finally reach a section marked on the map with a broken pillar symbol.
But as hours passed, small changes began.
First, the sound of insects decreased. Not suddenly, but gradually, and the buzzing that was always in the background of the forest slowly faded.
Then the birds disappeared. No more shadows passed above the roots. The luminous plants became dimmer, some completely dark.
The moss lost its vibrant green color and turned into a dull gray. Scattered bones on the ground increased.
At first, normal bones, remains of small monsters, then a rib several meters long, a broken skull in whose eye socket a person could stand.
And a few hours later, a bone whose thickness was almost equal to a tree trunk.
It was clear they were slowly approaching dangerous areas that even monsters did not dare to go near.
One suddenly stopped.
Its movement was so sudden that Seris placed her hand on the ant’s armored body to keep her balance.
One’s antennae rose, and its jaws opened slightly.
Lian felt a wave of anxiety through Hive Link.
A raw and instinctive feeling.
One did not see an enemy, but its entire body told it not to go forward.
"It’s scared." Seris looked at the ant. It was clear with just one look.
"I know." Lian answered and jumped down from One. He had not expected this ant to also hesitate to approach the graveyard.
Seris also came to the ground.
Both checked the surroundings. There was no obvious movement.
No monster could be seen, no smell of fresh blood or living creature came, but the silence was too deep.
Even the wind did not make a sound among the roots. The space looked like a part of the world that had been separated from the rest of nature.
Lian placed his hand on One’s armor and tried to understand the source of its anxiety through Hive Link.
There was no clear answer, only fear.
"Can you force it to move forward?" Seris asked. The path was not smooth, and if they had to continue on foot, it would be troublesome.
"I can." Lian looked at the gray path ahead, then back at One.
"But we’re not in a hurry." He did not force One to move at its previous speed.
They mounted again. This time, the ant’s steps were slower. Before each step, it would check the ground with its antennae and senses.
The further they went, the more the Forest of Giants remained behind them.
By late afternoon, almost no living plants were around them. The ground had become rockier. The green mist had turned gray.
And finally, the sign that Averian had mentioned appeared from within the mist.
At first glance, it looked like a stone pillar. Something tall and white that had risen dozens of meters from the ground and was broken in the middle.
But when they got closer, Lian saw the curved lines on its surface.
Natural cracks, tiny holes, and a texture that had no resemblance to stone.
It was a bone.
A finger bone. Part of a creature’s finger that was once so massive that just one joint stuck out of the ground like a tower.
Lian got down from One. At the lower part of the bone, old marks were carved.
The symbol of return, the warning of death, and a symbol that in the lizard culture meant absolute prohibition of entry. Some of the signs were so old that their edges were worn away.
Lian ran his finger over one of them. The bone dust settled on his hand.
He had learned these signs by studying the reports and understood their approximate meaning.
"This finger is really huge. How does this forest have such massive monsters?" Seris looked at the broken top.
Lian raised his head. The tip of the bone disappeared in the mist.
"If just its finger is this big..." He didn’t finish the sentence. There was no need. And they continued on their way.
From that point on, the Forest of Giants slowly ended. The ground became sloped, the roots decreased, and gray and black rocks took their place.
The mist became colder.
On the horizon, something like a mountain appeared. At first, it had no clear shape, a massive white mass in the mist. But the closer they got, two dark holes could be seen on it.
Holes as large as buildings. Then the jawline, the marks of broken teeth, and they understood that it was not a mountain but part of a massive skull.
One slowed down again.
Lian felt its anxiety increasing every moment.
Their path passed by a rocky cliff. For a few moments, the wind pushed the mist aside, and finally, a small part of the Giants’ Graveyard was revealed before them.
"You see it? We’re getting closer..."
Ribs like towers had risen from the ground, a spine several kilometers long was stretched through the valley.
Massive skulls were submerged in the mist. Broken swords the size of buildings were placed among the bones.
Some blades were half-sunk into the ground. Massive chains were wrapped around several skeletons.
Each of their links was the size of a house. On one of the distant bones, black spots were moving.
From that distance, they looked like ants.
But considering the size of the bone, each of those spots had to be larger than One.
The mist rose again, and the valley’s view was hidden.
"Where did those blades come from? How are they so massive?" Seris showed clear interest.
Her hand went to her sword’s hilt, and her black eyes looked more carefully into the mist.
"I don’t know either, but whoever can make such massive swords really knows their craft." Lian was also amazed.
"This place is very interesting."
"I knew you would like it."
Dusk was approaching, the gray light of the sky was getting weaker every moment. Lian decided to set up camp before entering deeper into the graveyard.
Between two curved ribs, they found a space that was closed from three sides. The ribs were like tall white walls around the spot.
Only a narrow entrance faced the mist, and One was stationed near that entrance.
Its body almost completely blocked the path. Lian placed a few light crystals on the ground, creating a soft white light.
They did not light any fire. They didn’t know what creatures the smell of smoke or heat might attract.
Seris sat next to one of the ribs, placed her sword on her knee, and looked at the mist ahead.
Lian opened the map. The lines had become much clearer after the map was completed.
The path showed that in the morning they had to pass through a section called Rib Passage, after that, a narrow path went down into the valley’s depth.
"Hmm? This isn’t right." But when Lian compared the path behind them with the map, something was wrong.
The root they had passed by hours ago should have been visible from that same point, but behind the camp, there was nothing but a wall of bone and mist.
Lian stood up, walked back a few steps, and examined the mist. There was no trace of the previous path!
"It seems the path has changed." Seris also looked back.
"Strange." Lian narrowed his eyes. There really was no trace of the previous path, and it seemed to have disappeared.
He looked at the map and then back at the bone wall.
"Is this an illusion, or has the path really changed?"
Seris did not answer. She placed her hand on the bone and examined it for a few moments.
"It’s real."
Lian came closer. The bone’s surface was cold and solid. There was no sign of an image or illusion. The path behind them had really been replaced by something else.
He remembered Averian’s warning, "Sometimes the path behind you disappears."
"We have to be careful." And both went into a light sleep for rest, while the ant was supposed to keep watch.
That night, neither of them slept deeply.
One remained anxious throughout. Lian could feel its states through Hive Link.
The ant kept turning its antennae toward the mist, but nothing could be seen.
However, at midnight, a sudden wave of One’s anxiety woke Lian up.
His eyes immediately opened, and his hand went toward his weapon... he too finally felt the danger!

There was no sign of an image or illusion.
The path behind them had really been replaced by something else.
He remembered Averian’s warning, "Sometimes the path behind you disappears."
"We have to be careful." And both went into a light sleep for rest, while the ant was supposed to keep watch.
That night, neither of them slept deeply.
One remained anxious throughout.
Lian could feel its states through Hive Link.
The ant kept turning its antennae toward the mist, but nothing could be seen.
However, at midnight, a sudden wave of One’s anxiety woke Lian up.
His eyes immediately opened, and his hand went toward his weapon... he too finally felt the danger!

chapters.title: Chapter 237: The Graveyard Of Giants II
paragraphs: The light crystals were still shining.
Seris was also awake. Perhaps she had not slept at all.
Her hand was on her sword’s hilt. No enemy could be seen in the range of the light, but both strongly felt it.
"Be careful, something is near us, but it can hide well." Lian warned and activated Predator’s Instincts.
He tried to track any sign of danger, but there was nothing other than the feeling of danger.
However, suddenly a sound came from within the mist!
"Lian!"
It was Ravian’s voice!
Lian narrowed his eyes. The voice was exact, the same tone, the same inflection, and even the anxiety in it seemed natural.
"Lian, where are you?"
The sound came from the left, and Seris did not look in that direction and only said quietly.
"There is something there."
A few moments later, another sound was heard, this time a human girl’s voice, trembling and crying.
"Help me..."
Lian’s heart reacted for a fraction of a second.
Seraphina.
One of his group members, his childhood friend, and someone he had been separated from after entering the Special Area.
The voice sounded exactly like hers. Not like a weak imitation, completely real! So accurate that it could make anyone doubt.
"Lian... please..."
The voice came from within the mist, but Seraphina could not be there.
She was probably hundreds and thousands of kilometers away, maybe even in another forest.
"I don’t know what you’re hearing, but it’s not real." Seris said briefly.
Her tone showed that she was hearing something different, or maybe hearing nothing at all.
"I know." Lian answered. He is not foolish enough to fall for such a trick.
But now he finally understood what the documents meant when they talked about strange sounds.
And even though he knew the sounds were false, they did not stop.
And suddenly he heard a sound he did not expect.
"This way!" Kain... his closest friend.
"Lian, don’t go alone." Liana’s worried voice.
"We found you! Do you know how long we’ve been looking for you?" He even heard Selina’s serious and familiar voice.
Then Sera, Nemi, and Ravian again.
The sounds came from different points, sometimes close, sometimes far, sometimes from behind the camp, and sometimes right next to the massive ribs.
They all had one goal, to pull him out of the light’s range, as if they could not get close or enter the light.
"If my guess is correct, they all want to pull us away from the light." Lian also noticed this.
Suddenly, shadows moved in the mist. For a moment, Ravian’s figure was seen and then disappeared.
A little further away, a shadow with Seraphina’s height and posture stood.
But the crystal light reached the mist, and the shape faded.
"So not only sounds, but they can also imitate appearances." Lian said with admiration and of course noticed the weak point, which was light.
"They’re getting closer." Seris said.
Lian nodded and turned off the crystals, waiting for the monsters to get closer so he could hunt them if possible, and turn the light back on if necessary.
One opened its jaws, lowered its body, and prepared to attack.
Nemi’s voice came from very close.
"Lian..." From behind one of the ribs.
"I told you to come back..." Someone came out of the darkness.
It was Nemi, at least at first glance.
Height, scale color, clothes, and the small bands beside the antennae, all were exact.
But a few things were wrong. Her hands were slightly longer than normal, her antennae moved in opposite directions.
Her eyes did not blink, and her smile was too wide, so wide that the corners of her mouth were almost stretched to the sides of her jaw.
"Nemi." She took a step toward them.
"I told you to come back..."
Lian moved without a moment’s hesitation. Before the creature could take a second step, he appeared in front of it.
His fist hit the fake face. The creature’s head was thrown back with a dry sound.
The fake skin tore, but beneath it was not flesh, but black bones and white, moist strands, a parasitic tissue that moved among the joints.
The panel appeared before Lian’s view.
[Grave Mimic]
[Level: 22]
[Rank: Normal]
Despite its broken neck, the creature was still standing. Its head turned at an unnatural angle, and the fake smile remained on its face.
"Disgusting." Lian threw a second punch directly at its chest.
The outer shell cracked, and a black heart was revealed among the white strands. At that same moment, several shadows came out of the mist.
One had Ravian’s shape, one had Sera’s, and another looked like Liana and Selina. A few human faces were also seen among them.
Marcus and Kain, Seraphina, and people Lian did not even recognize.
Some were perhaps shapes of previous victims, some perhaps images pulled from Seris’s mind.
The Grave Mimics attacked with fast and irregular movements. Their joints turned in directions that a normal body could not.
One of them ran on all fours, another jumped forward without bending its knees.
Lian crushed the black heart of the creature in front of him. The fake body trembled for a moment and then collapsed on the ground.
But before he could step back, white strands shot out from inside the corpse.
Directly toward his face, and Lian moved his head aside. The strands passed by him.
Seris’s sword moved at that same moment, and the strands were cut into pieces in the air.
She stood behind Lian. Without needing coordination, the two stood back-to-back.
Another Grave Mimic with Sera’s face attacked Seris.
The silver sword moved, and the fake body was split in half from shoulder to waist, but before the two halves could reach the ground, they were pulled back together by white strands.
"They regenerate." Seris narrowed her eyes.
"The heart is in the chest." Lian answered.
"Behind you!" one of the Mimics shouted with Kain’s voice.
Lian did not react to the sound. The creature attacked from the right. He grabbed its wrist, turned the body, and broke its ribcage with his knee.
The black heart came out.
Lian crushed it with his fingers, and the body immediately became still.
Seris changed her movement. She no longer only cut limbs.
Every cut went directly to the center of the chest. One silver line, then tearing the fake skin, breaking the black bone, and destroying the heart.
Three Grave Mimics fell in less than a few seconds.
One charged forward with a muffled roar. Its jaws closed around one of the creatures’ bodies.
With the pressure of its jaws, its bones were crushed. Another creature jumped on One’s back. White strands came out of its open mouth and searched for gaps between the armor plates.
Lian felt One’s sudden terror through Hive Link.
He immediately turned around. The creature had inserted its hand into one of the gaps.
The parasites were trying to enter the ant’s body. Lian grabbed the strands.
He pulled.
The white strands came out of the gap and twisted around his hand like living worms. They tried to stick to his skin.
Lian concentrated mana in his hand. The strands burned and dried up, and then with a direct strike, he crushed the Mimic’s heart.
The fake body fell off One.
Seris split the last creature in half, and Lian destroyed the heart before the two halves could reconnect.
For a few moments, silence returned. The Grave Mimic corpses lay on the ground.
But they did not remain. The white strands came out of the broken bodies one after another.
They crawled on the ground, moved toward the massive bones around, some sank into the cracks of the ribs.
Some disappeared under the soil. In less than a minute, nothing remained but pieces of fake skin and black spots.
Lian looked at the cracks in the bones. These creatures were not separate from the graveyard, they were part of it.
Perhaps the entire valley was connected like a living network.
Seris lowered her sword’s tip and looked at one of the cracks.
"These weren’t alone."
"Unfortunately." Lian said. Now he could understand why none of the lizardman tribes had been able to get out of here alive.
They hadn’t even entered the graveyard yet and had already encountered such strange monsters.
At that same moment, a massive cracking sound rose from the valley’s depth, not like the movement of a small monster, but like a bone hundreds of meters long being dragged on rock.
The ground beneath their feet trembled, and white dust fell from the ribs.
"What now?"
One lowered its body.
Seris turned her head toward the mist, but nothing could be seen.
The rest of the night, neither of them slept. The sounds did not return, but sometimes distant movements could be seen in the mist.
Sometimes the sound of bones rubbing, sometimes a weak tremor under the ground. When the gray light of morning passed through the sky, the mist parted for a few minutes.
Lian and Seris came out from between two ribs and approached the cliff’s edge.
This time, the Giants’ Graveyard showed all its grandeur. An endless valley stretched beneath them.
Hundreds of giant skeletons lay there. Some were humanoid, some had multiple arms, and some had skulls with twisted horns or animal jaws.
Skeletons of monsters that bore no resemblance to natural creatures could be seen. Spinal columns stretched like white roads across the valley.
Massive swords, spears, and axes were sunk among the bones. Black chains were wrapped around some bodies.
And in the center of the valley, the largest skeleton sat.
A sitting giant.
Its height, even in a sitting position, was greater than many mountains.
A broken crown was on its skull. A massive sword was sunk into its chest.
Black chains were wrapped around its neck, arms, and legs, and their ends disappeared into the ground.
Lian opened the map.
The marked path passed exactly under that same skeleton.
Seris looked at it. Instead of fear, calm excitement formed in her black eyes.
But before she could say anything, one of the giant’s fingers moved. The movement was very slow, so little that it could be attributed to a tremor in the ground.
But soil and small bones fell from its hand.
A red and incomplete panel appeared before Lian’s view.
[Level: Unable to Determine]
[Status: Dormant — Awakening 1%]
Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt, the spark of interest in her eyes grew stronger.
"Finally, we found something interesting."
Lian also placed his hand on his weapon, his gaze moving from the panel to the massive skeleton.
"I hope it doesn’t wake up before we pass." Just the aura he felt from this sitting giant was comparable to the Dreadmaw.
If his guess was not wrong, this thing could be an Unholy!
He preferred not to face such a thing...
But at that same moment, the writing before his view changed.
[Status: Dormant — Awakening 2%]

chapters.title: Chapter 238: The Graveyard Of Giants III
paragraphs: [Status: Dormant — Awakening 2%]
The red panel remained before Lian’s view for a few seconds. In the distance, the sitting giant was still motionless.
A massive skeleton that even in a sitting position cast a shadow like a broken white mountain over the entire Giants’ Graveyard.
Its shattered crown remained on its skull, and the sword that had passed through its chest looked more like a black tower than a weapon from this distance.
Massive chains were wrapped around its neck, shoulders, arms, and legs. Some links were intact, some were broken, and their remaining ends disappeared among the valley’s bones.
But the giant itself did not move again. Only that one finger had shifted slightly a few moments ago.
Or perhaps something inside it had moved.
Seris stood next to Lian, her black eyes not leaving the massive skeleton.
Unlike One, which had been anxious from the moment they approached the valley, there was no fear or hesitation in Seris’s gaze. A spark of interest and calm excitement had formed in her eyes.
"Finally, we found something interesting."
"No. We found something we shouldn’t get close to right now." Lian answered without taking his eyes off the giant.
"Are you scared?"
Lian gave a brief look at her this time.
"No." Then he stared at the giant again.
"I know the difference between courage and stupidity." He was sure this thing was an Unholy, and although he would also like to face and fight such a monster, he knew now was not the time.
First, the chance of their death was certain, and second, his main goal right now was reaching his first evolution, which he was not far from.
Maybe after his first evolution, he could face an Unholy.
Seris said nothing because she also knew this was true. Facing such a monster would be suicide.
Lian checked the panel again.
[Status: Dormant — Awakening 2%]
The percentage had not changed.
A few minutes passed. The gray mist moved over the valley’s bones, and white dust fell from some of the massive ribs.
The distant sound of something rubbing in the valley’s depth was heard, but the percentage still remained at two, and this point was important for Lian.
If the creature was truly awakening, there should be a clear process.
One percent.
Two percent.
Three percent.
But since the panel was first seen, no other change had occurred. The first possibility was that their entry had only caused a brief reaction.

The second possibility was the destruction of the Grave Mimics. Perhaps the death of those creatures had stimulated part of the graveyard’s network, and the system had recorded that reaction as Awakening.
The third possibility was more unpleasant. The panel might not show the giant’s own status at all.
Perhaps something was sleeping inside its bones, a sealed creature or a remnant of a power that had been buried with this giant thousands of years ago.
The last possibility was that the giant was completely dead, and the system had simply mistaken the activation of residual energy in its corpse for awakening.
But each of the possibilities had their own flaws and illogicalities. He himself was somewhat sure that killing those monsters had stimulated this giant’s awakening.
And this meant that killing monsters might affect this monster’s awakening, a point he had to keep in mind.
"It’s remained on two percent." Lian said under his breath.
"So?" Seris asked.
"So as long as it doesn’t go higher, we ignore it.
The silver-haired girl looked at the giant again.
"If it goes higher?"
"Then we decide again." Lian’s answer was simple, but it was the right decision.
They had not come to the Giants’ Graveyard to fight a creature whose Level could not even be detected by the system.
Their goal was to cross the valley and reach Glassthorn Forest.
Anything else was only worth it if the risk was manageable.
Lian took out the complete map from his storage space and spread it on a relatively flat rock. The strands inside the map lit up upon contact with the air.
The valley was not just one large depression. It had several layers, high paths on ribs and spinal columns, deep gaps between skeletons, tunnels passing through skulls and hollow bones.
And areas marked with red and black signs.
The main path to Glassthorn Forest consisted of three parts.
First, the Rib Passage, a path between the ribs of a dead giant that led from the northern edge of the graveyard to the lower level of the valley.
After that, the Hollow Spine, a path passing through the hollow spinal column of a massive creature and bypassing the central part of the graveyard.
And finally, the Crystal Wound, a crack in the valley’s eastern wall where the crystalline mist and cold of Glassthorn entered the graveyard.
There was also a direct path, a shorter line that passed almost through the valley’s center, but that direct path passed under the sitting giant’s skeleton.
Lian followed the path with his finger.
"The direct path passes under it."
"It’s shorter." Seris gave a brief look at the map.
Lian pointed at the chains around the giant.
"And whatever is chained up like that probably has a good reason, and we’re not going to find out by trying."
He chose the longer path.
The Rib Passage.
Moving from the north of the valley, bypassing the sitting giant’s skeleton, entering the Hollow Spine, and then moving toward the Crystal Wound.
The path was longer, but it kept more distance from the main threat.
Lian did not close the map. Before entering, he decided not to trust only the drawn lines.
He checked the bottom from the cliff’s edge. At first glance, the valley was nothing but a sea of bones, mist, and giant ruins.
But when he looked without moving for a few minutes, the patterns became clear. The black spots they had seen from a distance the day before were still moving on some bones.
They looked like insects, but their dimensions were much larger than what they had seemed at first glance.
The strange thing was that none of them approached a few specific skeletons. On the western rib, the black spots moved forward to an invisible border and then changed their path.
The same behavior was seen around a horned skull.
Lian concluded that those empty areas were not necessarily safe. They might be heavily contaminated or the territory of a stronger creature.
In some parts of the valley floor, crushed bones and small carcasses were scattered everywhere.
But a few long and narrow paths looked completely clean, with no bone pieces or monster remains on them.
At first glance, they seemed the best way to move, but he looked more carefully. The edges of the paths were not smooth. The crushed bones had been pushed to the sides.
As if something massive regularly passed through there and pushed aside any obstacle.
Lian marked those paths in his mind as danger lines. The gray mist also did not behave naturally.
The wind blew from north to south, but the mist moved against the wind in some places. It gathered around a few skulls, entered through the eye sockets, and came out through the jaw or neck cracks.
In one section, the mist flowed like a narrow river on the ground and avoided contact with the black chains.
This behavior could be reacting to mana, living creatures, or an unknown force.
The black chains were also different. Some still looked completely intact.
Their links remained on the bones without rust or cracks, but in places where the chains were broken, extensive destruction was seen.
Ribs were crushed in the middle, the ground was split, and bone fragments were thrown hundreds of meters away.
Lian drew a simple conclusion from this sign. Whatever had once been chained by these chains had not necessarily remained dead.
"I would like to know what happened here. It looks like it was a very big battle." He then whispered quietly.
Even imagining what had caused the formation of the Giants’ Graveyard was not easy, but he was sure it had been a battle, a very big battle.
"So this place was formed because of a battle? But a battle between who? Giants and giants?" Seris also looked at the graveyard.
"I doubt it. From the patterns, it seems the conflict was between giants and one person." Even he himself could barely accept the words he had just spoken.
"You mean one person alone created such a graveyard of such powerful giants? How powerful must they have been?" The silver-haired girl also seemed amazed.
"Whoever it was, they had at least the power of awakened ones who have passed four evolutions." Lian was also not sure.
Was it the work of one of this world’s natives? Or someone belonging to the Ruined Realm? There was no information to reason with.
But he was sure it was the work of one person, and it was clear whoever it was had a great hatred for giants to have done such a thing to them.
Seris stood silently beside him. Her thoughts were not discernible, but from her eyes, it was clear she was also amazed.
"Hmm?" Both stood still for a few moments, and then a sound was heard from beneath the valley.
Very weak, not regular, but repeating.
Not like a heartbeat, more like a massive mass being dragged under the soil and bones.
"Did you hear that?"
Lian nodded.
"Yeah." He kept his gaze on the valley floor.
"Something is moving under the bones."
One was restless behind them. Its antennae kept trembling, and its jaws were clicking together with a quiet sound.
Lian placed his hand on the armored plate beside its head and checked its condition through Hive Link.
One’s fear did not come from a specific point, not the sitting giant, not the mist, not one of the skeletons, but as if the entire valley felt wrong to it.
As if the entire Giants’ Graveyard had a smell that made living creatures’ instincts force them to flee.
Lian initially thought of leaving One at the edge of the valley, but this decision was not practical. Grave Mimics could infiltrate its body.
Leaving it alone in an environment where the paths changed was more dangerous than bringing it along.
He checked the Rib Passage path again on the map. The width of most of its sections was enough for One’s body.
Only a few narrow gaps existed that could be bypassed through side paths.
He kept his hand on the ant’s armor and sent a clear command through Hive Link.
"Don’t eat any corpses."
One opened its jaws slightly. A brief confusion passed through the link. For a creature like it, enemies’ corpses were a source of food and growth.
But Lian sent the command more firmly. No corpses, no bones, and no creature from inside the graveyard should be eaten!
The reason was clear. The corpses might be infected by parasitic monsters or something similar, and eating them could cause that thing to spread to One as well.
He closed the map.
"Before entering, you both need to follow a few rules..." He looked at the girl and the ant and said seriously.

sentences.text: [Status: Dormant — Awakening 2%]
The red panel remained before Lian’s view for a few seconds.
In the distance, the sitting giant was still motionless.
A massive skeleton that even in a sitting position cast a shadow like a broken white mountain over the entire Giants’ Graveyard.
Its shattered crown remained on its skull, and the sword that had passed through its chest looked more like a black tower than a weapon from this distance.
Massive chains were wrapped around its neck, shoulders, arms, and legs.
Some links were intact, some were broken, and their remaining ends disappeared among the valley’s bones.
But the giant itself did not move again.
Only that one finger had shifted slightly a few moments ago.
Or perhaps something inside it had moved.
Seris stood next to Lian, her black eyes not leaving the massive skeleton.
Unlike One, which had been anxious from the moment they approached the valley, there was no fear or hesitation in Seris’s gaze.
A spark of interest and calm excitement had formed in her eyes.
"Finally, we found something interesting."
"No.
We found something we shouldn’t get close to right now." Lian answered without taking his eyes off the giant.
"Are you scared?"
Lian gave a brief look at her this time.
"No." Then he stared at the giant again.
"I know the difference between courage and stupidity." He was sure this thing was an Unholy, and although he would also like to face and fight such a monster, he knew now was not the time.
First, the chance of their death was certain, and second, his main goal right now was reaching his first evolution, which he was not far from.
Maybe after his first evolution, he could face an Unholy.
Seris said nothing because she also knew this was true.
Facing such a monster would be suicide.
Lian checked the panel again.
[Status: Dormant — Awakening 2%]
The percentage had not changed.
A few minutes passed.
The gray mist moved over the valley’s bones, and white dust fell from some of the massive ribs.
The distant sound of something rubbing in the valley’s depth was heard, but the percentage still remained at two, and this point was important for Lian.
If the creature was truly awakening, there should be a clear process.
One percent.
Two percent.
Three percent.
But since the panel was first seen, no other change had occurred.
The first possibility was that their entry had only caused a brief reaction.
The second possibility was the destruction of the Grave Mimics.
Perhaps the death of those creatures had stimulated part of the graveyard’s network, and the system had recorded that reaction as Awakening.
The third possibility was more unpleasant.
The panel might not show the giant’s own status at all.
Perhaps something was sleeping inside its bones, a sealed creature or a remnant of a power that had been buried with this giant thousands of years ago.
The last possibility was that the giant was completely dead, and the system had simply mistaken the activation of residual energy in its corpse for awakening.
But each of the possibilities had their own flaws and illogicalities.
He himself was somewhat sure that killing those monsters had stimulated this giant’s awakening.
And this meant that killing monsters might affect this monster’s awakening, a point he had to keep in mind.
"It’s remained on two percent." Lian said under his breath.
"So?" Seris asked.
"So as long as it doesn’t go higher, we ignore it.
The silver-haired girl looked at the giant again.
"If it goes higher?"
"Then we decide again." Lian’s answer was simple, but it was the right decision.
They had not come to the Giants’ Graveyard to fight a creature whose Level could not even be detected by the system.
Their goal was to cross the valley and reach Glassthorn Forest.
Anything else was only worth it if the risk was manageable.
Lian took out the complete map from his storage space and spread it on a relatively flat rock.
The strands inside the map lit up upon contact with the air.
The valley was not just one large depression.
It had several layers, high paths on ribs and spinal columns, deep gaps between skeletons, tunnels passing through skulls and hollow bones.
And areas marked with red and black signs.
The main path to Glassthorn Forest consisted of three parts.
First, the Rib Passage, a path between the ribs of a dead giant that led from the northern edge of the graveyard to the lower level of the valley.
After that, the Hollow Spine, a path passing through the hollow spinal column of a massive creature and bypassing the central part of the graveyard.
And finally, the Crystal Wound, a crack in the valley’s eastern wall where the crystalline mist and cold of Glassthorn entered the graveyard.
There was also a direct path, a shorter line that passed almost through the valley’s center, but that direct path passed under the sitting giant’s skeleton.
Lian followed the path with his finger.
"The direct path passes under it."
"It’s shorter." Seris gave a brief look at the map.
Lian pointed at the chains around the giant.
"And whatever is chained up like that probably has a good reason, and we’re not going to find out by trying."
He chose the longer path.
The Rib Passage.
Moving from the north of the valley, bypassing the sitting giant’s skeleton, entering the Hollow Spine, and then moving toward the Crystal Wound.
The path was longer, but it kept more distance from the main threat.
Lian did not close the map.
Before entering, he decided not to trust only the drawn lines.
He checked the bottom from the cliff’s edge.
At first glance, the valley was nothing but a sea of bones, mist, and giant ruins.
But when he looked without moving for a few minutes, the patterns became clear.
The black spots they had seen from a distance the day before were still moving on some bones.
They looked like insects, but their dimensions were much larger than what they had seemed at first glance.
The strange thing was that none of them approached a few specific skeletons.
On the western rib, the black spots moved forward to an invisible border and then changed their path.
The same behavior was seen around a horned skull.
Lian concluded that those empty areas were not necessarily safe.
They might be heavily contaminated or the territory of a stronger creature.
In some parts of the valley floor, crushed bones and small carcasses were scattered everywhere.
But a few long and narrow paths looked completely clean, with no bone pieces or monster remains on them.
At first glance, they seemed the best way to move, but he looked more carefully.
The edges of the paths were not smooth.
The crushed bones had been pushed to the sides.
As if something massive regularly passed through there and pushed aside any obstacle.
Lian marked those paths in his mind as danger lines.
The gray mist also did not behave naturally.
The wind blew from north to south, but the mist moved against the wind in some places.
It gathered around a few skulls, entered through the eye sockets, and came out through the jaw or neck cracks.
In one section, the mist flowed like a narrow river on the ground and avoided contact with the black chains.
This behavior could be reacting to mana, living creatures, or an unknown force.
The black chains were also different.
Some still looked completely intact.
Their links remained on the bones without rust or cracks, but in places where the chains were broken, extensive destruction was seen.
Ribs were crushed in the middle, the ground was split, and bone fragments were thrown hundreds of meters away.
Lian drew a simple conclusion from this sign.
Whatever had once been chained by these chains had not necessarily remained dead.
"I would like to know what happened here.
It looks like it was a very big battle." He then whispered quietly.
Even imagining what had caused the formation of the Giants’ Graveyard was not easy, but he was sure it had been a battle, a very big battle.
"So this place was formed because of a battle?
But a battle between who?
Giants and giants?" Seris also looked at the graveyard.
"I doubt it.
From the patterns, it seems the conflict was between giants and one person." Even he himself could barely accept the words he had just spoken.
"You mean one person alone created such a graveyard of such powerful giants?
How powerful must they have been?" The silver-haired girl also seemed amazed.
"Whoever it was, they had at least the power of awakened ones who have passed four evolutions." Lian was also not sure.
Was it the work of one of this world’s natives?
Or someone belonging to the Ruined Realm?
There was no information to reason with.
But he was sure it was the work of one person, and it was clear whoever it was had a great hatred for giants to have done such a thing to them.
Seris stood silently beside him.
Her thoughts were not discernible, but from her eyes, it was clear she was also amazed.
"Hmm?" Both stood still for a few moments, and then a sound was heard from beneath the valley.
Very weak, not regular, but repeating.
Not like a heartbeat, more like a massive mass being dragged under the soil and bones.
"Did you hear that?"
Lian nodded.
"Yeah." He kept his gaze on the valley floor.
"Something is moving under the bones."
One was restless behind them.
Its antennae kept trembling, and its jaws were clicking together with a quiet sound.
Lian placed his hand on the armored plate beside its head and checked its condition through Hive Link.
One’s fear did not come from a specific point, not the sitting giant, not the mist, not one of the skeletons, but as if the entire valley felt wrong to it.
As if the entire Giants’ Graveyard had a smell that made living creatures’ instincts force them to flee.
Lian initially thought of leaving One at the edge of the valley, but this decision was not practical.
Grave Mimics could infiltrate its body.
Leaving it alone in an environment where the paths changed was more dangerous than bringing it along.
He checked the Rib Passage path again on the map.
The width of most of its sections was enough for One’s body.
Only a few narrow gaps existed that could be bypassed through side paths.
He kept his hand on the ant’s armor and sent a clear command through Hive Link.
"Don’t eat any corpses."
One opened its jaws slightly.
A brief confusion passed through the link.
For a creature like it, enemies’ corpses were a source of food and growth.
But Lian sent the command more firmly.
No corpses, no bones, and no creature from inside the graveyard should be eaten!
The reason was clear.

chapters.title: Chapter 239: The Graveyard Of Giants IV
paragraphs: "First, none of us follow familiar sounds."
Seris looked at him.
"Second, we don’t touch corpses unless necessary for examination."
"Third, we don’t take any bones, weapons, or items without identifying them first." He looked at the mist below the valley.
"Fourth, we don’t get more than a few meters apart from each other."
"Fifth, if the mist behaves abnormally, we retreat without argument."
He pointed at One with his hand.
"Sixth, it doesn’t eat anything." And finally he said.
"If the path changes, we trust the signs we leave ourselves, not just the map."
Seris was silent for a few moments.
"You talk too much." She then said.
"Because you usually act first and ask questions later." Lian gave a faint smile.
"It works." The young Pendragon shrugged and said.
"Besides, I haven’t found anything yet that can’t be solved by attacking it." Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt.
Lian looked at the sitting giant in the valley’s center.
"There is one there."
"It’s asleep for now."
"Better to keep it that way."
They began to move. The northern slope of the valley was covered with gray rocks, bone fragments, and white soil.
One descended slowly, its six legs checking the surface before each step.
Lian moved ahead, and Seris was slightly behind him. As they descended, the giant ribs on both sides of the path grew taller.
From above, they only looked like large bones, but at the valley floor, they resembled the pillars of an abandoned temple.
Each rib was dozens of meters tall, their upper parts disappearing in the mist. The surfaces of some were smooth and white.
Some were covered with deep cracks, and scratches could be seen on them, the depth of each being the size of a human arm.
There were also holes in various parts.
Some were small, and some were so large that One could crawl inside them.
Writings in an unknown script were carved on a few ribs.
Curved and angular lines that resembled neither the Lacerian language nor earthly scripts.
Parts of the bones were covered with dry black spots. In some places, thinner and decayed chains hung between two ribs.
The floor of the Rib Passage was covered with bone dust.
Every step One took created a white cloud in the air. Lian initially thought the weak airflow was moving the powder.
But then he noticed that part of the white soil was moving against the direction of their steps.
Not on the entire path, but only at a point a few meters ahead. The powder’s surface slowly rose, then fell, rose again, exactly like the ribcage of a creature breathing underground.
"Stop." Lian immediately raised his hand.
One stopped, and Seris looked at the spot.
"We go around it."
They changed their path and crossed over a piece of broken rib.

A few seconds later, that same part of the ground collapsed. The bone powder was pulled like water into a deep hole. A massive mouth opened from beneath it, with circular and multi-layered jaws covered with hundreds of thin teeth.
The mouth bit the air for a moment. When it found nothing, it sank back under the soil.
The bone powder fell over it, and the ground surface almost returned to its original state.
"Did you see it?" Seris looked at the spot.
"Not completely." Lian answered, his eyes remaining on the now-calm soil surface.

"But whatever it was, it was lying in ambush under the powder." With the help of Predator’s Instincts and the blood flow, he had realized something was under there, otherwise they would have been swallowed by now.
"Should we kill it?" Seris asked.
"No."
"Why?"
"Because we don’t know where its body is yet." Lian pointed at the path ahead.
"And because what we don’t need to fight is not our enemy right now."
Seris looked at him for a few moments, but did not draw her sword.
They continued. The deeper they entered the Rib Passage, the closer the black spots on the bones became.
At first, they were only unclear movements in the mist, but one of them crawled down from the rib, and its real shape became clear.
It was a four-legged and very thin creature. Its dry gray skin was stretched directly over its bones.
White and yellow plates had grown on its spine, shoulders, and legs.
Its face had no eyes, only a vertical slit from the top of its skull to the bottom of its jaw.
When its mouth opened, the two halves of its face separated, and rows of short teeth were revealed.
A panel appeared before Lian’s view.
[Bone Scavenger]
[Level: 21]
[Rank: Normal]
Another movement was seen on the right rib.
Then a third, a fourth. In less than a few seconds, more than ten Bone Scavengers appeared around the path.
But they did not attack directly. One moved on the tall rib above their heads, two creatures disappeared behind a pile of crushed bones.
Three others slowly circled behind One, and Lian followed their movement path.
"They’re blocking the retreat path."
Seris drew her sword. The sound of thin metal echoed in the dead space of the Rib Passage.
"Then let’s start."
The first Bone Scavenger jumped from above the rib, its body spinning in the air, and its jaw opening from the middle.
Seris only took one step, her sword moving in a silver line.
The creature was split in half from the middle, but instead of falling motionless, the two halves landed on the bone powder and trembled violently.
The bone plates on the path floor were pulled toward the cut flesh. Pieces of ribs and skulls stuck to the Scavenger’s body.
Dark strands reconnected the two halves.
Seris narrowed her eyes slightly. The incomplete creature tried to get up again.
Lian moved, placed his foot on the back of its skull, and delivered a direct strike.
The bone shell cracked. Inside the back of the head, a small black heart could be seen.
Lian crushed it, and the body became still at that same moment.
"Behind their heads." He looked at the remaining creatures.
"The heart, or whatever it is, is there."
Three Bone Scavengers attacked at the same time. Lian jumped over a protruding bone, and the first creature passed beneath him.
He spun in the air and struck the back of its skull with his heel. The bone plate cracked, and before the creature could regenerate, Lian destroyed the core with a second strike.
Another Bone Scavenger attacked One from the side. One opened its jaws and caught the creature’s body between them.
The jaw pressure crushed the bones. Its instinct encouraged it to swallow the carcass, but Lian’s command through Hive Link stopped it.
One threw the broken body a few meters away. The creature was still moving.
Seris passed by One, with a short cut, split the back of the skull and severed the core.
More creatures came out of the rib holes, moving on the bones without the slightest sound.
One of them ran up the tall rib.
The young Pendragon followed it up the vertical surface, her steps climbing the bone quickly.
When she reached the creature, her sword moved twice. First, she cut the back legs, and the second strike passed through the back of the skull.
The heart was broken.
Seris jumped from the rib toward the next creature without stopping. In one path, three silver lines formed.
Three Bone Scavengers fell, and Lian used the protruding bones as platforms.
With each jump, he changed his path and did not allow the creatures to surround him.
One of the Scavengers came out from behind a bone. Its vertical mouth opened, but instead of a roar, suddenly Seraphina’s voice came out of its throat.
"Lian... help me."
The voice was exact, but Lian did not even turn his head toward it.
The creature attacked, and he moved his hand forward, grabbed the upper jaw, and slammed its head to the ground with sudden force.
The bone powder scattered, and the next strike broke the heart.
Seris appeared behind two Bone Scavengers at that same moment, her sword moving in a completely straight line.
The blade passed through the back of both skulls, and both hearts broke at the same time.
The battle intensified in the narrow space of the Rib Passage. The Bone Scavengers did not have high raw power.
But their movements were fast, coordinated, and unnatural. Every time one was wounded, it would stick to the surrounding bones and form new armor on its body.
One of the creatures reached the carcass of its own kind. Its jaw opened, and it swallowed a few pieces of its body.
The broken plates on its back regrew. Lian realized at that same moment that something was wrong and shouted.
"Don’t let them eat the corpses."
Seris nodded, and a short shadow formed in the mist.
She appeared in front of the creature and passed the tip of her sword directly through its open mouth. The blade came out from the back of the skull.
The heart was destroyed.
One held the narrow entrance behind them.
Every Bone Scavenger that tried to approach from that side was thrown against the rib wall by the ant’s jaw or massive leg.
Lian grabbed the last creature near him, spun its body, and slammed the back of its skull into a sharp bone fragment.
The heart broke.
Four Bone Scavengers remained. They stood on the surrounding bones.
For a moment, none of them moved, and then they all turned their heads toward the depth of the Rib Passage at the same time.
A sharp and sudden movement, as if they had heard a sound that Lian and Seris were not yet able to hear.
Then they fled.
Not toward the surrounding cracks, all of them ran in the opposite direction of the valley’s depth.
One, while fleeing, passed over its own kind’s carcass, without even stopping to eat it.
"We didn’t cause them to flee." Lian looked at the emptied path and frowned, realizing something had happened. With the help of the powerful blood flow approaching, he realized danger was coming.
"Something is coming." Seris lowered her sword and stared into the darkness ahead, her senses also warning her of danger.
Something dangerous was approaching...

chapters.title: Chapter 240: The Graveyard Of Giants V
paragraphs: It was as if a massive blade or a heavy chain was moving through the Rib Passage.
One lowered its body.
"Keep your guard up and be careful." Lian prepared to move.
Seris gripped her sword’s hilt tighter.
Time passed... but nothing came out of the mist.
The sound came closer... then suddenly stopped.
Silence returned... a few seconds passed... then a few minutes, and no creature appeared.
"So what happened?" Seris frowned. The sense of danger and warning she had felt disappeared, as if it had never existed from the start.
"Let me see." Lian carefully moved forward. On the path’s floor, he found a deep line.
The bone powder had been pushed aside, and the stone beneath it had cracked. The mark was as wide as an arm, as if a massive blade or chain had been dragged on the ground.
The mark was fresh.
White dust was still falling from its edges. A little further ahead, a few Bone Scavengers could be seen.
Their bodies were completely crushed, reduced to piles of dry flesh and broken bones under a massive force.
He bent down next to one of them. There was no sign of biting or claws.
"Something large passes through here."
"Where is it?" Seris asked, her eyes sparkled slightly. Could they finally have an exciting battle?
"I don’t know." Lian looked at the mist and examined the deep mark again.
"But whatever crushed the Scavengers without eating them is probably not a normal predator, and for some reason, it didn’t come after us."
He couldn’t understand why a monster would give up attacking them. There could be different reasons, but he didn’t think any of his ideas were correct.

With one look, he was sure whatever had appeared and disappeared so quickly was powerful. He didn’t know how powerful, but from the blood flow he had seen, he could say it was at least level 30 or at least had that much power.
But since it had left them alone, there was nothing to do, and Lian decided to increase their speed.
Waiting to see the owner of the mark was not worth it.
"It could have been interesting." Seris was clearly not happy with this decision.
"If it shows up again, you can find out how interesting it is." Lian answered while mounting One.
"Okay." The young Pendragon sheathed her sword and also mounted the ant.

They continued on their path. Their priority was to get out of this graveyard as soon as possible and enter the other forest. Not only were there no opportunities here, but the environment was extremely dangerous.
Lian was looking for an opportunity that could help him reach level 20 as soon as possible, and he had a feeling he would find that opportunity in the next forest.
There, he might also be able to find the rest of his teammates.
In the next section of the Rib Passage, the bones became denser. The mist passed through the ribs and limited visibility.
Suddenly, they saw a sign on one of the ribs.
One stopped.
And Lian went closer to the wall. A straight line was on the bone, not a claw scratch, not a natural crack, but the mark of a blade! A shallow but controlled cut.
A few meters ahead, a torn rope was lying on the ground.
He picked it up. Its material was different from the ropes made by the tribes. This rope was stronger, more regular, and of higher quality.
This was exactly a rope from their world.
Further ahead, a broken spear was lying, and traces of dried blood could be seen on one of the ribs.
"It’s old." Seris bent down and examined it.
"Yes, but not that old." Lian nodded. This blood mark was at most from a few days ago.
If these traces were real, another group had entered the Giants’ Graveyard before them, meaning a group of awakened ones!
But the question was, were they real?
A little further ahead, a mark was carved on the wall with a blade, an arrow pointing down, and beneath it, a word in human language.
SAFE.
Lian looked at the writing for a few seconds.
"This is our language...?" Seris’s eyebrows also rose.
"Yeah." Lian examined the surroundings of the mark. The blade’s effect looked natural and real. The depth of the letters was not uniform.
In the lower part, the writer’s hand had probably trembled. But the Graveyard had already shown sounds that were not real.
Its creatures had imitated the faces of familiar people. This area might not only imitate sounds and appearances.
It might have the ability to create signs that seemed strange, familiar, or hopeful to its victims.
Lian’s guess was that the graveyard could show things that didn’t logically belong there, but they were so real that they couldn’t be easily distinguished.
He doubted another group of awakened ones had entered here.
They were probably seeing things that seemed strange but hopeful to them, and this was exactly what the graveyard showed its guests.
If his guess was correct, then he had understood the mechanism of the graveyard and the illusions they were hearing and seeing, and how they worked.
These illusions probably came from the mist, and the monsters living in this graveyard had the ability to use this mist.
The mist could force their minds to show them things that were hopeful, worrying, or terrifying for them.
Things that, if they saw or heard them, would activate and trigger their sense of danger. Hearing the voices of loved ones was naturally worrying for Lian.
And likewise, now seeing items that could belong to awakened ones could also be worrying for both him and Seris, and make them wonder what had happened to them?
This reality was a lie that their brains were showing them, and Lian guessed that probably someone or something wanted to pull them toward a specific direction.
But he and Seris are not ordinary people. Their Spirit power is high enough that illusions cannot fool them or disrupt their minds.
"Should we follow it?" Seris asked.
"Not directly. I guess it wants to waste our time or pull us to a specific point." Lian answered.
"So we ignore it? Isn’t it better to just follow it? We’ll find out if it’s real or not. If it’s a monster’s work, I’ll break it." The silver-haired girl added.

chapters.title: Chapter 241: The Graveyard Of Giants VI
paragraphs: Lian nodded, he agreed too.
He checked the direction of the arrow. The blood trail continued in that direction, but there were no clear footprints.
He decided to follow the path from a distance, not on the straight line of the sign, but parallel to it, from a higher part of the bones.
If there was a trap, he preferred to see it from outside.
About half an hour later, they reached a broken skull.
The upper part of the skull had collapsed, and one of the eye sockets was left open like the entrance to a large cave.
The SAFE sign pointed exactly toward it.
One did not approach the entrance. Through Hive Link, discontent and fear intensified again.
Lian got down from it.
"Stay here." He commanded it not to touch anything and to warn him through the link if it felt any movement.
Seris stood at the entrance. The inside of the skull was dark.
Lian took out a light crystal. The white light revealed the interior, and there were traces of an old camp there.
The remains of a dead fire in the center, a few dried food packages, a piece of bloody cloth.
A broken sword, and lines drawn on the ground to divide the guard posts.
At first glance, the camp could have belonged to a group of Awakened ones, but upon closer inspection, the differences became clear.
The food packages were made of compressed leaves and animal skin. The broken sword was not metal; it was made of black bone.
The patterns carved on the handle also belonged to the Lizardman tribes.
Lian bent down next to one of the packages. A small mark was on its knot, three broken lines on a red background.
The symbol of the Varkesh.
"It’s not humans’."
Seris looked at the items.
"It was one of the Varkesh groups."
Probably the same groups that had been sent to explore the Giants’ Graveyard years or generations ago and never returned.
The traces of at least six people were in the camp. Six sleeping spots, six containers, and six separate marks for placing weapons.
This was probably a real camp.
But no skeletons or corpses could be seen, not even signs of intense conflict.
A few items were on the ground, the food was half-opened, a stone cup was overturned next to the wall.
As if everyone in the camp had gotten up at the same moment and disappeared without taking anything.
"They probably stayed here for the night to rest, but something happened to them." Lian added and frowned.
Why did the signs lead them here? Why did it seem like someone wanted to pull them here?
What exactly had happened to the Varkesh? What had they encountered?
And what exactly was this place?
Seris looked at the inner wall of the skull. The walls gave her a very bad feeling, as if they were watching her.
A weak sound was heard.
Tap.
Both fell silent, and a few seconds later again.
Tap.
Tap.
The sound came from inside the bone, not from behind the skull, not from the ceiling, but from inside the wall itself.
As if someone was trapped inside the thick bone tissue and gently knocking.
"Did you hear it too?"
"It could be the sound of the wind?"
"I doubt it."
Lian looked at the entrance. The daylight outside had decreased rapidly.
It shouldn’t have been evening yet, but the mist had become thicker and was swallowing the valley’s gray light. The map showed that the next open space was far away.
The eye socket of this same skull was the only area that was apparently protected from several directions.
Lian didn’t want to camp inside it. Every instinct told him this place was not safe, but continuing in the thick mist also had its own risks.
He decided to stop only for a few minutes. Not to rest. Just to check their equipment and understand what had happened to the Varkesh group.
One remained outside the entrance, and Seris examined the inner parts.
Lian looked at the items one by one. On the handle of the broken sword, a name was carved in the old Varkesh language.
Part of it was not readable, but the military insignia next to the name showed that the weapon’s owner was probably the group’s commander.
The same tribal symbol was also on the bloody cloth. No doubt remained, this camp belonged to one of the Varkesh groups.
But none of the people from this group were there.
No bones, no bodies, and not even armor pieces. They had completely disappeared.
Lian looked at the guard lines on the ground. One of the lines stopped near the wall.
Next to it, a few scratch marks could be seen, as if someone had tried to pull themselves back on the ground.
But the scratches went straight to the skull’s wall and ended there.
He went closer and placed his hand on the bone. At first, he felt nothing.
The surface was cold, dry, and hard. Then the wall contracted very gently, a weak movement like the skin of an animal whose muscle beneath it twitched.
Lian did not immediately pull his hand back. He waited a few seconds, and the contraction repeated.
"It moved." Seris also noticed.
Lian stepped back. Very thin lines opened on the skull’s surface, like veins appearing under the skin.
A weak black light flowed through them, from the bottom of the wall to the ceiling and then spread around.
A panel appeared before Lian’s view.
[Unknown Colossal Remains]
[Condition: Dead]
[Secondary Condition: Occupied]
Lian narrowed his eyes, his gaze fixed on the last word.
Occupied.
Something was present inside these remains. Not necessarily the soul of the skeleton’s owner, not the giant itself, but another creature using this corpse as a home, nest, or body.
"Now I understand what this place is." Lian said slowly.
"This is a monster’s lair. The Varkesh camped here but didn’t know this place had an owner, and they were killed by that same owner."
"Probably the same monster we felt a few hours ago, the one that killed those Bone Scavengers, but left us alone."
"And that monster wanted to pull us here, because it clearly thought we were dangerous and wanted to face us here, in its own lair, where it has the advantage, to make sure it could kill us..."
Suddenly, both of their senses of danger peaked!
Seris drew her sword, and at that same moment, the knocking sounds stopped.
The tapping inside the bone suddenly went silent. Complete silence ruled over the skull’s space.
Lian and Seris both remained motionless.
"Welcome to my home." Then a voice said from behind them... exactly like Lian’s voice!
Exactly the same tone, the same inflection, and the same short pause between words!
Both turned around at the same time.
At the entrance of the eye socket, someone was standing.
The height... the hair... the armor... the face, and even the blue band tied around the wrist... everything looked like Lian!
But its smile was too wide, the corners of its mouth stretched almost to its cheeks.
Its eyes did not blink, and beneath the skin of its face, something like white strands was moving slowly.
The creature tilted its head slightly, and its smile grew wider, as if it was happily looking at its new prey.
"It looks exactly like you." Seris looked at the old Lian and the new Lian.
The resemblance was too strong!
And a new panel appeared before both of their views.
[Grave Doppelgänger]
[Level: 25]
[Rank: Fallen]

chapters.title: Chapter 242: The Graveyard Of Giants VII
paragraphs: [Grave Doppelgänger]
[Level: 25]
[Rank: Fallen]
The creature that had stolen Lian’s face was standing at the broken entrance of the skull.
The white light of the crystal fell on its face, revealing every detail with irritating clarity.
Black hair, eyes, armor, posture, and even the blue band that Nemi had tied around Lian’s wrist at farewell could be seen on the creature’s wrist.
The imitation was almost perfect, but only almost.
An overly wide smile was stretched across its face. The corners of its mouth extended almost to its cheeks, and the skin around its lips was stretched unnaturally.
The creature did not blink. Thin white strands were crawling beneath the skin of its face.
Every few seconds, part of its cheek or neck would twitch; as if something inside the fake body was still learning how to use the muscles.
It tilted its head slightly, a movement Lian sometimes made when examining enemies, but the fake version had imitated it too precisely and calculatedly.
"Which one do you think is real?" It said in Lian’s voice and looked at Seris.
His voice echoed in the hollow space of the skull, no different from Lian’s real voice.
The same calm tone, the same rhythm, and even the same coldness that was in his voice when threatening enemies.
Seris drew her sword without a moment’s hesitation and pointed its tip at the creature.
"You. You are uglier."
"Uglier? Does that mean I’m ugly too?" Lian gave her a brief look.
"I didn’t say that." The silver-haired girl refused to answer.
The Grave Doppelgänger’s smile widened for a moment. Its teeth looked exactly like human teeth, but there were too many of them.
"Anyway, that’s the bastard that pulled us here. It has high intelligence and can even talk, so we need to be careful." The young Vorhelm said.
The fact that it had been able to plot against them showed it had intelligence, and a monster with intelligence was always dangerous.
Lian was still examining it when the creature moved.
The bone powder beneath its feet exploded, and its body faded for a fraction of a second, leaving a white and gray shadow in the skull’s space.
Its movement pattern was familiar, too familiar, similar to the Thunder Step skill, but not the real version. No thunder was heard, and no blue or white lightning formed in the air.
Only bone powder, gray mist, and white strands remained at its previous point.
It was clear it still couldn’t fully copy the skill.
The creature appeared right in front of Lian, a bone blade had come out of its forearm, and the strike went directly toward Lian’s neck.
"Only one of us can exist! Die, you fake!" The monster shouted.
Lian raised his forearm, a heavy impact sound echoed inside the skull. The impact pressure was more than what he expected from a level 25 creature.
Lian’s foot slid a few centimeters back on the bone powder, and the bone blade created a shallow line on his forearm.
The creature immediately turned its wrist and sent a second strike from a different angle. Its movement resembled Lian’s fighting style.
The first strike was to test the defense, and the second was to target a point that had opened for a moment.
Lian moved his head aside, the blade passed by his face, and at that same moment, the creature’s knee came toward his stomach.
He placed his palm on its thigh and deflected the strike’s path, grabbing its blade-wielding wrist with his other hand.
The creature paused in front of him for a moment, its face still smiling.
"You call me fake, you bastard?" Lian increased the pressure of his fingers.
Under the fake skin, he didn’t feel a natural bone structure, but several black, joint-like pieces connected by moist strands.
This was not a human body. It was only something that had covered itself in human shape.
The creature suddenly bent its elbow in the opposite direction, and the dry sound of bone cracking was heard.
But instead of feeling pain, its hand twisted like a loose rope from between Lian’s fingers and came out.
The joint locked again in another place, and the Grave Doppelgänger stepped back a few meters with an irregular movement.
Lian kept his gaze on it. In those few seconds, he had gathered enough information.
The creature had not only imitated his appearance, it had also stolen part of his physical power, attack rhythm, movements, and perhaps his decision-making pattern.
But it was still incomplete. It was too reliant on imitation, and it performed some movements without understanding their reason.
Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly. Based on this short exchange of strikes, he could say that every second that passed, the creature learned more from his movements.
So time was on the enemy’s side.
If the battle dragged on, it might learn to imitate more dangerous skills.
It might not only steal his movements, but perhaps also extract memories, emotions, or information from his mind.
"It looks like a very powerful skill." Lian’s eyes sparkled. This was probably one of the best skills he had ever seen.
Of course, he doubted it was just a skill. It might be this monster’s talent.
The Grave Doppelgänger moved again.

This time, it made three consecutive displacements. At the first point, a white shadow remained; at the second, thin strands rose from the ground; and at the third movement, its body completely disappeared from normal view.
Lian, with the help of Predator’s Instincts, tried to track the monster’s blood flow, and the creature’s blood appeared in a dark and contaminated form in the mist.
The fake version appeared behind Lian and sent its bone blade toward his spine.
This time, Lian did not defend.
[Diamond Skin]
His skin took on a metallic shine at the moment of impact. The bone blade broke with a loud sound on his back.
Cracks ran along the fake weapon.
The Grave Doppelgänger paused for a fraction of a second, and that was enough.
Lian turned, grabbed its wrist, placed his front foot between the creature’s legs.
Then he activated Iron Fortress Charge at a very short distance.
Explosive pressure gathered in his entire body, and his shoulder hit the creature’s chest.
Both moved toward the skull’s wall at high speed.
The Grave Doppelgänger’s body hit the massive bone with a loud crash, the wall cracked, and white powder fell from the ceiling.
The fake body was crushed between Lian and the wall, its chest caved in.
"Now you know who’s real?" Lian said mockingly.
But the creature was still smiling, its head turned backward.
Almost a full circle, its unblinking eyes stared at Lian.
White strands came out from the crack in its chest and wrapped around Lian’s arm.
"Damn it, what the fuck are you exactly?" Lian stepped back before they could tighten.
The strands twisted in the air, and the Grave Doppelgänger placed its hand on the wall.
White strands came out from the bone cracks and entered its body. The crushed chest slowly returned to its original state.
"It’s connected to the wall." The young Vorhelm thought for a moment and realized a point, then looked at his teammate.
"Don’t you want to help?
Seris had been standing next to them from the start but had not entered the battle.

[Level: 25]
[Rank: Fallen]
The creature that had stolen Lian’s face was standing at the broken entrance of the skull.
The white light of the crystal fell on its face, revealing every detail with irritating clarity.
Black hair, eyes, armor, posture, and even the blue band that Nemi had tied around Lian’s wrist at farewell could be seen on the creature’s wrist.
The imitation was almost perfect, but only almost.
An overly wide smile was stretched across its face.
The corners of its mouth extended almost to its cheeks, and the skin around its lips was stretched unnaturally.
The creature did not blink.
Thin white strands were crawling beneath the skin of its face.
Every few seconds, part of its cheek or neck would twitch; as if something inside the fake body was still learning how to use the muscles.
It tilted its head slightly, a movement Lian sometimes made when examining enemies, but the fake version had imitated it too precisely and calculatedly.
"Which one do you think is real?" It said in Lian’s voice and looked at Seris.
His voice echoed in the hollow space of the skull, no different from Lian’s real voice.
The same calm tone, the same rhythm, and even the same coldness that was in his voice when threatening enemies.
Seris drew her sword without a moment’s hesitation and pointed its tip at the creature.
"You.
You are uglier."
"Uglier?
Does that mean I’m ugly too?" Lian gave her a brief look.
"I didn’t say that." The silver-haired girl refused to answer.
The Grave Doppelgänger’s smile widened for a moment.
Its teeth looked exactly like human teeth, but there were too many of them.
"Anyway, that’s the bastard that pulled us here.
It has high intelligence and can even talk, so we need to be careful." The young Vorhelm said.
The fact that it had been able to plot against them showed it had intelligence, and a monster with intelligence was always dangerous.
Lian was still examining it when the creature moved.
The bone powder beneath its feet exploded, and its body faded for a fraction of a second, leaving a white and gray shadow in the skull’s space.
Its movement pattern was familiar, too familiar, similar to the Thunder Step skill, but not the real version.
No thunder was heard, and no blue or white lightning formed in the air.
Only bone powder, gray mist, and white strands remained at its previous point.
It was clear it still couldn’t fully copy the skill.
The creature appeared right in front of Lian, a bone blade had come out of its forearm, and the strike went directly toward Lian’s neck.
"Only one of us can exist!
Die, you fake!" The monster shouted.
Lian raised his forearm, a heavy impact sound echoed inside the skull.
The impact pressure was more than what he expected from a level 25 creature.
Lian’s foot slid a few centimeters back on the bone powder, and the bone blade created a shallow line on his forearm.
The creature immediately turned its wrist and sent a second strike from a different angle.
Its movement resembled Lian’s fighting style.
The first strike was to test the defense, and the second was to target a point that had opened for a moment.
Lian moved his head aside, the blade passed by his face, and at that same moment, the creature’s knee came toward his stomach.
He placed his palm on its thigh and deflected the strike’s path, grabbing its blade-wielding wrist with his other hand.
The creature paused in front of him for a moment, its face still smiling.
"You call me fake, you bastard?" Lian increased the pressure of his fingers.
Under the fake skin, he didn’t feel a natural bone structure, but several black, joint-like pieces connected by moist strands.
This was not a human body.
It was only something that had covered itself in human shape.
The creature suddenly bent its elbow in the opposite direction, and the dry sound of bone cracking was heard.
But instead of feeling pain, its hand twisted like a loose rope from between Lian’s fingers and came out.
The joint locked again in another place, and the Grave Doppelgänger stepped back a few meters with an irregular movement.
Lian kept his gaze on it.
In those few seconds, he had gathered enough information.
The creature had not only imitated his appearance, it had also stolen part of his physical power, attack rhythm, movements, and perhaps his decision-making pattern.
But it was still incomplete.
It was too reliant on imitation, and it performed some movements without understanding their reason.
Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Based on this short exchange of strikes, he could say that every second that passed, the creature learned more from his movements.
So time was on the enemy’s side.
If the battle dragged on, it might learn to imitate more dangerous skills.
It might not only steal his movements, but perhaps also extract memories, emotions, or information from his mind.
"It looks like a very powerful skill." Lian’s eyes sparkled.
This was probably one of the best skills he had ever seen.
Of course, he doubted it was just a skill.
It might be this monster’s talent.
The Grave Doppelgänger moved again.
This time, it made three consecutive displacements.
At the first point, a white shadow remained; at the second, thin strands rose from the ground; and at the third movement, its body completely disappeared from normal view.
Lian, with the help of Predator’s Instincts, tried to track the monster’s blood flow, and the creature’s blood appeared in a dark and contaminated form in the mist.
The fake version appeared behind Lian and sent its bone blade toward his spine.
This time, Lian did not defend.
[Diamond Skin]
His skin took on a metallic shine at the moment of impact.
The bone blade broke with a loud sound on his back.
Cracks ran along the fake weapon.
The Grave Doppelgänger paused for a fraction of a second, and that was enough.
Lian turned, grabbed its wrist, placed his front foot between the creature’s legs.
Then he activated Iron Fortress Charge at a very short distance.
Explosive pressure gathered in his entire body, and his shoulder hit the creature’s chest.
Both moved toward the skull’s wall at high speed.
