chapters.title: Chapter 243: The Graveyard Of Giants VIII
paragraphs: Seris’s mana spread around her body. The space became heavier for a moment.
Just from the amount of mana being used, it was clear how angry she was at seeing a copied version of herself.
Her hand movement disappeared from view.
[Silver Requiem]
Dozens of impact sounds echoed almost simultaneously inside the skull, a sound like metal falling on glass, and every fake line was met with a real strike.
The shadows split, the bone blades cracked, and the incomplete imitation waves collapsed.
In less than a second, all of the Doppelgänger’s attacks were destroyed, but Silver Requiem did not stop there.
Several silver lines passed through the fake version’s body, and narrow cracks appeared on its neck, chest, arms, and legs.
A moment later, black blood and white strands came out of all of them.
The Grave Doppelgänger stepped back, but was still standing.
"That’s how it is." Seris lowered her sword and said with a cold tone.
The fake version lost its smile. It was clear that the monster also realized it had just been humiliated.
Then both creatures attacked at the same time. The Lian version went toward Seris, and the Seris version went toward Lian.
Their movement had a clear purpose. They did not only want to fight their originals.
They wanted to disrupt Lian and Seris’s rhythm, force them to cross each other’s attack paths in the enclosed space.
And perhaps momentarily make them confuse the real and fake versions. But Lian and Seris did not need to talk.
They knew each other’s movement rhythm.
Lian knew when Seris would shift her weight to her front foot before a strike.
Seris knew when Lian would intentionally open his defensive space to lure the enemy into his strike range.
Lian’s Grave Doppelgänger attacked Seris from above with its bone blade.
Seris stepped back half a step without looking.
Lian understood that retreat was not for escape, and now the space was open.
[Thunder Calamity]
Blue and white lightning exploded inside the skull. Lian entered the gap and slammed his fist into the fake version’s side.
The creature was thrown toward Seris.
And she turned at the same time, her sword moving from top to bottom. Lian’s version was forced to bend its body unnaturally to avoid the cut.
At the same moment, Seris’s Doppelgänger reached Lian from behind.
Lian lowered his body, the black sword passed over his head, and the real Seris, without pausing, sent a horizontal strike.
The blade passed over Lian’s head and split the fake version’s chest.
They did not act like two separate fighters. One’s movement was the continuation of the other’s. The gap Lian created became Seris’s strike path.
Seris’s defense sent the enemy to a point where Lian was already waiting.
The Doppelgängers tried to imitate their rhythm, but there was a fundamental difference.
They saw the movement, but did not understand trust.
Seris’s version stepped back a few steps and placed its hand on the wall. The surrounding bone plates began to tremble.
Pieces of the skull separated and came toward its body, placing themselves on its shoulders, chest, arms, and legs.
Within seconds, thick bone armor was formed on the fake body.
Seris attacked its chest with a direct strike. The blade split part of the armor.
But new pieces immediately filled the gap. The fake version formed a smile on its face again, and the young Pendragon lowered her sword slightly.
The mana around her changed, and the glow of King’s Edge became heavier.
Its pressure was no longer only concentrated on the blade. At the moment of contact, it was also supposed to weaken the enemy’s defense.
[King’s Breaker]
Seris took a step forward and sent a direct strike to the center of the bone armor.
At the moment of contact, a deep sound echoed in the space. The defensive plates cracked from the impact point, and the cracks spread through the entire armor.
The defense ability of the structure collapsed for a moment. Her blade, with much greater penetrating power than the bone, passed through the fake flesh and white strands.
The fake version was almost split in half. The two parts of the body remained connected only by a few white strands.
But the heart had still not been destroyed. Seris kept her gaze on the creature’s chest. The strands were most concentrated near the heart.
Unlike the Grave Mimics and Bone Scavengers, this creature’s heart was not behind the skull.
To better imitate the human body, it had placed it at a point near the heart.
On the other side, Lian’s version placed one hand on the ground. Black and white cold spread around its fingers.
The bone powder froze, and icy strands moved along the ground. Then a massive claw of dead ice formed.
Curved, unstable, and full of black cracks, an imitation of Glacial Reaper Claw.
Lian frowned for a moment. The creature was not only reconstructing his movements but also his Skills.
But the fake version had an obvious difference.
It had no cold, no control, and the mana inside it flowed chaotically and decayed. Only raw power that had been imperfectly poured into the form of his skill.
Lian raised his hand.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
Blue and white cold swirled around his arm. The temperature in the skull’s space suddenly dropped.
The bone powder on the ground froze, and cold vapor formed in the air. Transparent and long claws came out from Lian’s fingers.
Every edge shone like blue glass. The two claws collided. The fake ice did not resist even for a second. Its cracks exploded.
The claw passed through it and froze the Grave Doppelgänger’s arm from fingertip to shoulder.
The fake skin’s color turned to pale blue, and the strands beneath it stopped.
Lian wrapped his hand around the frozen arm, squeezed, and the entire arm shattered into hundreds of crystalline pieces.
The Grave Doppelgänger screamed, but the voice that came from its throat was Lian’s own voice.

His voice of pain, his broken breath. Hearing it from another creature’s mouth was momentarily disturbing even for Lian, and it made him more certain that he had to get rid of this creature as soon as possible.
The creature used that same pause.
Seris’s version, with an almost split body, suddenly appeared behind Lian.
White strands had connected the two halves of its body. Its bone sword rose, and the blade came down directly toward Lian’s neck.
He had seen the attack and could defend, but before he could move, an invisible pressure spread in the skull’s space.
No mana wave was seen, no sound was made, and only for a moment, everything became heavy.
As if a massive will had cast a shadow over the entire space. The black eyes of the real Seris lit up with a deep glow.
[Sovereign’s Judgment]
The fake version’s sword stopped a few centimeters above Lian’s neck.
The command was not reaching the body from the brain. Its will was crushed under the pressure of a spiritual force.
Sovereign’s Judgment did not target the enemy’s body.
It attacked the mind and soul, and for a few seconds, or against weaker enemies even a few minutes, it took away their ability to control their body.
Seris’s version stood like a motionless statue. Its shiny eyes were still open, but no awareness could be seen in them.
The real Seris calmly walked toward it, placing her sword on the creature’s chest.
Right on the heart’s location. Then she said with a cold voice.
"No one can be me, especially not a dirty, possessed monster." The blade moved, and King’s Edge passed through the chest like a silver line.
The black heart inside the body was split open. The fake version trembled for a moment, and then its body collapsed.
Pieces of fake flesh and bone fell on the ground. White strands came out of its remains, but instead of crawling toward the wall, they moved toward Lian’s version.
The Grave Doppelgänger opened its remaining hand. The strands entered its body, and the remains of Seris’s version dried up on the ground.
The creature’s panel changed.
[Grave Doppelgänger]
[Level: 27]
[Rank: Mutated Fallen]
Its body began to change. The right side of its hair turned silver, one of its eyes turned completely black, and half of its face was still Lian.
The other half was an incomplete imitation of Seris.
Its severed arm regrew, but not as a normal arm. A long bone blade took the place of its fingers.

In the other hand, black cold again gathered in the form of an ice claw. The creature was now a combination of both of them. The defeated abilities of the two Doppelgängers had been gathered into one body.
The smile on its half-and-half face returned. This time, its voice was also a combination. Part of the words in Lian’s voice, part in Seris’s voice.
"Now... I’m better, more complete... flawless... and stronger!"
Lian looked at the mutated creature and felt a headache... killing one of them had not only not made things easier, but had also made them harder...
"Maybe I should have tortured it before death so it wouldn’t dare to use my face again." Seris snorted coldly.

chapters.title: Chapter 244: The Graveyard Of Giants IX
paragraphs: Lian did not react specifically to Seris’s words. Instead, he put together all the information he had.
From the moment they had entered the Giants’ Graveyard, it was clear they were being watched by something. At first, he thought it might just be normal monsters.
Then he realized that was not the case, and they were being watched by even stronger monsters like these Doppelgängers.
Now he understood to some extent why monsters did not want to go near this graveyard. The monsters living in this abandoned area were not normal.
All of them had undergone changes and mutations. An example was the pseudo-immortality that all the monsters in this graveyard possessed.
As long as the thing resembling a heart inside their bodies was not destroyed, they would regenerate and return to life every time. Second, they could use the wandering mist in this abandoned area.
As he had guessed before, the mist had hallucinogenic abilities, and the monsters in this area could manipulate it.
Now the question was, what caused these changes in the area’s monsters? Was it the mist itself? Or the residual effects of the massive battle that had formed this graveyard?
He thought for a moment and then let it go. It was not like the answer to this question mattered. In the end, he just had to massacre these monsters.
Lian then looked at the Doppelgänger and then at the living walls of the skull.
If more creatures appeared and this creature absorbed them, its power would increase every moment.
Fighting the bodies was not enough. They were puppets. The main source was elsewhere.
"We need to find the main core." Lian said. If his guess was correct, these creatures were probably just copies of the real source.
This real source was what had the ability to create Doppelgängers, and it was clear that whatever it was, it must be hidden in the walls of this skull.
"Let’s finish this quickly." Seris looked at the black veins on the wall.
The combined Grave Doppelgänger attacked.
On its bone sword, mana resembling King’s Edge gathered.
Unstable but dangerous, and the ice claw simultaneously came toward Lian.
He placed his hand on the skull’s wall, controlled his mana, and this time did not release Cataclysm Pulse for complete destruction.
He sent a narrow and controlled wave into the bone.
[Cataclysm Pulse]
The mana pulse entered the wall from his palm, passed through the bone layers, and for a moment, the interior of the skull transformed in his mind into a network of lines and cavities.
Cracks, black veins, white strands, and very thin connections that went from the Grave Doppelgänger’s body into the wall’s depth.
The creature was not independent. Strands controlled it like a puppet.
Every movement, every regeneration, every imitation was connected to a larger source.
It might seem strange, but it really wasn’t. Some monsters could only make multiple copies of themselves, like clones.
And this main source they were facing could create clones of others.
Lian sent the wave deeper. Behind the inner wall of the eye socket, exactly where the quiet knocks had been heard, he felt a large mass.
A dense center of contaminated mana.
The main source!
"It’s behind the wall."
"I’ll take it." Seris raised her sword.
The combined version lunged forward to stop them, and Abyss Veil formed around Lian.
The Grave Doppelgänger wanted to attack, but for a fraction of a second, it lost its target. More precisely, the target moved so fast that it couldn’t follow its movement.
Its ice claw split the empty space.
[Thunder Step]
This time, real thunder exploded inside the skull. Blue lightning ran over the ribs and bone walls.
Lian appeared behind the creature, activated Iron Fortress Charge, and his shoulder hit the Doppelgänger’s back.
The creature was thrown across the space at high speed and slammed into the center of the skull. Before it could get up, Seris stood in front of the identified wall.
King’s Breaker was activated again.
Heavy silver mana gathered on her sword. The first strike hit the wall, and a deep sound like breaking rock was heard.
The defensive power of the bone decreased at the contact point. Black and white cracks spread on the surface.
Seris took the second step.
[Silver Requiem]
Dozens of strikes landed on the same point simultaneously, each cut exactly on the cracks from the previous strike.
The bone lost its resistance, and a large part of the wall collapsed with an explosion of white powder.
Behind it, something was revealed that bore no resemblance to the natural interior of a bone. A large mass of white strands, black bones, and semi-transparent tissues.
And several bodies that had been absorbed into it. In the center of the mass, a black and massive core was pulsing.
Each pulse created a weak wave in the wall’s veins.
Six Lizardman bodies were seen around the core.
The members of the lost Varkesh group. The tribe’s old armor was still on their bodies, and the color of their scales had faded.
But their bodies, unlike the passage of time, remained almost intact.
White strands had passed through their mouths, eyes, ears, and the cracks in their armor.
They had kept them attached to the wall. One of the bodies suddenly raised its head.
Its eyes were empty, and its jaw opened with a dry movement.
It was neither alive nor aware. The network was only moving the body like a puppet.
Now the reason for the absence of any bodies at the camp was clear. The skull had swallowed them, pulling their bodies inside the wall.
It had extracted their memories, voices, movements, and perhaps their fears.
"So it wanted to pull us here to do the same thing to us?" Seris looked at the core mockingly.
She too realized what that corrupt and strange source had been planning all along. It wanted to lure them here to use them like the Varkesh as a source of food.
She even had a guess. This thing probably became more powerful the more food sources it had to feed on, and could create more Doppelgängers.
The core sensed the danger. All the strands suddenly tightened, and the six Varkesh bodies separated from the wall. Bone and tissue tore from around them.
Their feet landed on the ground with a dry sound. One held a rotten spear, and another held a short blade.
The third moved with bare hands, but white strands were protruding from its fingers.
They all came toward Lian and Seris at the same time. Seris raised her sword.
The mana around her suddenly changed, and the space became heavy. Silver light emerged from around the blade, and its pressure even pushed the bone powder on the ground aside.
For a moment, an image of a massive blade formed above Seris’s head.
Not complete, but clear enough to feel the skill’s destructive power.
[Heavenfall Execution]
"No." Lian said immediately.
"Why?"
"You’ll collapse the whole skull on our heads."
The massive aura remained for a few seconds, and the surrounding walls developed new cracks under the mana pressure.
Then Seris canceled the skill, and the light subsided.
"Okay."

chapters.title: Chapter 245: The Graveyard Of Giants X
paragraphs: Lian did not want the entire skull to collapse, and besides.
His mana intensified, his heartbeat rose, and his power, speed, and reactions increased in an instant.
He went straight among the six puppet bodies.
Glacial Reaper Claw formed on his hand.
With the first movement, he cut one’s spear, and the second strike slammed the puppet body into the wall.
Ice spread from the impact point on the strands and slowed their movement.
The second body attacked from the side. Lian sank the claw into its chest, but there was no core inside the body.
These were only carriers. He threw the body aside and continued his path toward the core.
Seris moved on the other side. King’s Edge cut the white strands at precise points each time.
She did not destroy the bodies; she severed their connection. With each cut of a strand bundle, one of the bodies fell to the ground and became still.
The combined Grave Doppelgänger rose again.
Half of its face was broken, but it was still moving. It came toward Lian with an imitation of Thunder Step.
This time faster than before, and its bone sword moved toward Lian’s back.
Seris sent a strike without looking. The silver blade collided with the fake sword and deflected its path.
Lian took advantage of the opportunity and reached for the core.
He released Cataclysm Pulse again, but this time, he sent the wave directly into the black mass.
The core’s pulse faltered for a moment. The strands trembled, the walls contracted, and the core became unstable.
Seris covered the distance in one step. King’s Edge was concentrated on her blade.
All the force gathered at the sword’s tip. She sent a direct strike, and the blade passed through the core’s center.
For a moment, everything stopped. Then the core split in half, and a black liquid splashed from inside.
All the white strands tightened simultaneously, then fell motionless on the ground. The Varkesh bodies collapsed like puppets whose strings had been cut.
The combined Grave Doppelgänger was only a few steps away from Lian.
Its ice claw was raised, but before the attack could be completed, its body began to crumble.
The silver part of the hair turned to dust, the bone sword cracked.
The skin on its face separated, the strands fell from inside its body, and this time, nothing returned them to the wall.
The creature fell on its knee.
"I... better..." For the last time, it said in the combined voice of Lian and Seris.
Its sentence was not completed. Its body collapsed into a mass of black bone and white tissue.
The skull began to tremble. The occupying core had kept part of the structure alive.
With its death, the inner walls cracked, and parts of the ceiling collapsed.
Bone powder fell like rain.
"Outside." Lian said.
They moved at the same time.
One was waiting outside the entrance. Its anxiety intensified through Hive Link.
Lian and Seris jumped out of the eye socket, landed on One’s back, and Lian gave the command to retreat.
The ant distanced itself from the skull at full speed. A few seconds later, part of the eye socket collapsed, and massive bone pieces crashed to the ground.
A wave of white powder spread through the Rib Passage.
But the entire skeleton was not destroyed. Only the contaminated inner part had collapsed. When the tremors ended, silence once again ruled over the valley.
Lian looked toward the center of the Giants’ Graveyard.
He called up the sitting giant’s panel.
[Status: Dormant — Awakening 5%]
The awakening percentage had increased by 3 percent!
3 percent! And that was only because of killing three monsters!
They had killed dozens of monsters before this and had barely gotten a 1 percent increase, so why had it suddenly gone up by 3 percent?
Did that mean there was a specific reason? Because these were stronger? Their species was different? Or this area is different?
System notifications appeared before Lian’s view one after another.
[You have killed an Occupying Grave Core level 28.]
[The area under the occupying core’s control has been freed.]
Lian kept his gaze on the last notification. So the occupying core did not only live inside the skull.
It also affected the surrounding environment. This made him curious whether there were more monsters of this kind.
This was the first time he had seen such a thing. The occupying core itself had no combat or defensive power, but it could create clones.
Its clones were not weak either. It had been able to create two Fallen ones!
Of course, they were not as powerful as real Fallen ones. If Lian wanted to rank them, they were the weakest Fallen ones he had ever seen.
"There are probably more of these in the Giants’ Graveyard."
After the bone powder settled, Lian approached the skull’s remains again.
Seris moved beside him.
One remained outside.
The interior was almost destroyed. The white strands were dry and blackened.
The six Varkesh bodies were lying on the ground. For the first time after years or generations, their bodies had been freed from the wall.
Lian bent down next to one of the bodies. Something dark was visible under its arm.
A piece of black bone. At first, he thought it was part of the contamination, but there were regular lines and writings on its surface.
He examined it. No living flow was seen in it. There were no strands or active mana.
He carefully picked it up. The bone’s surface was divided into several sections.
Some parts were broken, some sections were contaminated by the core’s black liquid and could no longer be read.
But the writings belonged to the Varkesh.
"What is it?" Seris asked.
Lian wiped the dust off it.
"It seems to be a report."
The Varkesh group had recorded everything they had seen on the path on this bone.
Creatures, paths, dangers, points where they could stop.
Their goal was to deliver the report to the tribe upon their return and keep it in the archive.
This mission was probably one of the Varkesh’s first attempts to explore the Giants’ Graveyard in depth.
But they had never had the chance to return. Most of the writing was destroyed.
The words were incomplete, sentences were cut off in the middle, and only recognizable fragments remained.
"Creatures without eyes... inside the bones... don’t believe the sounds..."
"The chain’s trail... movement in the mist..."
But none were complete. Lian turned the bone piece. On the back side, a deeper line was carved.
Probably the last sentence one of the group members had written before death.
This part had remained more intact than the rest.
Seris moved closer to take a look as well.
Lian read the writing.
"After any bloodshed in ... when the chain sound stops, don’t move." The two looked at each other.
The chain sound...?
"What do you think it means?" Seris asked curiously.
"I have no idea. They didn’t write anything more to understand their meaning. It’s not even clear where they meant bloodshed." Lian had no opinion.
The part that said "bloodshed in" was erased in front, and it was not clear exactly where they meant.
In the end, they shook their heads and placed the bone in Lian’s storage space. There was nothing else there that caught their attention, and they left the skull.
They wanted to mount One when suddenly...
"Shhhhhhhhhhhh..."
Suddenly, both of their ears perked up, and at that same moment, a sound was heard from the depth of the Rib Passage.
The dragging of a massive metal on bone... a chain.
The sound moved calmly and regularly in the mist.
Once.
Twice.
The third time.
Lian raised his head, Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt, ready to engage again.
The chain sound continued... closer... heavier... and then suddenly stopped.

chapters.title: Chapter 246: The Chain Stops ...
paragraphs: The sound of the chain being dragged suddenly stopped.
At that same moment, a heavy and complete silence descended upon the Rib Passage.
Neither the sound of the mist moving nor the sound of bone powder falling from the massive ribs could be heard.
Not even the sound of One’s feet scraping on the ground. Lian, Seris, and One all remained in the same position.
Motionless.
Seris’s hand was on her sword’s hilt, but her fingers did not move even slightly.
One’s body beneath them remained still like a massive black statue. Only its antennae, which usually moved at the smallest change in the environment, were now completely stopped in the air.
Lian sent a clear and firm command through Hive Link.
Do not move at all, not even one step, even if something comes close to you.
One’s fear was transmitted to his mind through the link, but the ant accepted the command.
The gray mist a few meters ahead moved slowly. Something was present inside it, something very large.
But before its full shape could be revealed, a few stored system notifications appeared before Lian’s view.
He had not had the chance to check all of them during the battle inside the skull.
Now the panels, without making sound or physical movement, opened one after another before his eyes.
[You have slain Grave Doppelgänger — Mutated Lv.27.]
[You have slain multiple Bone Scavengers.]
[You have slain multiple Grave Mimics.]
[Butcher has been activated.]
[The Stats of slain creatures have been analyzed.]
[You have obtained 141 Stat Points.]
Lian kept his gaze on the remaining number.
One hundred and forty-one permanent points.
This amount had not been obtained from only one enemy. Butcher had analyzed all the monsters they had killed on the path and extracted one percent of their Stats.
The majority of the points had come from the Grave Doppelgängers, Bone Scavengers, and the occupying core.
The Grave Mimics had a smaller share, but their numbers were greater, and in total, they had added a significant amount.
Lian opened his current status.
[Strength: 618]
[Spirit: 400]
[Speed: 400]
[Mana: 910]
[Resistance: 448]
[Stat Points: 164]
With the addition of one hundred and forty-one new points, his stored points reached three hundred and five.
[Stat Points: 305]
Lian did not intend to keep them.
In an environment like the Giants’ Graveyard, storing power that could be used at that very moment was meaningless.
But he could not put all the points into only Mana or Strength.
The creature present in the mist probably would not be defeated by raw power alone.
Reaction speed, damage tolerance, and spiritual power to resist unknown abilities.
And enough Mana for continuous use of Divine Skills.
All were necessary.

[Speed increased by 65.]
[Mana increased by 55.]
[Resistance increased by 60.]

A new panel appeared.
[Strength: 693]
[Spirit: 450]
[Speed 465]
[Mana: 965]
[Resistance: 508]

Not explosive, and not so intense that he lost control, more like the compression of new force into his muscles, bones, and mana flow.
His heartbeat became deeper, his vision became clearer, and he felt the time between perceiving danger and his body’s reaction had shortened.
More mana flowed in his veins, and his body’s resistance to environmental pressure increased.
But no excitement appeared on his face. The chain sound had stopped only moments before.
In such a situation, even a small movement could be deadly.
He now understood what the Varkesh warning meant, and he wanted to take it seriously, especially because he felt a powerful blood flow in the mist.
A blood flow even stronger than the Doppelgängers.
The next notification appeared.
[Glutton has successfully devoured three Skills.]
Three panels opened one after another.
The first skill came from the Grave Doppelgänger.
[Echo Adaptation]
[Rank: Common (+)]
[By observing an enemy’s movements, the user gradually analyzes their combat rhythm and predicts repeated patterns.]
[The longer you observe a target, the more accurately you can recognize and anticipate its repeated movements.]
[Current Limitation: Only one primary target may be fully analyzed at a time.]
Lian quickly reviewed the text. At its current rank, the skill could not copy the enemy’s Skill.
It only analyzed patterns, movement rhythms, and repetitions in fighting style. But even that was very valuable.
In long battles, every time the enemy repeated a movement, the chance of predicting the next move increased.
Against fighters with chaotic patterns or enemies with a huge power gap, the skill was more limited.
However, combining it with his own knowledge could create a very dangerous result, although that itself was not something to be ignored.
Lian stared at the rank section for a moment.
Common.
Only the first level.
If this Skill, like his other skills, had the potential to grow to Divine, its final form would probably be far beyond predicting movements.
Perhaps at Divine rank, it could do what the Grave Doppelgängers did.
Not just recognizing the rhythm of a skill, but creating a real version of it.
Even if copying an enemy’s Skill completely was impossible, the ability to temporarily reconstruct its structure alone would be an extraordinary power.
The Doppelgängers, in the middle of battle, could create weaker versions of skills they saw and use them. He was sure that when this skill reached Divine rank, he could do the same.
So even though it was useless at its current rank, at Divine rank, it could be significantly useful.
The second panel opened.
[False Presence]
[Rank: Common (+)]
[Creates a temporary false presence carrying the user’s voice, scent, and weak mana signature. Each one costs 25 mana.]
This Skill had been obtained from the Grave Mimics.
Lian could not create a physical body or a complete Doppelgänger, but he could create a false presence within a close range.
Voice, smell, a weak mana trace, and even the sound of footsteps heard from another point.
The false presence only lasted a few seconds and would collapse upon direct contact or the first attack.
Creatures with very high Perception might notice the difference, but in combination with Abyss Veil, its true value became clear.
Lian could hide his real presence and simultaneously leave a fake trace in another location.
In battle against an enemy that hunted based on sound, smell, or Mana Signature, this Skill could change the outcome of the fight.

Besides, this was only the lowest rank. When it reached Divine rank... maybe it could create clones of himself? Although he doubted they would be at the level of the Doppelgängers, even these clones could be helpful in many situations.
The third skill came from the Bone Scavengers.
[Ossuary Armor]
[Rank: Common (+)]
[Nearby compatible bones may be shaped into disposable defensive plates.]
[The armor’s strength depends on the quality, density, and condition of the consumed bone material.]
[Consumes 0.9 mana per minute.]
Unlike Diamond Skin, this Skill did not harden Lian’s body. Unlike Solar Forge Aegis, it also did not create a permanent or massive armor of solar fire and magma.
Ossuary Armor was an environmental tool. It absorbed nearby bones and turned them into temporary armor.
It could cover only one part of the body.
The forearm, shoulder, leg, or even form as a multi-layered shield against a strike.
The armor would shatter after absorbing an attack, and its quality depended directly on the bones used.
In an environment like this graveyard, the raw materials were almost unlimited.
Lian assessed the value of all three skills in a few seconds.
Ossuary Armor would be useful in this environment, and even outside it, it still had many uses.
Echo Adaptation would become one of his best analytical skills for long battles.
But in the current situation, False Presence had the most immediate value.
The Varkesh warning was still repeating in his mind. When the chain sound stops, do not move.
If the creature in the mist sensed movement, a false presence might be able to change its path.
But Lian had not yet activated the Skill.
First, he had to confirm the rule and see exactly what they were dealing with.
The mist slowly moved aside. A massive shadow appeared among the giant ribs.
At first, only its legs were visible. Long, bony legs, each made from several bones belonging to different creatures. Its knees were at a height taller than One’s height.
Black strands and thin chains held the bones together.
Then its torso emerged from the mist. The creature was about eighteen meters tall.
It was very thin. Its ribcage was made of a collection of irregular ribs, and among them, no heart or natural organ could be seen.
Black chains were wrapped several times around its chest, neck, and shoulders.
Some links were sunk into the bone, some passed through the body and came out from the other side.
Its head was almost human, but it had no eyes. The surface of its face was flat and white.

Lian, Seris, and One all remained in the same position.

chapters.title: Chapter 247: The Warden’s Rule
paragraphs: There was only a vertical slit in place of the creature’s mouth.
A few chain links passed through its jaw and connected the head to the neck.
In its right hand was a massive blade, its wide and rusted edge was being dragged on the ground, creating a deep mark in the bone powder.
In its other hand, it held the end of a thick chain that disappeared into the mist behind it.
It was unclear where the other end was attached. Pieces of skeletons and crushed bodies hung from the chains around its body.
With every step, those remains would collide with each other, but now the creature stood motionless.
Because the chain sound had stopped.
A panel opened before Lian’s view.
[Chainbound Ossuary Warden]
[Level: 40]
[Rank: Normal]
Level 40 but Normal rank.
Defeating such a creature was not impossible. Both Lian and Seris had enough power to fight it.
After all, it was only a Normal rank monster. If they were willing to put everything on the line, they might even be able to win.
But the issue was not only power. Fighting among thousands of skeletons, parasites, and hidden creatures could trigger the entire graveyard.
If the noise woke the sitting giant or whatever was moving under the bones, victory against the Warden would be meaningless.
And more importantly, victory would not be easy. They would have to use everything they had, forced to use all their trump cards.
The creature’s faceless head slowly turned toward them.
Seris even shortened her breath.
One remained completely still.
The chains hanging from the Warden’s body trembled slightly. The creature seemed to be listening to the surrounding space.
But not with ears. A weak wave of Mana came out of its ribcage and spread across the ground.
Lian saw it. The wave passed through the bones, checking every small vibration, every movement, and every mana fluctuation.
So physical movement was not the only thing that mattered. Even suddenly releasing a Skill could attract its attention.
A few seconds passed.
The Warden found nothing. Its head turned back to its previous direction.
Its foot moved, the heavy blade was dragged on the bones again, and the chain sound returned.
Lian immediately gave the command for slow movement through Hive Link.
One took only one step.
Then the second step.
The Warden showed no reaction.
So the Varkesh report’s rule was probably correct. As long as the chain sound was heard, movement was allowed.
But Lian still needed more confirmation. He did not know exactly what they were dealing with, what skills it had, and what exactly it was.
At that same moment, a Bone Scavenger came out from among the bones on the right side.
The gray creature was moving on four legs.
It was probably aware of the Warden’s presence, but to reach a carcass on that side of the path, it had been forced to cross the open territory.
The chain was still being dragged on the ground.
The Bone Scavenger ran.
The Warden did not even turn its head toward it. The sound of metal suddenly stopped.
The Bone Scavenger did not notice the change. It took another step.
The Warden’s head turned toward it with a sharp movement at that same moment. The giant creature disappeared.
Not literally, but its speed was so high that its eighteen-meter body only left an elongated shadow in the mist.
A massive impact shook the Rib Passage, and bone powder was thrown into the air.
When the mist and white dust cleared, the Bone Scavenger was no longer there. Only a spot of gray flesh and crushed bone plates remained under the Warden’s blade.
The creature pulled the blade out of the ground. Without eating or even looking at the carcass, it returned to its previous path.
The chain was dragged again.
Lian was now sure. Movement during silence invited death.
They moved. One moved forward with short and controlled steps, and Lian and Seris remained on its back.
He was checking the path ahead.
The mist, the gaps, the bone powder, and more importantly, the Warden’s movement. The chain sound was not regular. Sometimes it would continue for ten seconds.
Sometimes it would stop after only two steps.
The first time, Lian gave the stop command only upon hearing the change in sound.
One stopped right before the silence.
The Warden stopped at a distance, its perception wave passed over them.
Then it moved again.
The second time, the movement distance was shorter.
One took only four steps.
The sound stopped.
This time, one of its front legs was still a few centimeters above the ground, but Lian’s command had arrived before the foot came down.
One maintained that position, its body trembling under the pressure, but it did not lower its foot.
The Warden passed through the mist.
Its distance from them was less than ten meters.
The thick chain hanging from its hand lay on the ground next to One’s body. One of the links was only a few centimeters away from the ant’s foot.
The creature’s faceless head turned toward them. The vertical slit of its mouth opened slightly. Inside, nothing but darkness and a few chain strands could be seen.
Seris did not draw her sword. Lian kept the Mana flow completely stable.
One was trembling with fear, but it kept the trembling so small that the Warden did not detect it.
A few seconds later, the guardian moved. The sound of the blade and chain being dragged echoed on the path again.
One lowered its foot and moved forward. They repeated this cycle several times.
Move.
Stop.
Silence.
Wait.

Each time, the Warden covered a different distance. Sometimes it would deliberately speed up. Sometimes it would lift the blade off the ground for a moment, and the sound would stop without the creature itself stopping.
Then suddenly, it would lower the blade.
It was clearly trying to trick creatures that had understood its rule.
Lian activated Echo Adaptation.
[Echo Adaptation Activated.]
[Primary Target Selected: Chainbound Ossuary Warden.]
[Target combat rhythm is being analyzed.]
His eyes focused on the Warden’s body.

Lian did not only listen to the chain. He examined the movement of the shoulders, the angle of the feet, the hand’s pressure on the blade, the change in Mana in the ribcage, and the beats of the different chain links.
[Analysis: 17%]
In the next stop, he noticed that just before the sound stopped, the Warden’s left shoulder would lower a few centimeters.
But this sign was not always present.
He checked the next movement.
[Analysis: 34%]
This time, the third chain link hit the back of the blade slightly before the stop.
A short sound.
Click.
Then the dragging of the metal stopped. Lian gave the stop command before the silence.
One stopped at that same moment.
Seris gave him a brief look. She had realized that Lian was no longer only reacting to the chain sound and seemed to be finding the pattern.
[Analysis: 51%]
The third sign was the change in Mana speed.
Half a second before the stop, the energy flow in the Warden’s legs would decrease and gather in its ribcage.
Lian could now predict the stop a little earlier.
But the analysis was not complete.
The Warden deliberately changed the pattern several times. Once, its left shoulder lowered, but it continued moving.
Another time, the third link hit the blade, but the stop occurred three steps later.
The skill analyzed, but it could not fully predict the behavior of a creature with changing patterns.
[Analysis: 63%]
The number stopped there.
For more understanding, Lian would have to observe it for a longer time, but sixty-three percent was enough.
They crossed a large part of the Rib Passage without mistake.
After a while, the path changed before them. The massive ribs had collapsed and blocked the main route.
The gap between the bones was enough for Lian and Seris to pass, but One could not get through.
Leaving it behind was also not possible.
Lian checked the map. The alternative path was on the right. A long and almost flat strip of ground with no crushed bones on it.
The same clean paths he had observed from above the valley.
Back then, he had guessed that something massive regularly passed through them and pushed the bones aside.
Now the reason was in front of him. This path was the Warden’s patrol route.
To reach the Hollow Spine, they had to travel a few hundred meters on that same path.
But that thing was between them and the exit. If they only moved with the stop-and-go rule, crossing would take a long time.
Each stop increased the chance of error, and the Warden was also getting closer to them.
Lian checked the path, the distance, and the mist. Then he decided to use his new skill.
"Do whatever you can to minimize your presence."
Both nodded. They didn’t know what he was going to do, but they completely trusted him.
Then Lian activated False Presence.
[False Presence]
At a distance of about fifty meters to the left, between two broken ribs, a weak fluctuation formed in the mist.
The smell of a human, the sound of breathing, a trace of Mana, and footsteps moving on the bone powder.
The false presence had no physical body, but to the senses of ordinary creatures, it seemed completely real.
Lian’s own voice was heard from within the mist.
"I’m here."
The Warden’s head immediately turned in that direction, but it did not attack. The chain was still moving.
The guardian had sensed the presence, but it did not break its own rule.
Lian waited. Echo Adaptation detected the change in Mana in the Warden’s ribcage.
The stop was near. He moved the false presence. The sound of footsteps continued at the exact moment the chain stopped.
The Warden disappeared.
The massive blade came down with terrifying force at the false presence’s location.
The False Presence collapsed at that same moment, but the strike shattered several giant ribs.
Bone fragments fell on the path.
The Warden was distracted from the main path for a few seconds.
"Now." Lian shouted quietly!
This was their only chance to escape this hellish situation!

Another time, the third link hit the blade, but the stop occurred three steps later.
The skill analyzed, but it could not fully predict the behavior of a creature with changing patterns.
[Analysis: 63%]
The number stopped there.
For more understanding, Lian would have to observe it for a longer time, but sixty-three percent was enough.
They crossed a large part of the Rib Passage without mistake.
After a while, the path changed before them.
The massive ribs had collapsed and blocked the main route.
The gap between the bones was enough for Lian and Seris to pass, but One could not get through.
Leaving it behind was also not possible.
Lian checked the map.
The alternative path was on the right.
A long and almost flat strip of ground with no crushed bones on it.
The same clean paths he had observed from above the valley.
Back then, he had guessed that something massive regularly passed through them and pushed the bones aside.
Now the reason was in front of him.
This path was the Warden’s patrol route.
To reach the Hollow Spine, they had to travel a few hundred meters on that same path.
But that thing was between them and the exit.
If they only moved with the stop-and-go rule, crossing would take a long time.
Each stop increased the chance of error, and the Warden was also getting closer to them.
Lian checked the path, the distance, and the mist.
Then he decided to use his new skill.
"Do whatever you can to minimize your presence."
Both nodded.
They didn’t know what he was going to do, but they completely trusted him.
Then Lian activated False Presence.
[False Presence]
At a distance of about fifty meters to the left, between two broken ribs, a weak fluctuation formed in the mist.
The smell of a human, the sound of breathing, a trace of Mana, and footsteps moving on the bone powder.
The false presence had no physical body, but to the senses of ordinary creatures, it seemed completely real.
Lian’s own voice was heard from within the mist.
"I’m here."
The Warden’s head immediately turned in that direction, but it did not attack.
The chain was still moving.
The guardian had sensed the presence, but it did not break its own rule.
Lian waited.
Echo Adaptation detected the change in Mana in the Warden’s ribcage.
The stop was near.
He moved the false presence.
The sound of footsteps continued at the exact moment the chain stopped.
The Warden disappeared.
The massive blade came down with terrifying force at the false presence’s location.
The False Presence collapsed at that same moment, but the strike shattered several giant ribs.
Bone fragments fell on the path.
The Warden was distracted from the main path for a few seconds.
"Now." Lian shouted quietly!
This was their only chance to escape this hellish situation!

chapters.title: Chapter 248: Running!
paragraphs: One’s six legs pushed the bone powder aside at the same time, its massive body accelerating on the flat path.
Seris bent down on its back to maintain her balance. Lian looked back.
The Warden pulled the blade out of the ground.
Its head turned toward the empty location of the false presence. It remained motionless for a moment, and then a deep vibration came from its ribcage.
It was not a roar, nor was it a sound, but all the surrounding bones trembled.
The chains around its body shook violently.
The creature turned back. It no longer waited for the sound to stop. It dragged the blade on the ground and ran after them with unnatural speed.
Lian immediately understood that the previous rule no longer provided complete safety.
In Pursuit mode, the Warden had identified them as targets.
"Damn it, the bastard is after us!" He cursed.
"Faster! Run faster!"
A thick chain was thrown from the mist. Its links twisted in the air like a massive snake.
The chain wrapped around One’s back leg. The ant lost its balance, and its body was pulled to one side.
Lian activated Glacial Reaper Claw.
[Glacial Reaper Claw — Divine]
The ice claw formed on his hand. He leaned over One’s back and placed the claw on the chain.
The cold spread along the links. The black metal was covered with a layer of blue ice.
Its movement slowed. Its structure became more brittle under the intense cold.
"Help!" He looked at the silver-haired girl and said urgently.
Seris jumped off One.
She spun in the air, and King’s Breaker was activated on her sword.
Mana gathered on one point of the chain. The strike landed, and the chain’s defensive power decreased at the moment of contact.
The blade passed through the frozen section, and the chain broke with a loud crash!
One freed its leg and accelerated again. Seris landed on its back. The Warden released the broken part of the chain.
It raised its massive blade, and this time, it threw the weapon.
The blade spun in the air. Its wide edge was coming directly toward One’s body.
Lian kept his eyes open and saw the impact path. He did not have enough time to completely stop the weapon.
But he could change its angle. He looked around, and upon seeing that the place was full of bones, his eyes sparkled.
[Ossuary Armor]
The bone fragments trembled in the air, moving toward Lian’s forearm and shoulder. Multi-layered plates locked together and formed a thick shield.
He placed himself in the blade’s path. The impact was like an explosion.
Ossuary Armor cracked at that same moment. The first plate shattered, the second broke, and the third only resisted for a fraction of a second.
But that short time was enough.
Lian deflected the strike upward with all his power. The massive blade passed over One’s body.
It hit one of the ribs beside the path and split it in half.
The bone armor on Lian’s hand completely collapsed. Its pieces fell on the ground, and his forearm had gone numb from the impact pressure.
But the bones in his body remained intact.
Ossuary Armor could not directly stop an attack from a creature at that level, at least not for now.
However, as a disposable defense, it had been able to deflect a deadly attack’s path.
That was enough.
The entrance to the Hollow Spine appeared before them. A massive spinal column was located in the valley’s wall. The vertebrae extended like stone and bone rings one after another.
Its interior space resembled a massive tunnel.
The entrance was wide enough for One, but the Warden could also fit part of its body inside.
However, if they entered, maybe they would be safe!
"At full speed! Go inside the tunnel!"
One entered the tunnel.
Lian looked back. The guardian was only a few dozen meters away. The thrown blade had returned to its hand through another chain being pulled.
The Warden raised it.
Seris stood on One’s back and pointed her sword at the entrance’s ceiling.
King’s Edge was activated.
The first strike cut the connections between the upper vertebrae.
Then Silver Requiem. Dozens of silver lines appeared in an instant, splitting the damaged sections of the ceiling.
A few massive vertebrae separated from their places and fell behind One.
The entrance to the tunnel was blocked under a pile of bone. A few seconds later, the Warden’s blade hit the barrier from outside.
The entire Hollow Spine trembled, and cracks formed on the walls...
But the barrier did not collapse, not with the first strike.
One moved through the tunnel without slowing down. The inside of the Hollow Spine was dark and cold.
Thin veins of blue crystals had grown in the bones, creating a faint light.
Holes were on both sides of the vertebrae. Indistinct murmurs could be heard from inside them.
Sometimes small shadows moved behind the cracks. A few eyes opened in the darkness. Thin and crawling creatures watched them from inside the bones.
But none attacked. The pressure of Lian and Seris’s power, One’s massive body, and the Warden’s angry strikes from behind kept them in their shelters.
The second strike hit the entrance.
The tunnel trembled again. A part of the bone powder fell from the ceiling.
Lian opened the map. The Hollow Spine did not have a direct path, but its side branches were few, and most of them seemed to be dead ends.
The Crystal Wound was at the eastern end.
The distance was not far. They just had to keep moving without stopping.
A few minutes later, gray mist entered the tunnel from behind. At first, a thin strand, then a thicker mass.
Lian looked back.
The Warden had not completely destroyed the entrance. Perhaps it had entered through another path, or its chains had found a way between the vertebrae.
"How long is this bastard going to follow us? Just leave us alone, damn it!"
He sent the command to increase speed through Hive Link.
One ran faster.
The sound of its feet echoed in the hollow spinal column.
Blue light appeared at the end of the path. At first a small point, then wider, and purple color was also added to it, and colder air was blowing from the front.
But unlike the dead cold of the graveyard, this air smelled of life.
Moist soil, plants, and natural Mana. They had reached the end of the Hollow Spine.
The Crystal Wound was in front of them.
A massive crack in the Giants’ Graveyard’s wall. Tall and transparent crystals had grown on both sides of the crack. Some blue, some purple, and some almost colorless.
The gray mist changed as they approached that area.
Its color became lighter, gray turned to silver, and then veins of blue formed in it.
Beyond the crack, transparent trees could be seen.
Glassthorn Forest.
But between them and the exit, there was a bridge made of broken bones. Beneath the bridge was a deep gap, its bottom disappearing in the mist.
One stepped onto the bridge and took the first step.
At that same moment, a chain from behind hit one of the bridge’s supporting ribs.
The links wrapped around the bone. A strong pull was applied, and the bridge trembled.
A few pieces of bone fell from under One’s feet. The Warden had reached the end of the Hollow Spine through another path.
Part of its tall body could be seen among the vertebrae. Its faceless head was pointed at them.
It pulled the chain with all its strength. The supporting rib cracked, and the bridge began to collapse!
"At this rate, our path will be blocked!" Seris frowned and struck the ant’s rump firmly to force it to run even faster!
Poor One ran with all its might.
Every step crushed pieces of the path.
But stopping meant falling.
Seris stood on One’s back at the rear. Another chain came through the air, and her sword moved.
King’s Edge deflected the chain’s edge.
The links hit the bridge’s side and broke part of it.
Lian moved forward with Thunder Step. Blue lightning ran on the bones. He appeared a few meters ahead of One. A pile of collapsed bones had blocked the path.
He activated Iron Fortress Charge.
His shoulder hit the barrier with force. The bones exploded in front of him.
And the path opened!

chapters.title: Chapter 249: The Graveyard of Giants ( Final )
paragraphs: One passed through the white dust without slowing down. Behind them, the bridge was collapsing piece by piece.
The Warden pulled part of its body out from between the vertebrae and raised its massive blade.
The pressure of its Mana weighed on the space.
If the strike landed, it would not only destroy One but also the remaining part of the bridge!
Seris gripped her sword’s hilt tighter. Mana gathered around her.
But Lian did not look at the Warden. His gaze was on the chain on the creature’s left side.
Echo Adaptation was still active. It had analyzed the monster’s movements since the first observation.
Now he understood something. When the Warden delivered heavy strikes, it would shift its weight to a specific chain.
The chain on the left was not only a weapon or restraint. Its tall and irregular body’s balance depended on it.
"The left chain!." Lian said.
Seris only looked once and understood.
Lian activated Thunder Step. In an explosion of lightning, he landed on the chain. Glacial Reaper Claw formed again.
He slammed the ice claw onto the thick link. The cold spread along it.
The black metal froze, and blue cracks formed on its surface.
The Warden lowered its blade, but at that same moment, Seris moved.
[King’s Breaker]
Her sword hit the frozen point. The chain’s defensive power collapsed, and the massive link broke... the chain was severed in half!
All of the Warden’s weight suddenly fell to one side. Its tall body lost its balance, and the blade hit the wall instead of the bridge.
The creature fell among a pile of bones. Several massive ribs shattered under its weight.
Mist and bone dust rose in the air.
It was not killed... it did not even seem severely wounded, but it needed time to get out from among the bones.
Those few minutes were enough.
"This is our only and last chance! Cross this damn thing right now!"
One crossed the last part of the bridge. The bones collapsed behind its feet.
Its body passed through the Crystal Wound. The moment they crossed the border, the pressure of the Giants’ Graveyard disappeared.
Not gradually, but suddenly, as if an invisible wall had been between the two areas.
The sound of the wind returned, the leaves moved, a bell-like sound echoed among the trees, and the cold and living air hit their faces.
One ran a few more meters and then slowed down. Lian felt through Hive Link that the ant’s deep fear had lessened.
Anxiety was still there, but that instinctive pressure that came from the entire graveyard remained behind them.
Seris turned back. The gray mist of the Giants’ Graveyard stopped at the Crystal Wound’s border.
Its strands came to the edge of the crack like long fingers, but did not enter the forest.
In the distance, the Warden moved among the bones again. It placed its hand on the ground, and its tall body slowly rose, but it did not chase them.
Perhaps it could not leave its territory. Perhaps the black chains were not only weapons but also bindings that kept it in the Graveyard.
The area panel appeared before Lian’s view.
[You have left Giant’s Graveyard.]
[You have entered Glassthorn Forest.]
Lian looked at the words for a few seconds. They had not conquered the Giants’ Graveyard.
They had not killed the sitting giant, nor had they discovered all the graveyard’s secrets, but they had survived it.
They had passed the Grave Mimics, Bone Scavengers, the occupying core, the Doppelgängers, and the Warden.
Not by recklessly using their most powerful Skills, but through observation, analysis, and coordination. And that too was a kind of victory.
Lian got down from One. His feet landed on the cold, dark soil of Glassthorn Forest.
He took a deep breath. The forest air was sharp and cold... but it did not smell of death.
It smelled of wet crystals, tree bark, and unknown plants.
The trees of Glassthorn had unusual heights. Their bark was transparent, and blue and purple lights moved inside the trunks, as if Mana flowed through them instead of sap.
The branches had come out of the trunks like cut glass. The leaves were narrow, semi-transparent, and hard.
With every gust of wind, they hit each other and created a delicate sound like small bells.
Light broke several times among the trees. Shadows were cast in unnatural directions. In the distance, large shapes moved behind the transparent trunks.
But due to the light refraction, it was impossible to determine their real distance and size.
Seris also got down from One. She examined the forest for a few moments.
"Better than the graveyard."
"Still not clear." Lian looked at a shadow that moved behind three trees, and fell on the ground, leaning against his ant.
"What was that?" Seris looked back again.
Ever since they entered that graveyard, they had faced strange and bizarre creatures one after another, each stranger than the last.
"I have no idea. I don’t even know exactly what it was built for... but most likely, it was a type of guardian."
"A guardian?" The young Pendragon frowned, but a moment later, a spark seemed to ignite in her mind.
"You mean... to prevent that giant from waking up?"
"Correct." Lian nodded in confirmation.
"According to the Varkesh warning, that Warden only patrols a specific area and reacts to bloodshed. Whenever blood is spilled in that area, it immediately intervenes and eliminates its cause."
He paused for a moment and then continued.
"If you noticed, after we killed the occupying core and the Doppelgängers, the sitting giant’s awakening percentage directly reached five percent."
He fixed his gaze into the distance.
"If my guess is correct... that giant has never died. It is trapped between life and death, and by absorbing the bloodshed within this graveyard, it gathers the necessary energy to awaken."
The more he thought about it, the more logical this hypothesis seemed to him.
That was why monster corpses should not be destroyed. The giant needed blood or perhaps a type of residual energy left in the victims’ bodies to continue its awakening process.
And precisely for that reason...
That Warden would reduce to ashes any creature that caused bloodshed.
Not just kill...
But leave no trace of its body behind; no flesh, no bone, not even a single cell.
As if it wanted to ensure nothing remained to feed that giant.
Probably that was also why the occupying core had kept the six Varkesh bodies intact.
It knew that if their blood was spilled on the ground, the Warden would immediately appear and destroy everything.
But as long as the conflict did not end in bloodshed...
That guardian would not interfere either.
Lian said with more confidence.

"The Warden’s duty is this; it patrols around the most sensitive part of the giant’s burial site and does not allow bloodshed in that area. If anyone violates this rule, it reduces them to ashes without exception."
Seris frowned slightly.
"But we fought several times inside the graveyard and there was no sign of it. Does that mean the area it protects is that small?"
"Probably." Lian thought for a moment and answered.

"In the first battles, the giant’s awakening percentage only increased by one percent. But when we reached that skull and killed the occupying core and the Doppelgängers, another three percent was added."
His eyes narrowed.

"I suspect that same area is the most sensitive point of this graveyard; where every drop of blood has the greatest effect on the giant’s awakening. That is why the Warden protects exactly that same area."
"That sounds logical..."
Seris nodded slowly, but another question would not leave her mind.
"But who placed that Warden there? Who was willing to build such a guardian to stop that giant’s awakening at any cost?"
A heavy silence fell among them.
"And more importantly..." Her gaze was fixed on the graveyard’s dark depths.
"What exactly is that giant... that they went this far to keep it asleep? So much so that they turned this entire graveyard into its prison?"
Lian remained silent. He had no answers to give to these questions. He too was curious about what exactly had happened in this graveyard.
But they had no information, not even a little, to reason with...
Although neither Lian nor Seris... at that time, knew that the secret of the Giants’ Graveyard was the reason this world still existed...
A world that, of course... was approaching its end.

I don’t even know exactly what it was built for... but most likely, it was a type of guardian."
"A guardian?" The young Pendragon frowned, but a moment later, a spark seemed to ignite in her mind.
"You mean... to prevent that giant from waking up?"
"Correct." Lian nodded in confirmation.
"According to the Varkesh warning, that Warden only patrols a specific area and reacts to bloodshed.
Whenever blood is spilled in that area, it immediately intervenes and eliminates its cause."
He paused for a moment and then continued.
"If you noticed, after we killed the occupying core and the Doppelgängers, the sitting giant’s awakening percentage directly reached five percent."
He fixed his gaze into the distance.
"If my guess is correct... that giant has never died.
It is trapped between life and death, and by absorbing the bloodshed within this graveyard, it gathers the necessary energy to awaken."
The more he thought about it, the more logical this hypothesis seemed to him.
That was why monster corpses should not be destroyed.
The giant needed blood or perhaps a type of residual energy left in the victims’ bodies to continue its awakening process.
And precisely for that reason...
That Warden would reduce to ashes any creature that caused bloodshed.
Not just kill...
But leave no trace of its body behind; no flesh, no bone, not even a single cell.
As if it wanted to ensure nothing remained to feed that giant.
Probably that was also why the occupying core had kept the six Varkesh bodies intact.
It knew that if their blood was spilled on the ground, the Warden would immediately appear and destroy everything.
But as long as the conflict did not end in bloodshed...
That guardian would not interfere either.
Lian said with more confidence.
"The Warden’s duty is this; it patrols around the most sensitive part of the giant’s burial site and does not allow bloodshed in that area.
If anyone violates this rule, it reduces them to ashes without exception."
Seris frowned slightly.
"But we fought several times inside the graveyard and there was no sign of it.
Does that mean the area it protects is that small?"
"Probably." Lian thought for a moment and answered.
"In the first battles, the giant’s awakening percentage only increased by one percent.
But when we reached that skull and killed the occupying core and the Doppelgängers, another three percent was added."
His eyes narrowed.
"I suspect that same area is the most sensitive point of this graveyard; where every drop of blood has the greatest effect on the giant’s awakening.
That is why the Warden protects exactly that same area."
"That sounds logical..."
Seris nodded slowly, but another question would not leave her mind.
"But who placed that Warden there?
Who was willing to build such a guardian to stop that giant’s awakening at any cost?"
A heavy silence fell among them.
"And more importantly..." Her gaze was fixed on the graveyard’s dark depths.
"What exactly is that giant... that they went this far to keep it asleep?
So much so that they turned this entire graveyard into its prison?"
Lian remained silent.
He had no answers to give to these questions.
He too was curious about what exactly had happened in this graveyard.
But they had no information, not even a little, to reason with...
Although neither Lian nor Seris... at that time, knew that the secret of the Giants’ Graveyard was the reason this world still existed...
A world that, of course... was approaching its end.

chapters.title: Chapter 250: The Forest Of Glassthorn
paragraphs: Seris’s question lingered in the cold air of Glassthorn Forest for a few moments.
Who had built the Warden?
What exactly was the sitting giant?
And why had someone been willing to turn that entire graveyard into a massive prison to prevent it from awakening?
Lian was still looking at the border between the two areas.
Behind them, the gray mist of the Giants’ Graveyard was stopped along the Crystal Wound like a living wall.
Its thin strands reached the edge of the crack, but none entered the forest.
In the depth of the mist, the edge of a few giant ribs could still be seen, but there was no trace of the Warden.
Only the deep marks its blade and chains had left on the bones extended into the distance.
He was silent for a few more moments. He was also thinking about those same questions.
If the sitting giant was truly trapped between life and death, who had put it in that state?
If the Warden was built to prevent its awakening, its creator must have known not only the giant’s power but also the law of absorbing blood and energy.

And more importantly, if the survival of this world really depended on keeping that creature asleep, why did the sitting giant seem so unknown? And why was there no information about it in the tribes’ archives?
But for now, all of these were only hypotheses.
Hypotheses built on a few percent changes in Awakening, the behavior of a guardian, and a few incomplete Varkesh notes.
The more they thought about it, the more questions arose and the fewer answers there were. Finally, Lian took his gaze off the mist.
"For now, it’s better to set this matter aside."
Seris looked at him.

"No matter how much we think about it, we won’t reach a conclusion without more information. We don’t even know what race the giant was, who imprisoned it here, or what creature exactly built the Warden."
His eyes returned to the graveyard’s depths for a moment.
"If there is an answer, we’ll probably find it further ahead."
The young Pendragon was silent for a few seconds, then looked at the gray border one last time.
No movement could be seen in the mist.
The graveyard had returned to its heavy and deadly silence; as if no battle had taken place inside it and no creature had escaped its clutches.
Seris nodded and turned her gaze to the forest ahead.
"Now we’re in the middle of Glassthorn Forest. What should we do?"
Lian did not answer immediately. His gaze moved among the trees.
Glassthorn Forest was different from the Giants’ Graveyard in every way.
The graveyard was a colorless and dead world. But here, everything was shining.
The transparent trunks of the trees rose to unusual heights. Blue and purple lights flowed inside them, like veins of Mana slowly moving through the forest’s heart.
The branches resembled long glass blades.
The leaves were narrow, transparent, and hard, and every time the wind passed through them, they would hit each other and create a sound like hundreds of small bells.
Reflections could be seen on every surface. One tree sometimes carried the image of five other trees on its trunk.
Shadows were cast in directions that did not align with the light’s angle.
Sometimes something moved in the distance, but it was not easy to tell whether it was a real creature or a broken image on several crystalline surfaces.
"It depends." He said after examining the environment.
"On what?"
"On what your goal in coming to this world actually is." His own main reason for coming was to become stronger and find an opportunity to reach and pass his first evolution.
Where they should go from now on and what they should do depended to some extent on their goals. His goal was clear.
But this girl’s goal? He didn’t know, but he could guess... and he was sure his guess was correct.
"Becoming stronger and fighting." Seris answered without needing to think.
Lian looked at her for a few seconds. There was no hesitation on her face, as if she had given the simplest and most logical answer possible.
"I didn’t expect a more complex answer." He then said with a dry tone.
"Then why did you ask?" Seris showed the slightest discomfort.
"To make sure."
"Now you’re sure."
Lian opened his status panel.
[Name: Lian Vorhelm]
[Level: 18]
The EXP bar was almost full. Only a narrow part at the end was empty. He was not far from Level 19.
But his real goal was not Level 19. His eyes focused on the number twenty.
"My current goal is to reach my first evolution."
In the normal system, the first evolution occurred at Level 20.
For normal classes, evolution mostly meant increasing stats capacity, enhancement, opening a new stage of traits, and upgrading the class structure.
But Monster Class was not a normal class. Lian still did not know what change his first evolution would bring.
Maybe his innate traits would be strengthened, maybe a new innate Skill would open.
Maybe the dormant Monster Talent would enter the next stage.
Or maybe the structure of his body, blood, and everything else would change in a way that he could no longer hide.
Whatever it was, he was sure reaching Level 20 would probably be the biggest power jump since Monster Class was activated.
But a question also occupied his mind. Would he have to do a Quest for evolution like everyone else? Or would it be different for him?
Typically, awakened ones receive an evolution Quest upon reaching Level 20. The stronger the class, the more dangerous and deadly the Quest will be.
"I guess my goal is the same." Seris said.
Lian closed the panel and looked at her.
"What level are you?
"Just seventeen."
Lian was surprised for a moment. She had just entered Level 17. The last time he knew Seris’s level, she was Level 15.
At that same time, Lian was still around Level 12 or 13.
But now the situation had changed. He was on the verge of Level 19, and this girl had just reached Level 17.
He quickly understood the reason. During this time, Seris had mostly trained.
Training with the sword, strengthening Skills, increasing Mana control, and preparing for the Special Area, which is why she had not come to the Ruined Realm.
But Lian had entered the Ruined Realm after his sister’s birthday ceremony and had gone through many experiences and conflicts.
Along with these, Bloodlust absorbed one hundred percent of the Experience from killing creatures.
Even genius awakened ones at most absorb up to 50 percent of a monster’s EXP.
But for Lian, no EXP was wasted.
The difference between training and real battle, combined with Bloodlust, had closed the old gap between them, and he had pulled ahead.
"So our only path is clear. We have to hunt monsters and raise our Level."
Seris nodded with satisfaction. For her, this plan was probably the best news she could hear.
"But there is a problem."
"What?"
"The monsters in this forest are probably weaker than the creatures in the Forest of Giants."
His gaze moved among the glass trees.
"According to the map, Glassthorn Forest is dangerous, but not as much as the Forest of Giants or the Graveyard. That means we need more kills for Leveling Up."
Seris thought for a few moments.
"Maybe we should have stayed longer in the Forest of Giants." She then said completely seriously.
Lian only gave her a brief look and then took out the map.
With a look, he was able to determine their current position on the western edge of Glassthorn Forest.
Behind them was the Giants’ Graveyard. To the east, the border of the next area could be seen, which was the Emberroot Forest.
Unlike Glassthorn, that forest was not only home to monsters. Among the notes he had read in the tribe, there were a few brief mentions.
Cities built among massive trunks, trade routes, settlements of several species, and a civilization that apparently was considered the largest remaining community in this world.
A living civilization meant information.
The history of this world, different areas, survivors, and perhaps a way to find the other group members, and maybe they could even find information about the graveyard and the sitting giant there.
Just before the connecting path between Glassthorn Forest and Emberroot, a mark was on the map.
There was no writing next to it, no warning or explanation, but it was marked.
The map has several markings in general, but most of them are in Emberroot, and in Glassthorn and the Forest of Giants, there is nothing special.
Except for this specific point that is located on the border between these two forests and is marked.
Unfortunately, there was no specific explanation for why these markings were there, but Lian felt that there was definitely something special and important about them.
"Until we reach this point, we hunt." He then placed his finger on the marked point.
